title: Mahler's Problem on Liouville Numbers II. Rational Maps
abstract: In 1984, Mahler asked which analytic functions map the set $\mathscr L$ of Liouville numbers into itself. In the first paper of this series, we proved that every real-analytic solution on an open interval is the restriction of a real rational function. We now identify a canonical subfield $\mathbb L$ of $\mathbb R$ such that, for every nonconstant $R\in\mathbb R(X)$ and every nonempty open interval $I$ in its domain, $R(I\cap\mathscr L)\subseteq\mathscr L$ if and only if $R$ is defined over $\mathbb L$ and $R^{-1}(\mathbb Q)\cap I\cap\mathscr L=\varnothing$. The weaker inclusion $R(I\cap\mathscr L)\subseteq\mathbb Q\cup\mathscr L$ holds if and only if $R$ is defined over $\mathbb L$. If $R$ is not defined over $\mathbb L$, every such interval contains a Cantor set of Liouville numbers whose images under $R$ are irrational and have irrationality exponents bounded by a constant depending only on $R$. We also construct continuum many positive strong Liouville numbers $σ$ for which $σX^m$ preserves $\mathscr L$ for every $m\geq2$, with all nonzero rational fibers consisting of $U_m$-numbers.

title: Metallic Circles: Concyclic Tangency Points of Ford Circles over $k$-Fibonacci Quotients
abstract: Extending a result of Kocik, we show that the tangency points of the Ford circles built over quotients of $k$-Fibonacci numbers are concyclic: they lie on a circle centred on the horizontal axis, of radius $\sqrt{k^2+4}/2$, meeting it at the reciprocal of the metallic ratio $σ_k$ and at $-σ_k$. Concyclicity turns out to be a quadratic identity of the sequence read in coordinates. In the Poincaré half-plane, this circle is a geodesic along which the tangency points advance with constant step $2\lnσ_k$.

title: How to Look Inside the Black Box: A Survey of Yu. E. Nesterov's Contributions (On the Award of the 2026 Gauss Prize)
abstract: On July 23, 2026, at the opening of the International Congress of Mathematicians in Philadelphia, the International Mathematical Union announced the award of the Gauss Prize to Yurii Evgenievich Nesterov -- an award for mathematical work with significant applications outside mathematics. This article explains the mathematical content of the recognized work of Yu. E. Nesterov and traces its influence on modern computational practice. The exposition is based on a concept that Yu. E. Nesterov himself regards as one of his main results: the classical complexity theory of convex optimization is oriented toward a black-box oracle, but its pessimistic bounds can be overcome by using a priori information about the internal structure of the objective function. We trace Yu. E. Nesterov's scientific career, then introduce the language of oracle complexity together with a classification of objective function models (geometric, algebraic, and structural), and subsequently discuss his main results in chronological order: the fast gradient method, fast automatic differentiation, the theory of self-concordant barriers and polynomial-time interior-point methods, the $π/2$ theorem, the stable dynamics model of traffic flows, the smoothing technique, primal-dual methods, cubic regularization of Newton's method, the modified Gauss--Newton scheme, coordinate descent methods and methods for huge-scale problems, gradient-free methods, universal gradient methods, implementable tensor methods, and "superfast" methods. Each topic is accompanied by historical background, precise statements specifying the problem class, oracle, and type of guarantee, examples, and a discussion of the current state of the art.

title: Logically Augmented Quantum LDPC Codes: Construction and Hierarchical Decoding
abstract:
We propose a joint framework for constructing and decoding Logically Augmented (LA) quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes. This is motivated by the need for flexible coding rates and adaptive error protection while preserving block length and code structure. On the construction side, we use an auxiliary \textit{Logical Protection Code (LPC)} to impose additional stabilizer constraints on selected logical qubits of a \textit{primary} code. On the decoding side, the proposed decoder uses the LPC syndrome to generate logical error hypotheses and condition belief propagation (BP) on each hypothesis. The proposed \textit{Hierarchical Logical List Decoder (HLLD)} is invoked only when the initial BP decoder for primary code fails to converge. It then selects the correction with the smallest Hamming weight among the syndrome-consistent candidates produced by hypothesis-conditioned BP runs.
  For numerical evaluation, we focus on short repetition LPCs, which provide a flexible means of trading rate for additional error protection. Each LPC syndrome admits exactly two logical error hypotheses, irrespective of repetition length, which enables HLLD to explore both possibilities without relying on a single logical estimate. Numerical results show that varying the repetition length provides a tunable trade-off between rate and error-correction performance across a wide range of primary code constructions and their operating regimes. On the decoding side, with the overall LA code held fixed, HLLD reduces the logical error rate by up to 81\%, 75\%, and 69\% for LA codes based on mitten, lifted-product, and bivariate bicycle codes, respectively, compared with conventional BP decoding of the same LA codes.

title: Explicit bounds for the number of solutions to Roth-type inequalities over adelic curves
abstract: In this paper, we provide an upper bound on the number of a special system of Roth-type Diophantine inequalities over proper adelic curves. By refining the technique from previous work, we successfully eliminate the large-height restriction on the solutions. Furthermore, the constraints on the parameters within the inequality are further relaxed. We also give a constructive quantitative generalization of the Vojta-Dolce-Zucconi system, replacing compactness-based extraction by a discrete pigeonhole argument and a finite grid partition, so that the resulting bound has explicit dependence on the relevant parameters.

title: Classification of real Lie algebras of dimension five
abstract: We summarize a coordinate-free classification of five-dimensional real Lie algebras up to isomorphism. Rather than solving the overdetermined quadratic Jacobi system modulo $\mathrm{GL}(5,\mathbb{R})$, the method uses Levi--Malcev theory and nilradical stratification. In the non-solvable case, the Levi factor is three-dimensional, $\mathfrak{so}(3)$ or $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{R})$, acting on a two-dimensional radical; this yields exactly five classes, including the indecomposable $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{R})\ltimes\mathbb{R}^2$. In the solvable case, Schur's bound on commutative subalgebras of $\mathfrak{gl}(2,\mathbb{R})$ implies $\dim\mathfrak{n}\in\{3,4,5\}$, eliminating one- and two-dimensional nilradicals. The nilpotent case $\dim\mathfrak{n}=5$ has nine classes: three decomposable and six indecomposable, including $\mathfrak{h}_5$ and two filiform algebras. For $\dim\mathfrak{n}=4$, classification reduces to normal forms of outer derivations for $\mathbb{R}^4$, $\mathfrak{h}_3\oplus\mathbb{R}$, and $\mathfrak{n}_4$ under automorphism and scaling. For $\dim\mathfrak{n}=3$, it uses two-dimensional abelian subalgebras of $\mathrm{OutDer}(\mathfrak{n})$ containing no nonzero nilpotent operators. The work also computes minimal faithful representation dimensions $μ(\mathfrak{g})$, gives a dictionary with classical tables, and designs a deterministic identification algorithm.

title: Hypergraphs with zero uniform Turán density at intermediate levels
abstract: An $r$-uniform hypergraph $H$ is uniformly dense with respect to $j$-graphs if, up to a small error, at least a prescribed proportion of the $r$-cliques of every $j$-uniform hypergraph on the same vertex set are edges of $H$. For a forbidden hypergraph $F$, its uniform Turán density at level $j$ is the supremum of these density bounds over arbitrarily large $F$-free hypergraphs with the error tending to zero. For every $r\ge4$ and $1\le j\le r-3$, this paper proves that this Turán density is zero precisely when $F$ admits a vertex ordering in which every $(j+1)$-set shared by two edges occupies the same positions in both edges. This generalizes the zero-density characterizations of Erdős at $j=0$ and of Reiher, Rödl, and Schacht at $j=r-2$, and establishes the latter authors' proposed extension to the remaining nontrivial levels. Consequently, at level $j$, every positive uniform Turán density of a possibly infinite forbidden family is at least $N^{-N}$, where $N=\binom r{j+1}$. The proof combines hypergraph regularity with adjacent exchanges in spreadable random hypergraphs.

title: Scalar curvature bounds and rigidity of Ricci shrinkers
abstract: We prove that a complete noncompact gradient shrinking Ricci soliton of dimension at least two is a finite quotient of an Einstein cylinder if its scalar curvature is bounded below by the cylindrical value. The corresponding pointwise strict bound implies compactness. We also establish one-endedness criteria using curvature information at critical points of the potential, including degenerate ones, and obtain sharp one-endedness and rigidity results under global Ricci norm bounds.

title: A Partial-Matching Proof of the Neyman--Pearson Lemma
abstract: Testing seeks to distinguish distributions, whereas matching seeks to identify their common mass. I show that this apparent opposition provides a direct proof of the Neyman--Pearson lemma. Maximal partial matching between the alternative distribution and a scaled null distribution separates them into a common component and two mutually singular residuals. An elementary dual problem then turns this separation into a testing rule: complementary slackness forces rejection on the alternative residual and non-rejection on the scaled-null residual, leaving freedom to randomize at the likelihood-ratio threshold. Thus the optimal test emerges from maximal matching rather than being proposed in advance. The matching profile also determines the optimal power envelope.

title: Two-row Schur times Schubert via parallel classes of positroid varieties
abstract: Schubert structure constants are intersection numbers of Schubert varieties. Finding positive combinatorial formulas for these constants remains a major open problem. We resolve this problem when one of the indexing permutations corresponds to a two-row partition. Our approach uses increasing chains, introduced by Sottile for the one-row case, and builds on the skew Schubert functions studied by Bergeron and Sottile. The key step is to connect increasing chains and these functions with the parallel classes of positroid varieties.

title: Finite-Support Approximation in Variable-Coefficient Sobolev Spaces on Nonhomogeneous Flow-Measure Trees
abstract:
Let $T$ be a nonhomogeneous rooted tree equipped with a positive flow measure $m$. For $1<p<\infty$, consider the variable-coefficient Sobolev space on the nonhomogeneous flow-measure tree~$T$ \[ W_a^{1,p}(T,m) =
\left\{ f\in L^p(T,m): \sum_{x\ne ρ}a(x)m(x)\lvert f(x)-f(π(x))\rvert^p<\infty \right\}, \] where $a$ is a positive variable coefficient, $ρ$ denotes the root and $π(x)$ denotes the parent of $x$. Using an averaging method over descendant levels, we prove the density of finitely supported functions in $W_a^{1,p}(T,m)$ for coefficients satisfying a weighted moment condition. As an application, the relationship between solutions on finite domains and global solutions is clarified for $p=2$.

title: Sobolev homeomorphisms and Jordan curves with positive area
abstract: Each homeomorphic parametrization of a Jordan curve via the unit circle $\mathbb{S}\subset \mathbb{S}^2$ extends to a homeomorphism of the entire $\mathbb{S}^2.$ We show that there exists a Jordan curve of positive area whose every parametrization via $\mathbb{S}$ admits a homeomorphic extension that has $p$-Sobolev regularity on $\mathbb{S}^2$ for all exponents $1\le p<2 .$ This is obtained via a new sharp extension result for the case of $p<2.$

title: Compressions of Linear Relations in Krein Spaces
abstract: Given an orthogonal decomposition \(\widetilde{\mathfrak{H}} = \mathfrak{H}[\dotplus]\widehat{\mathfrak{H}}\) of a Krein space, we study compressions \({\mathrm{C}_{\mathfrak H}}(R)\) of linear relations \(R\) in \(\widetilde{\mathfrak{H}}\) to \(\mathfrak{H}\). We formulate a sufficient condition that ensures that compression commutes with taking adjoints, that is, the adjoint identity \({\mathrm{C}_{\mathfrak H}}(R^{\widetilde{*}}) = {\mathrm{C}_{\mathfrak H}}(R)^{*}\) holds. We derive preservation and reflection results for the compression of maximal dissipative, maximal symmetric, and self-adjoint linear relations. For nonnegative linear relations, the adjoint identity also implies that compression commutes with taking the Friedrichs extension. For \(\mathfrak{H}\ne\{0\}\), we characterize finite dimensionality of the exit space \(\widehat{\mathfrak{H}}\) by universal compression properties. Finally, we give a criterion for the adjoint identity to hold in terms of bounded linear functionals on \(R\).

title: Rational Turán exponents of a single $k$-uniform hypergraph
Cubic Optimization over Three Nonnegative Integers Is NP-hard
abstract: We prove that deciding whether an integer cubic polynomial takes a value at most one over three nonnegative integers is NP-hard. Hardness holds even when every feasible objective value is a positive integer, so every constructed instance has a finite, attained minimum. This establishes a sharp dimension boundary for the tractability of cubic integer optimization in fixed dimension. Our reduction from positive 1-in-3 satisfiability encodes Boolean constraints as modular conditions and uses an algebraic norm to construct a cubic objective whose minimum is one exactly for satisfiable formulas. The resulting six-parameter threshold language is NP-complete and admits short exponent certificates.

title: Fields Generated by a Single Point on Elliptic Curves
abstract: We study the finite extensions of a number field generated by a single point on an elliptic curve. We construct geometrically non-isomorphic elliptic curves with complex multiplication that generate the same collection of extensions, giving a negative answer to a question of Mazur and Rubin. For torsion-generated fields, we prove that inclusion of the collections up to finitely many exceptions implies isogeny over the ground field, and in the non-CM case even isomorphism. When all geometric endomorphisms are defined over the ground field, we characterize equality of the torsion-generated collections by the existence, for every prime $p$, of an isogeny over the ground field of degree prime to $p$. This condition also implies equality of the full collections of fields generated by a single point.

title: Values of differentials of plane branches: block decomposition and semiroots
abstract: We study the passage of special gaps from a Zariski semiroot to a plane branch. A decomposition into rectangular blocks allows us to compute the maximal valuations of the coefficients of differentials and describe the image of the transition map. We treat vertical and horizontal decompositions, as well as decompositions with alternations, obtaining criteria for the preservation of special gaps. For towers whose ramification indices after the first are all equal to two, the value semigroup of the branch and the special gaps of the first semiroot determine the special gaps of the branch.

title: On the Topology of the Set of Nonnegative Forms That Are Not Sums of Squares
abstract: We study the topology of the normalized space of real nonnegative forms of degree $2d$ in $n$ variables that are not sums of squares. Whenever it is nonempty, we prove that it is path-connected but not acyclic, and in particular not contractible. We give explicit bounds on the degrees in which its reduced homology can be nonzero. In the two minimal nonempty cases, we show an embedding of an exterior algebra into the cohomology ring, and prove containment of the binary octahedral and binary icosahedral groups, respectively, in its fundamental group.

title: $s$-quasi-transitive weakly distance-regular digraphs
abstract: A digraph is $s$-quasi-transitive if, for every path $(x_0,x_1,\ldots,x_s)$ of length $s$, either $(x_0,x_s)\in AΓ$ or $(x_s,x_0)\in AΓ$ (or both). In this paper, we give a characterization of $s$-quasi-transitive commutative weakly distance-regular digraphs, where $s=4$, or $s\geq 5$ and the cycle polar diameter is at least $s$.

title: Support in the domain of numerical algorithms in the education of future secondary school mathematics teachers
abstract: This article presents web-based applets designed primarily to educate future mathematics teachers in the field of numerical algorithms and, secondarily, to serve high school students themselves. The applets allow users to explore the behaviour of basic numerical algorithms as applied to fundamental mathematical topics taught at high schools. The advantage is that no software is required, and students can intuitively test how a given method works by adjusting specific problem parameters, not only by viewing a list of approximate solutions, but especially through graphical output. Furthermore, they have access to multiple different methods for comparison.

title: On explicit units in a family of cubic fields and the arithmetic of curves arising from powers of these units
abstract: For an integer $b\neq0,1$ let $K_b$ be the cubic field generated by the unique real root of $x^3-3bx-b^3$, let $η_0$ be its fundamental unit, and let $η_b$ be the explicit unit studied in the companion paper (arXiv:2609.37389). Write $η_b=η_0^{n(b)}$. Deciding whether $n(b)$ is divisible by $q$ amounts to finding the integral points of a plane curve $C_q$ of degree $2q$. We prove that for every integer $q\ge1$ the curve $C_q$ is irreducible with $g(C_q)=\binom{q-1}{2}$, the genus of a smooth plane curve of degree $q$ rather than of degree $2q$. The proof is not a genus computation but a structural one: $C_q$ is the inverse image, under the $q$-power map of a two-dimensional torus, of the curve traced by the minimal polynomial of $η_b$ as $b$ varies, and the formula falls out of two applications of Riemann-Hurwitz in the resulting tower. As a consequence the problem splits into exactly three regimes: $q=2$ rational, $q=3$ elliptic, and $q\ge4$ of general type. In particular only finitely many $b$ have $q\mid n(b)$ for each $q\ge4$. A lower bound for linear forms in two logarithms gives $n(b)<6082138$ for every $b$, so $n(b)\in\{1,2\}$ for all but finitely many $b$, though not effectively. We add two computations: $n(b)$ is determined outright for $|b|\le10^{30}$, and the rational points of $C_4$ are determined by quadratic Chabauty, giving $4\mid n(b)\iff b\in\{-75,-3,5,96\}$. We state precisely which parts of the latter rest on certified arithmetic and which do not. Finally, we show that $K_b\cong K_{b'}$ with $b\neq b'$ holds for $\{b,b'\}=\{-1,5\}$, and otherwise only if one of the two parameters, $c$ say, satisfies $|c|>10^{30}$ and $n(c)$ is divisible by a prime $q\ge5$. There are only finitely many such pairs.

title: The $q$-Poincaré sum and separability in a Coxeter group
abstract: Given a finite Coxeter group $W$ and an element $q$ of a commutative ring $\mathbf{k}$, we define the element $\mathbf{L}_{q} :=\sum_{w\in W}q^{\ell\left( w\right) }w$ of its group algebra $\mathbf{k}\left[ W\right] $. We say that an element $w\in W$ is $W$\emph{-length-symmetric} if its coefficient in the commutator $\left[ \mathbf{L}_{a},\mathbf{L}_{b}\right] $ is $0$ for all $\mathbf{k}$ and all $a,b\in\mathbf{k}$. We prove several sufficient criteria for elements to be $W$-length-symmetric. In particular, we show that any separable permutation (i.e., permutation avoiding the patterns $2413$ and $3142$) in the symmetric group $S_{n}$ is $S_{n}$-length-symmetric. More generally, we construct a notion of separable elements of a finite Coxeter group $W$ (which, for finite Weyl groups, agrees with the eponymous notion introduced by Gaetz and Gao), and show that all such elements are $W$-length-symmetric. This is only a sufficient condition; other $W$-length-symmetric elements include (twisted) involutions and elements of dihedral parabolic subgroups.

title: Coupled free energy and a diagonal approach to coupled Kähler-Einstein metrics
abstract:
In this paper, we introduce the coupled free energy $F_{-γ}^{\rm cp}$ which is a natural generalization of the free energy functional defined by Berman. In the Fano case, our coupled free energy provides a diagonal approach to the coercivity of the coupled Ding functional. We also define the non-Archimedean coupled free energy $F_{-γ}^{\rm cp,NA}$ on the space of finite energy measures on the Berkovich analytification. As a consequence of the regularization process of the non-Archimedean entropy established by Boucksom-Jonsson, Chi Li and Trusiani, we prove that the existence of a unique coupled Kähler-Einstein metric is equivalent to the stability condition that there exists $ε>0$ such that $F_{-1-ε}^{\rm cp,NA} \geq 0$ on the space of measures associated with a test configuration for the anticanonical line bundle.
  As a coupled version of the work by Berman, we show that the law of the empirical measure satisfies a large deviation principle whose rate function is the coupled free energy under the assumption that a conjecture by Hultgren is true. We also introduce a coupled version of the microscopic stability thresholds and prove that a uniformly coupled Gibbs stable Fano manifold has a unique coupled Kähler-Einstein metric. This is a generalization of the results by Fujita-Odaka and Berman.

title: Braided Multisections and Akhmedov's Fake Quadrics
abstract: We give handlebody decompositions of the complements of the cyclic multisections in $Σ_g\times S^2$ constructed in~\cite{AB}. The 2-handle framings are induced by the product coordinates. We compute the integral homology of the complements from their handle chain complexes, including the torsion subgroup of $H_2$. For the degree pairs $(3,3)$ and $(2,4)$, we specify surface diffeomorphisms inducing the maps on first homology prescribed in~\cite{AY} and recover the integral first homology groups $(\Z/3)^2\oplus\Z/(3m)$ and $(\Z/2)^2\oplus\Z/(4m)$, respectively, for $m\geq1$. For the symmetric $m=1$ sum, we also give a simultaneous surface diagram of the relative product attachments and identify their product framings with the surface framings. The resulting symplectic sums are aspherical and symplectically minimal, and have the rational cohomology ring of $S^2\times S^2$.

title: Noether's Second Theorem and the Pareto Front Structure in Multi-Criteria Variational Problems
abstract: This paper establishes a rigorous connection between Noether's second theorem and the structure of Pareto fronts in multi-criteria variational problems. We prove that for a family of functionals invariant under a common gauge Lie group, the regular part of the Pareto front is contained in the union of solutions to weighted Euler--Lagrange equations, and that on Pareto-optimal sections, combinations of Noether currents are conserved. Gauge symmetries are shown to impose additional constraints on the Lagrange multipliers via Bianchi-type identities, reducing the dimension of the admissible weight space. Two practical approaches are derived from this result: dimensionality reduction via gauge fixing and scalarization with penalty terms. The theory is validated on three classical problems: the linear-quadratic regulator with two criteria, a model predictive control problem with a minimax criterion, and the double integrator with control constraints. In each case, the Pareto front is shown to satisfy an exact conservation law, and the analytical structure of the front is recovered from the symmetries of the problem. The results demonstrate that gauge functions (null Lagrangians) can restore invariants even when the dynamics break the symmetry, and that control constraints do not destroy the underlying conservation laws but merely restrict the admissible set. The proposed approach yields a Pareto front with minimal deviation from the theoretical curve, outperforming known multi-objective algorithms, and provides a new foundation for the analytical treatment of multi-criteria optimization in nonlinear dynamics and control.

title: Functional Converses for Private Matrix-Product Retrieval under Library-Wide Decoder-Side Correlation
abstract: We consider private retrieval of the matrix product $A^\top B^{(θ)}$ from replicated $P_c$-colluding servers when $B^{(\ell)}=A+N^{(\ell)}$, with the innovations mutually independent and independent of the user-held $A\in\mathbb{F}_q^{m\times m}$. The servers store the full library, correlated with $A$, which changes both the communication problem and the security definition: a secrecy condition including the stored library cannot hold, as the library itself partly reveals $A$. We therefore measure only additional leakage and require index privacy conditioned on $A$; both reduce to classical notions under independence. For $A$ of rank $k<m$ we prove, with no structural hypothesis on the map, $D^*\geq H(A^\top B^{(θ)}\mid A)/C_{\mathrm{PIR}}(N,P_c,L)-o(km)$, where $C_{\mathrm{PIR}}(N,P_c,L)$ is the replicated $P_c$-colluding private-information-retrieval capacity. The proof rests on a colluding converse for servers storing arbitrary refinements of the demanded messages, whose answers need not be measurable functions of the functional-message library, and a privacy-transfer characterization. Publishing a canonical row-space representative makes the bound achievable for arbitrary independent and identically distributed innovations under a public-setup measure. Under a strengthened observational model (exact correctness, common conditional library support, and full-transcript security), concealment forces $D\geq H(G_m N^{(θ)})/C_{\mathrm{PIR}}$, where $G_m$ spans the linear join of all row spaces in the support of the operand distribution; this extends to vanishing error under a simultaneous-decodability assumption. In the full-rank case product recovery reduces to innovation recovery: $D^*=H(N^{(θ)})/C_{\mathrm{PIR}}+o(m^2)$.

title: On the number of edges in quasiplanar graphs
abstract: A $k$-quasiplanar graph is a graph drawn in the plane with no $k$ pairwise crossing edges. Pach, Shahrokhi, and Szegedy conjectured that every such graph on $n$ vertices has $O_k(n)$ edges. ChatGPT produced a proof of this conjecture. Here, we present a simplified, self-contained version of that proof.

title: Selecting the best UAV pursuer for minimum time moving target interception among obstacles
abstract: A team of unmanned aerial vehicles (pursuers) with different positions, headings, speeds, minimum turning radii and launch delays must respond to a target that moves at constant velocity through a region containing static circular obstacles. Only one pursuer is launched, namely the one that can intercept the target first. We present a computationally efficient, obstacle-aware interceptor-selection framework for this setting. The interception problem of each pursuer is posed as a minimum-time optimal control problem and is solved over an explicit family of candidate path types through an arc-parameterised nonlinear programme in which the obstacles are toured tangentially and every part of the path is kept out of every obstacle by exact (not sampled) distance constraints. A closed-form lower bound, obtained by relaxing the curvature and obstacle constraints, is combined with the verified feasible interception times in a bound-and-select algorithm. We prove that the pruning is certified: a pursuer is skipped only if it cannot improve the best verified interception time, so bound-and-select returns the same pursuer and the same time as solving every pursuer, and the method reports a boundary on the optimal team interception time. Numerical experiments with solver diagnostics and repeated random starts, sensitivity studies in the target speed (with the selection crossover located by bisection), the launch delay, the turning radius and the obstacle configuration, a comparison with nearest-pursuer, fastest-pursuer and straight-line-time selection rules on random scenarios, a computational comparison with full enumeration for growing team sizes, and a geographic case study show that the selected pursuer is frequently neither the nearest nor the fastest, and that lower-bound pruning removes a large part of the computational effort without changing the decision.

title: Well-posedness and large deviations for 3D primitive equations with jumps
abstract: We establish the global pathwise well-posedness and a Freidlin--Wentzell large deviation principle for the three-dimensional viscous primitive equations driven by multiplicative Lévy noise represented by a compensated Poisson random measure. Under local Lipschitz and moment growth assumptions on the noise coefficient, we construct local martingale solutions and obtain a unique maximal pathwise solution with càdlàg trajectories in the $H^1$ energy space. Additional sixth-moment growth in $H^1$ and $L^6$ growth bounds on the baroclinic component of the noise yield global pathwise well-posedness. The proof combines the jump Itô formula with baroclinic and anisotropic energy estimates to rule out finite-time blow-up. Under further exponential integrability and structural assumptions on the noise coefficient, we establish a Freidlin--Wentzell large deviation principle in a strong path topology by the weak convergence approach.

title: Higher Noncommutative Motives and Higher K-theory
abstract: We construct higher additive noncommutative motives of stable $(\infty,n)$-categories, extending the additive motives of Blumberg, Gepner, and Tabuada and the secondary theory of Mazel-Gee and Stern. We formulate a notion of exact sequences and establish the universal property of the resulting additive motives. We give two equivalent constructions: a localization of enriched presheaves and a weighted Waldhausen $S$-construction on complete exact flags. We then compute their Hom objects, obtaining ordinary K-theory at the first level and lower additive motives recursively at higher levels. Our results recover the classical and secondary theories, provide coherent multiplicative structures, and yield an endofunctor on the category of Stefanich rings. In short, higher motives are higher K-theory.

title: Non-migration for planar elastic flows
abstract: We consider a closed planar curve evolving by the free or the length-preserving elastic flow. We prove that the scale-invariant bound $L\int k^2\,ds\le 4π^2+8/3$ at the initial time prevents the entire curve from crossing any line between two times. For the free flow, the proof combines a monotonicity estimate for the normalized bending energy with a barrier that compares centroid motion to an expanding energy radius. For the length-preserving flow, a quantitative gradient estimate controls the total centroid displacement.

title: Exact penalties for maximum-edge bicliques in bipartite graphs
abstract: Given a bipartite graph $G$, we denote by $g(G)$ the largest product $|A||B|$ over pairs of vertex sets $A$ and $B$, one on each side, with no edge between them. These pairs are the bicliques of the bipartite complement of $G$; hence, computing $g(G)$ is the maximum-edge biclique problem, which is NP-hard, as shown by Peeters in 2003. Gillis and Glineur characterized it by a continuous quadratic program, in which a large enough penalty on the edges of $G$ makes the global maximizers correspond to the maximum pairs and the local maximizers to the maximal ones. We propose a new threshold for the penalty, which depends only on $g(G)$. For any penalty at or above it, the global maximizers correspond exactly to the maximum pairs, and every local maximizer with positive value corresponds to a maximal pair. This threshold is never larger than theirs and is sharp up to an additive $1/2$. Spectral and semidefinite bounds give computable penalties; in experiments, a simple local ascent succeeds far more often with the semidefinite one than with the earlier thresholds, although on our graphs that bound already reveals $g(G)$. The penalty formulation, whose optimal value is $\sqrt{g(G)}/2$, is also a copositive formulation of $g(G)$. Strengthening a semidefinite bound of Laurent, Polak and Vargas with the completely positive cone gives exactly $\sqrt{g(G)}/2$, while the doubly nonnegative strengthening is already inexact on six vertices. Finally, Pólya's linear programming approximations of the copositive cone become finite at an explicit level and converge to $\sqrt{g(G)}/2$ without ever being exact.

title: Neyman Orthogonalized Specification Tests for Conditional Tail Index Models
abstract: We develop specification tests for parametric conditional tail index models of heavy-tailed distributions. The tests are based on a projected empirical process that removes the first-order effect of estimating the null parameter. Within the conditional Hall class, we identify conditions under which projection also eliminates the leading Pareto approximation bias in the test process, permitting lower thresholds while preserving asymptotically correct size. We establish the validity of the tests via multiplier bootstrap. For log-linear models, bootstrap validity extends to settings in which covariates among observations above a common threshold concentrate and the smallest eigenvalue of the information matrix tends to zero. We further propose a data-driven threshold selection rule based on an estimate of the Pareto approximation bias after projection. The rule allows lower thresholds to retain more observations for testing while limiting size distortions, with potential gains in power. The finite sample performance of the tests is examined through simulations and a real data application.

title: Energy methods and optimal decay for time-fractional equations
abstract:
We study energy methods for the time-fractional equation $\partial_t^α(u-u_0)-(a(t,x)u_x)_x+(F(t,x,u))_x=Q(t,x,u)$ on the real line, where $0<α<1$, the coefficient $a$ is measurable and bounded from above and from below by positive constants, $σ\partial_xF\ge0$, $σQ\le0$, and the data are in $L^1\cap L^\infty$. Using Yosida approximations of the kernel, an iteration on the $L^{2^m}$ norms gives the parabolic decay $\|u(t)\|_{L^\infty}\le C\|u_0\|_{L^1}t^{-α/2}$.
  In $L^2$ it gives the rate $t^{-α/4}$, which, already for the linear equation, improves the rate $t^{-α/5}$ obtained before by the classical energy method. For the convection--diffusion equation $\partial_t^α(u-u_0)-u_{xx}+(|u|^{q-1}u)_x=0$, $q>1$, the parabolic rate is optimal for $q\ge2$, and for $1<q<2$ the convection improves it. An $L^1$ time-regularity estimate of Bénilan--Crandall type gives the pointwise flux bound $|u|^{q-1}u-u_x=O(\|u_0\|_{L^1}t^{-α})$. This bound takes the place of the Oleĭnik estimate and yields the optimal rate $\|u(t)\|_{L^\infty}\lesssim t^{-α/q}$ for $1<q<2$. For nonnegative data, matching lower bounds hold for the $L^p$ norms.

title: An improved bound for the intersection of two longest cycles in $k$-connected graphs
abstract: A conjecture attributed to Smith states that in every $k$-connected graph, every pair of longest cycles intersects in at least $k$ vertices. We prove that every two longest cycles in a $k$-connected graph on $n$ vertices intersect in at least $\min\{k,10k-n-30\}$ vertices. Consequently, Smith's conjecture holds whenever $k\ge \frac{n+30}{9}$. This improves the previous bound of $\frac{n+16}{7}$ for $n>33$ and also implies a bound of $\frac{n+22}{9}$ for paths instead of cycles.

title: An extremal unimodular lattice of rank 37
abstract: We construct an extremal unimodular lattice of rank 37, resolving the last undetermined optimal minimum in ranks at most 48. The construction begins with the Cayley table of $\mathbb{Z}/13\mathbb{Z}$, assigning a vector of norm four to each cell. We prove that the resulting incidence lattice has exactly 26 unimodular completions of minimum four, all isometric. The resulting Cayley lattice $Λ$ has automorphism group $\mathrm{AGL}(1,13)\times C_6$ and is $s$-extremal, with shadow minimum $13/4$ and kissing number $35\,594$. An explicit $4$-frame in $Λ$ yields a Type I self-dual $\mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z}$-code of length 37 and minimum Euclidean weight 16, resolving the corresponding open case in coding theory.

title: Practical Semialgebraic Optimization via Sparse Sample-Based Sum-of-Squares Programming
abstract: As the importance of semialgebraic optimization grows in engineering, so does the need for scalable sum-of-squares (SOS) methods. Their convex relaxations can guide mixed-integer search and often deliver certified global optima outright. Scaling traditional SOS typically requires hand-crafted bases and redundant constraints, whereas sample-based SOS numerically exploits feasible set geometry to reduce bases and build smaller, often tighter relaxations from black-box evaluations. However, discrete variables can require exponentially many samples, and each sampled equation couples all cliques, destroying correlative sparsity. In this work, we avoid enumeration and slack variables by sampling a tractable variety that contains the feasible set, with multipliers only for the omitted constraints. To recover sparsity, we introduce "separator" polynomials that split the sampled equations into local systems coupled only on clique overlaps. This yields a novel, convergent hierarchy of semidefinite programs (SDPs) with block sizes and sample requirements governed by local interactions rather than total problem size. Lastly, we show how to verify sample sufficiency and prune redundant equations numerically before solving. In robust estimation and motion planning, we obtain certifiably small optimality gaps at scales far beyond those reported for traditional sparse SOS. For example, we solve a truncated least-squares 3D registration problem with 1600 candidate correspondences in under 49 seconds using an off-the-shelf SDP solver on a laptop CPU.

title: A physics-based adaptive low-rank method for 6D Vlasov simulations
abstract: The numerical simulation of kinetic plasma models in six-dimensional phase space poses significant computational and memory challenges, particularly when considering modern high-performance computing architectures. In this work, we propose an adaptive dynamical low-rank approach for the efficient solution of the 6D Vlasov--Poisson system. Our strategy is an extension of the projector-splitting dynamical low-rank integrator. The algorithm changes the rank based on physical observables (e.g., the electric field and energy) as opposed to controlling the error in the distribution function. Our approach is memory efficient in the sense that only rank $r$ objects are required to implement the scheme. This makes the algorithm suitable for performing high-dimensional computations on graphic processing units. Comparisons with rank adaptive Basis-Update & Galerkin integrators exhibit both significant memory savings and reduction in run time. We show, by presenting a variety of 6D benchmark experiments implemented in the C++/CUDA low-rank framework Ensign, that our technique allows us to run simulations with a significantly smaller rank, while still preserving the physical fidelity. Thus, the approach substantially reduces memory footprint and computational cost and enables simulations that are prohibitively expensive for full-rank or less memory-efficient low-rank schemes.

title: The square function estimates for cones in arbitrary dimensions and elliptic quadrics
abstract: We demonstrate that the square function estimate for the light cone in $\R^d$, $d\ge3$, at the exponent $p=2(d-1)/(d-2)$, with loss $[\log(2R)]^{5/p}$ can be deduced from local-smoothing and auxiliary-energy statements in the October 25, 2026 OpenAI manuscript. Exact affine sections preserve these logarithmic bounds and give corresponding estimates for spheres, ellipsoids, elliptic paraboloids, and compact patches of two-sheet elliptic hyperboloids in $\R^{d-1}$.

title: Resolving Tusnády's Problem
abstract: We prove a lower bound of $Ω_d((\log N)^{d-1/2})$ for the worst-case combinatorial discrepancy of $N$-point sets with respect to anchored boxes in every fixed dimension $d\ge3$. Together with Nikolov's upper bound of the same order and Wei's planar lower bound, this settles Tusnády's problem: the discrepancy of axis-parallel boxes is $Θ_d((\log N)^{d-1/2})$ in every fixed dimension $d\ge2$. The proof combines smoothed product test functions, sampling discretization, and an entropy argument for conditioned Gaussian vectors.

title: Efficient counting of 2 x 4 LEGO brick buildings
abstract:
We outline the algorithmic advances behind our recent computation of the number
  8364925094730088313
  of ways to combine eleven 2 x 4 LEGO bricks.

title: Regularity Theory for the Equation $\det(D^2u) = f(u)$ in Two Dimensions
abstract: We study the interior regularity of convex solutions to $$\det D^2u = f(u)$$ in planar domains, with no regularity or monotonicity assumptions on $f$. In particular, when $f$ is bounded between positive constants, we show that $u$ is locally $C^{1,\,1}$, and that its level sets near a critical point are asymptotically ellipses. Our analysis relies on a new monotone quantity for a second-order flow satisfied by the support functions of the level sets of $u$. As a byproduct of our methods, we obtain Liouville theorems that generalize a classical result of Jörgens, and include a complete classification of global solutions in 2D to an obstacle problem studied by Jin-Tu-Xiong. As another application, we obtain regularity and rigidity results for rotating-wave solutions of the semigeostrophic equations from meteorology.

title: The Spectral Theory of Cographs: A Survey, Organized by Graph Matrix
abstract: Cographs, the $P_4$-free graphs, are exactly the graphs obtained from a single vertex by repeated disjoint union and complementation. They contain the threshold graphs, $\mathcal{C}$-graphs and form one of the primary areas for spectral graph theory. This survey is organized by matrix: after a preliminary section, there is one section for each of the adjacency, Laplacian, signless Laplacian, distance, eccentricity, Seidel, distance Laplacian and distance signless Laplacian matrices. Within each section we collect what is known for general cographs, for the subclass of $\mathcal{C}$-graphs, and where relevant, for threshold graphs. We highlight the results from the recent years, including the foundational work of Mohammadian et al., Jacobs et al., Ghorbani, Li et al., Niu et al., Lou et al., Wang at al., Mandal et al. Two structural facts are used throughout: every connected cograph has diameter at most $2$, which ties all four distance-type matrices to the adjacency and Laplacian matrices, and the partition of the vertex set into twin classes is equitable for every one of the eight matrices, giving a uniform description of each spectrum (for the Laplacian this is the twin-reduction theory of Barik--Reddy, which we present in detail). Besides surveying the literature, we record several consequences, and mark them as such: an exact decomposition of the eccentricity matrix of a connected cograph, yielding an eigenvalue-free interval for the eccentricity spectrum of all connected cographs; the full distance Laplacian spectrum and its extremal eigenvalues; an eigenvalue-free interval for the distance signless Laplacian valid for every connected graph of diameter at most $2$; an interlacing theorem tying the distance spectrum to the adjacency spectrum. A comparison table across all eight matrices and a list of open problems close the paper.

title: Preservation and Loss of Log-Concavity in the Repulsive Vlasov--Poisson System
abstract: Prékopa's theorem shows that, for jointly log-concave initial data, free transport preserves the log-concavity of spatial densities. This paper asks whether this property persists in the repulsive Vlasov--Poisson system. In dimensions two and higher, we construct smooth, strongly log-concave initial distributions whose spatial densities lose log-concavity at arbitrarily small positive times. For one-dimensional cold-ion data, we prove that the spatial density remains log-concave for all time.

title: Energy-conserving scheme for a shallow-water model with capillary effects
abstract: We consider numerical approximations of shallow-water and thin-film flow models with capillary effects. These models lead to third-order differential equations, and we work with an augmented model with second-order derivatives. For a wide class of such models, which includes the classical shallow-water model and thin-film flow models, we develop a fully discrete energy-conserving scheme for both the quadratic and fully nonlinear capillary models. Numerical results show that the proposed scheme is stable and conserves total energy in the absence of dissipative effects.

title: Infinitely many nonradial positive solutions for two-coupled nonlinear Schrödinger equations in $\bbr^N$ without symmetry
abstract: In this paper, we consider the following two-coupled nonlinear Schrödinger equations: \begin{equation*} \begin{cases} &-Δu+P(x)u=μu^3+βuv^2,\quad\text{in }\R^N,\\ &-Δv+Q(x)v=νv^3+βu^2v,\quad\text{in }\R^N,\\ &u,\,v\in H^1(\R^N) \end{cases} \end{equation*} where $N=2,3$, $P(x)$ and $Q(x)$ are potentials, $μ$ and $ν$ are positive coefficients and $β\in\R\setminus\{0\}$ is the coupling parameter. By developing the intermediate reduction arguments in [del Pino-Wei-Yao, Calc. Var., 2015], we prove the existence of infinitely many nonradial positive solutions to the above system under suitable regularity and decay conditions on $P(x)$ and $Q(x)$, {\bf but without any symmetry assumptions on them}. The scalar version of our result also gives {\bf a positive answer} to the first part of [Question~3, del Pino-Wei-Yao, Calc. Var., 2015] and our method might be helpful in studying other problems.

title: Boltzmann equations with dilatation and shear: global well-posedness and stability
abstract: We study global well-posedness and stability for Boltzmann equations with linear velocity deformation, allowing for arbitrarily large deformation strength. For diagonal dilatation with $-2<γ\leq0$ and cylindrical dilatation with $-3/2<γ\leq0$, with or without shear, we construct global homogeneous solutions for small data and prove their stability under small spatially inhomogeneous perturbations. In scaled variables, the perturbations remain uniformly controlled in deformation-adapted spaces and decay in mixed spatial--velocity norms, algebraically in the diagonal regime and exponentially in the cylindrical regime. For homogeneous simple shear with $-2\leqγ\leq0$, we prove global existence and uniqueness for nonnegative data with finite mass and Fisher information, without smallness or a finite-energy assumption. These solutions conserve mass and propagate additional Sobolev regularity. For spatially inhomogeneous simple shear with $-2<γ\leq0$, we establish global well-posedness for small data. The analysis combines commuting vector fields, dispersive and bilinear collision estimates, and integrability of the rescaled collision coefficients. For homogeneous shear, a positivity-preserving splitting transfers Fisher-information control to rough data, while a Lorentz-space estimate includes the endpoint $γ=-2$ in the global continuation argument.

title: Energy-Time Optimal Decoding Using Expander-Graph LDPC Codes and Mesh Network Architecture
abstract: Within the Thompson VLSI model, the first energy optimal decoding schemes (up to polylogarithmic factors) that also reach clock cycle lower bounds are constructed. Let $N$ be block length. Then, there is an exponential error scaling function and a binary symmetric channel, such that for all $f(N)$ that scales to zero more slowly than this, there is a decoding scheme for this channel with error probability that scales as $O(f(N))$ that has number of clock cycles $T\le O(\sqrt{-\log(f(N)})\text{polylog}(N))$ and energy $E\le O(N\sqrt{-\log(f(N))}\text{polylog}(N))$. This matches fundamental lower bounds up to polylogarithmic factors. The technique uses expander-graph based LDPC codes, a mesh network architecture, and a parallelization technique. The key technical result needed for this is a lemma in graph theory. This lemma is used to show that communication graphs of bounded node degree can be routed through two- and three-dimensional mesh networks without overflowing the memory of any mesh node. Upper bounds are also extended to three dimensions.

title: Last-Iterate Convergence of Stochastic Gradient Methods for Unbounded Problems
abstract: Last-iterate convergence guarantees for stochastic gradient methods have attracted significant attention as practical implementations typically return the last iterate instead of an average of the iterates. In this paper, we study two approaches for analyzing the last-iterate convergence of proximal and projected stochastic gradient methods without bounded domain or bounded variance assumptions, where black-box variational inference serves as a running example. Under two related assumptions relaxing the bounded variance, we show near-optimal anytime rate $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(1/\sqrt{T})$ for the last iterate. Moreover, when the horizon $T$ is known, we remove the logarithmic factor and obtain the optimal order $\mathcal{O}(1/\sqrt{T})$, matching the order known under bounded variance or bounded domain assumptions.

title: A true $Π^0_1$ sentence independence of PA
abstract: We give a true $Π^0_1$ sentence $\varphi$ which is independent of Peano Arithmetic. Moreover, if $\widehatφ$ denotes its interpretation on $ω$ as a sentence of set theory, then $\widehatφ$ is a $Π^0_1$ sentence independent of ZFC.

title: Weak uniqueness for the stochastic heat equation with nondegenerate diffusion: the full Hölder regime
abstract: We prove weak well-posedness for the scalar stochastic heat equation on the one-dimensional torus with uniformly nondegenerate diffusion that is Holder continuous of any positive order. This resolves the weak uniqueness problem in the full positive Holder range, extending our earlier result for exponents above two thirds (arXiv:2608.01279). The proof couples a weak solution to a smooth companion and uses spatial cancellation to estimate the signed covariance difference in a negative Sobolev norm. A finite Gaussian expansion on each Littlewood-Paley block gives the decay needed to remove the coupling drift by a change of measure. A localized Girsanov argument extends the result to measurable drifts of linear growth.

title: Gaps in the Most Frequent Sizes of Integer Sumsets
abstract: Nathanson observed that, for four-element sets $A$ of integers, the most frequent sizes of the iterated sumset $hA$ are separated by triangular numbers. Senger proved this and suggested an analogue for larger sets. We establish this pattern for $k$-element subsets of $\{1,\ldots,q\}$, for every fixed $k\geq3$, where $h\geq2$ is either fixed or grows slower than $q^{1/(2k-1)}$. As $q\to\infty$, almost every such set has the largest possible $h$-fold sumset, and almost every exception has one of $h-1$ explicit smaller sizes. The differences between consecutive sizes among these $h$ values are consecutive $(k-2)$-dimensional simplex numbers.

title: Noncommutative weak almost periodicity and left uniform continuity over locally compact quantum groups
abstract: We study weak almost periodicity and left uniform continuity for Hopf-von Neumann algebras and locally compact quantum groups. For a Hopf-von Neumann algebra $(M,Γ)$, we introduce the space ${\rm WAP}_{{\rm Bessel},π_u}(M_*)$ through norm convergence conditions on rows and columns of slices associated with Bessel families in the universal representation. We prove that this space is the largest $C^*$-subalgebra of ${\rm WAP}(M_*)$ when separately continuous lift of the co-multiplication is multiplicative, and that the two spaces coincide when $M$ is commutative. Furthermore, the algebra $\{x\in C_b(\mathbb{G}): Γ(x)\in M(C_0(\mathbb{G})\otimes C_b(\mathbb{G}))\}$ is characterized as the greatest left introverted $C^*$-subalgebra of ${\rm LUC}(L^1(\mathbb{G}))$ satisfying a left Bessel condition on $L^2(\mathbb{G})$. We also show that ${\rm LUC}(L^1(\mathbb{G}))$ is a $C^*$-algebra whenever the center of $C_0(\mathbb{G})$ contains an element on which the bounded counit is non-zero.

title: Orbital stability and instability of standing waves for an inhomogeneous logarithmic Schrödinger equation
abstract: We study the inhomogeneous logarithmic Schrödinger equation \[ i\partial_tu+Δu+|x|^{-1}u\log|u|^2=0, \qquad (t,x)\in\R\times\R^N,\quad N\ge2. \] For every initial datum in $H^1(\R^N)$, we establish global existence of weak solutions. We also construct explicit positive stationary solutions and solve the associated Nehari minimization problem. For $ω\ge0$, the minimizer is unique up to {a constant} phase and is given by \[ e^{\frac{N-1}{2}(1+\sqrt{1+ω})} e^{-(1+\sqrt{1+ω})|x|}, \] whereas for $ω<0$ the infimum is zero and is not attained. Finally, we prove that the standing waves associated with these profiles are orbitally stable for $ω>0$ by a variational argument, and orbitally unstable for $-1<ω<-1+(N-1)^{-2}$ by combining spectral analysis, localized energy and mass estimates, and phase modulation.

title: A second eigenvalue lower bound for the directed configuration model
abstract: We prove a high-probability lower bound for the second eigenvalue in modulus of the transition matrix of the simple random walk on a directed configuration model with minimal out-degree at least two and maximal degree not too large. The lower bound matches the upper bound found by Coste (2021) on the same model. Our proof bypasses the need to establish convergence of the empirical eigenvalue distribution. Instead, it reduces the spectral lower bound to a central limit theorem for the trace of the transition matrix at powers much larger than the logarithmic scale, a range that previous results failed to reach. Both the general strategy and the central limit theorem might be of independent interest.

title: Necessary and sufficient conditions for the martingale property of stochastic exponentials driven by multi-dimensional diffusions
abstract: We give necessary and sufficient coefficient conditions for stochastic exponentials driven by multidimensional diffusions to be true martingales. The classical reduction to non-exit of the diffusion with Girsanov-shifted drift separates the analysis into smooth boundary points, infinity, and nonsmooth boundary pieces. On smooth domains, under regularity and non-explosion hypotheses, martingality is equivalent to nonpositivity of the shifted Fichera drift, provided an explicit local condition holds where that drift vanishes and the stochastic integrand is unbounded. At infinity, Feller's test gives exact criteria when a scalar function of the diffusion reduces to a one-dimensional diffusion up to a time change with rate bounded above and away from zero. General radial and projection tests supply sufficient conditions. Applications give explicit necessary and sufficient conditions for inverse-CIR and $4/2$ models with correlated factors and singular stochastic integrands, including critical equality cases. The coupled non-affine examples go beyond direct scalar Feller tests and affine Riccati criteria, and exhibit boundary exits not decided by tests at infinity. Further exact criteria cover logarithmic boundary singularities, weighted distances, and an absorbed factor. The martingale conditions also yield uniqueness criteria for associated valuation equations.

title: Compatible Hamel Topologies, Real Valued Isomorphisms and Rational Scalar Continuity
abstract: We study Hamel character topologies on the real line in two parts. Part I treats the full real-orbit (TVG) and the rational-parameter (TVGQ) dual pairs. A divisibility-chain criterion decides compatibility on the rationals and on Q/Z. Compatible subsets of one chain have a compatible join, but two different chains need not: an explicit Chinese remainder construction gives two compatible topologies with an incompatible join. This answers the compact-union question negatively, disproves the Greatest Compatible TVG Conjecture for every nonzero rational-valued Hamel functional, and shows that the corresponding rational and real dual pairs admit no Mackey topology. We classify additive homomorphisms and isomorphisms of the real-valued observation spaces and their automorphism groups, prove that both prime square-denominator topologies are non-nuclear, classify sequences converging for every coefficient functional, and show that the real parameters of continuous characters of the integers with the mixed-prime metric form a set of Hausdorff dimension zero. Part II studies real vector spaces whose Hausdorff additive group topology makes every fixed rational scalar multiplication continuous (TVGQ). A rational-valued Hamel functional and a rational parameter space S generate precompact, modular and real-valued observation topologies whose exact scalar ring is the multiplier ring of S. We compute their completions and character groups, classify the precompact TVGQ topologies, characterize universal separating sequences, show that local compactness and sigma-compactness force the scalar ring to be a field, classify isomorphisms within each modular family (exactly 2^c types), identify greatest-compatible existence with the unrestricted Mackey problem, and prove that all compatible topologies for the rational Hamel pair are non-Baire.

title: Validity of the Behrens--Fisher solution
abstract: The Behrens--Fisher fiducial interval for the difference of two normal means is known from the numerical work of Robinson (1976) to be conservative, but a proof has been lacking. The results here prove that the fiducial interval for any linear combination of $k$ normal means has coverage probability at least its nominal level for all values of the unknown variances. Taraldsen (2026) explains this in more detail using the original data of Behrens (1926). The proof presented in the following rests on a novel plug-in inequality: if a threshold function controls a scaled sum of pivots pointwise in the scale vector, then it also controls the sum with the observed scales plugged in, provided the location errors satisfy a concentration condition formulated through a weighted geometric mean. Independent normal errors satisfy the condition.

title: Boundary Projection Acceleration for 2D One-cell Inversions in the Scattering Limit
abstract: Efficient radiation transport on modern high-performance computers requires algorithms that expose spatial parallelism while maintaining robust convergence. One-cell inversion (OCI) replaces the spatially sequential transport sweep of source iteration with a cell-local solve, making discrete ordinates transport space-parallel, but its spectral radius approaches unity in diffusive problems, and existing accelerators such as transport synthetic acceleration reintroduce sweeps. Here we show that projecting the OCI residual onto a low-order angular space on cell boundaries accelerates convergence in scattering-dominated problems without a transport sweep. We implement the projection in a two-dimensional simple-corner-balance discretization with two angular bases: a linear ($P_1$) basis and one augmented with a quadrant moment ($P_1Q$). Fourier analysis of an infinite homogeneous medium shows that both corrections reduce the spectral radius in optically thick, highly scattering regimes, with $P_{1}Q$ being most effective. Across several test problems, including a modified version of the void-duct streaming benchmark, the method accelerates diffusive and scattering cases but does not uniformly improve convergence in streaming dominated problems. We also find that $P_{1}Q$ is a more robust accelerator than $P_1$ in situations where the flux has strong angular variation. Boundary projection substantially improves OCI convergence in diffusive regimes, and these results delimit the regimes that require additional stabilization or richer projection spaces.

title: Maximal Absolute Monotonicity of Balanced Rational Functions with a Single Repeated Pole
abstract: We study the radius of absolute monotonicity of rational approximations to the exponential of the form \[ φ(z)=\frac{P(z)}{(1-z/b)^s}, \qquad b>0,\qquad °P\le s, \] with approximation orders two and three. For second-order approximation, we prove that the maximal radius in degree $s=5$ is $10$ and determine the unique extremizer. Hence the conjectured value $2s$ by Lóczi and Ketcheson (LMS Journal of Computation and Mathematics, 17 (2014), no.~1, 159--205) remains valid in this case. In contrast, for every integer $s\ge6$ we construct explicitly a rational function with rational coefficients and exact radius \[ 2s+\frac{4(s-3)}{s^2-3s+4}>2s. \] For third-order approximation, we construct, for every $s\ge5$, an explicit rational family with exact radius \[ 2s-1>s-1+\sqrt{s^2-1}. \] These constructions disprove the conjectures of Lóczi and Ketcheson concerning rational functions with a single repeated pole.

title: Measures of maximal entropy for monotone factors of smooth surface diffeomorphisms
abstract: We prove that a transitive monotone factor of a smooth surface diffeomorphism has a unique measure of maximal entropy whenever its topological entropy is positive. Its entropy is the entropy of a single homoclinic class of the diffeomorphism, and the factor map is a measure-theoretic isomorphism on every ergodic measure with positive entropy of that class. The other homoclinic classes are mapped to periodic orbits. We give an application to the essential factor of a diffeomorphism isotopic to a pseudo-Anosov map ---possibly relative to a finite invariant set--- constructed by García-Sassi \& Tal: the essential factor has a unique measure of maximal entropy, which is Bernoulli and has full support.

title: Extending a property of vector spaces to abelian groups
abstract: In this note, we determine the finite abelian groups $G$ such that for every subgroup $H\leq G$ there exists an automorphism $f\in{\rm Aut}(G)$ with ${\rm Fix}(f)=H$. This provides a partial answer to a problem posed by Deaconescu and Walls. Two generalizations of this problem are also proposed.

title: Clifford BMW Categories and Conformal Embeddings of Types B C and D
abstract: In this paper, we give diagrammatic descriptions of the quantum subgroups coming from conformal embeddings of the form $\mathcal{V}(\mathfrak{g}), \check{h}) \subset \mathcal{V}(\mathfrak{so}_{\dim \mathfrak{g}}, 1)$ for $\mathfrak{g}\in \left\{\mathfrak{so}_N, \mathfrak{sp}_{2N}\right\}$, as well as the conformal embeddings of the form $\mathcal{V}(\mathfrak{sp}_{2r + 2}, 2r) \subset \mathcal{C}(\mathfrak{so}_{\dim \mathfrak{sp}_{2r + 2}}, 1)$, extending the techniques of Edie-Michell and Snyder which applied to conformal embeddings of the form $\mathcal{V}(\mathfrak{sl}_r, r) \subset \mathcal{V}(\mathfrak{so}_{\dim \mathfrak{sl}_r}, 1)$. Our main conceptual innovation is the use of fermion condensation to construct a continuous family of planar superalgebras, which we call the Clifford BMW supercategories. The tower of endomorphism algebras, $CW_n(σ, ε)$ is a combination of Birman Wenzl Murakami algebras and Clifford algebras, much in the spirit of the Hecke Clifford algebras. This tower of algebras appears to be new, and already yields some exciting combinatorics.

title: Holomorphic sectional curvature and the Calabi operator on Kähler C-spaces
abstract: We study holomorphic sectional curvature and the Calabi curvature operator on compact Kähler manifolds. First we show that every homogeneous Kähler metric on a generalized flag manifold has positive holomorphic sectional curvature. For the standard homogeneous Kähler-Einstein metric with Einstein constant 2, it is shown that the spectrum of the Calabi operator lies in $(-2,2]$. We determine its sharp upper bound in terms of the anticanonical degrees and characterize the 2-eigenspace. The spectral bounds imply nonnegative cross quadratic bisectional curvature and positive dual cross quadratic bisectional curvature, proving conjectures of Ni and Zheng. We also show that these conditions do not characterize homogeneity: we construct a nonhomogeneous Kähler-Einstein 13-fold whose Calabi spectrum lies strictly inside $(-2,2)$ after the same normalization, as well as nonhomogeneous examples in dimensions 4 and 5. The proofs involve an integral identity for holomorphic sectional curvature, projective embeddings, root-space estimates, and explicit metrics on projective bundles.

title: An axiom of unique reflection
abstract: We characterize neutral planes by three metric conditions: existence of geodesics, side-side-side congruence, and uniqueness of reflection.

title: The Higman-Sims graph and a geometric construction of the Steiner system $S(3,6,22)$
abstract: The Higman-Sims graph is the unique strongly regular graph with parameters $(100,22,0,6)$. In this paper, we show that the only distance-regular antipodal double cover of the Higman-Sims graph is its bipartite double cover. Our main tool is a geometric construction of the Steiner system $S(3,6,22)$.

title: Rigorously Certified Neural-Network Computation of Nonlinear Water Waves at Near-Machine Precision
abstract: We present a computational framework that combines machine-learning-based discovery with rigorous computer-assisted numerical certification and formal verification for strongly nonlinear partial differential equations. We demonstrate the approach for periodic gravity-capillary traveling water waves. Physics-informed neural networks are used as a search mechanism, with the wave profile, wave speed and, in continuation experiments, surface tension learned directly from the governing equations without training data. Through a staged training and refinement procedure, the neural networks achieve near-machine-precision residuals of the governing equations, even in strongly nonlinear regimes. A single formulation recovers high-amplitude Stokes waves, Crapper waves and Wilton ripples. Continuation from a high-amplitude Wilton ripple in surface tension reveals new high-amplitude candidate solutions. We freeze one candidate as an explicit finite representation and rigorously certify a uniform bound on its governing-equation residual using interval arithmetic, accounting for floating-point roundoff, Fourier truncation, aliasing and grid-to-continuum errors. This independently validates the neural-network accuracy. We formalize the certification argument in Lean, which machine-checks the deductions from certified numerical bounds to the residual theorem. Both the interval certification and formalization were developed with substantial assistance from a large language model, while the validity of the result remains independent of the language model: the numerical bounds are rigorously enclosed by interval arithmetic and the subsequent mathematical deductions are checked by the Lean kernel. Together, these steps provide a pipeline from neural discovery to rigorous numerical certification and machine-checked verification with auditable mathematical guarantees.

title: Asymptotic behavior of an integral equation of Landau-Lifschitz type
abstract:
In this paper, we study an integral equation of Landau-Lifschitz-type involving the Riesz potential $$
  u(x)=\ell+C_*\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\frac{u(y)(|\nabla u(y)|^{2}+|u_k(y)|^2)-u_k(y)e_k}{|x-y|^{n-α}}dy, $$ where $\ell \in \mathbb{R}^k$ is a constant vector, $C_* \neq 0$ is a constant, $u\colon\mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{S}^{k-1}:=\{u=(u_1,u_2,\cdots,u_k) \in {\mathbb{R}^{k}};|u|=1\}$, $k \geq 1$, $n \geq 2$, and $0<α<n$. We provide a decay rate at which $|u_k|$ converges to zero under some mild conditions. This argument still works for the Ginzburg-Landau-type integral equation.

title: Continuous-time q-Learning for Finite-Horizon Portfolio Choice with Optimal Stopping in Jump-Diffusion Markets
abstract: We develop a structured continuous-time q-learning framework for finite-horizon investment and optimal stopping under jump-diffusion dynamics with unknown parameters. A penalty approximation transforms the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman variational inequality into an HJB equation with a binary control for the stopping penalty. An auxiliary state incorporates the resulting control-dependent discount factor into a Markovian formulation. We randomize controls on the mixed action space and introduce Shannon entropy regularization, establishing policy improvement and martingale characterizations of the continuous-time q-function. These results motivate a structured q-learning algorithm that constructs the q-function from the penalty HJB equation and jointly learns the value function and unknown generator parameters from sample paths. We apply the method to portfolio choice with optimal stopping in a simulation study. We further conduct a two-asset empirical study, evaluating learned strategies on bootstrap paths from held-out test returns versus an MLE-finite difference benchmark.

title: From What Is Used to What Is Missing: Rethinking Dynamic Rank in LoRA
abstract: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning with LoRA is governed by rank, which controls parameter budget and locally accessible task updates. Existing dynamic-rank methods mainly focus on capacity allocation, leaving unresolved whether the current adaptation space is sufficient for the task. We characterize the first-order information boundary of standard factor gradients, showing that their unobservable subspace coincides with the normal space of the low-rank manifold. Thus, factor gradients alone cannot distinguish under-optimization within the current space from task-relevant directions beyond its first-order reach. This motivates a geometric view of rank evolution, where tangent information optimizes existing degrees of freedom and the normal spectrum quantifies the value of new ones. Under a local quadratic model, we show that leading normal singular directions yield the locally optimal rank expansion, with spectral energy determining its gain. Building on this characterization, we propose GEAR, which turns the tangent--normal decomposition into rank evolution through tangent-space optimization, matrix-free normal-spectrum estimation for rank expansion, and task-induced geometric initialization. Across language and vision benchmarks, GEAR achieves the best average performance in all evaluated settings with substantially fewer trainable parameters. On LLaMA3-8B, it raises the average commonsense score from 86.61 to 88.45 while reducing trainable parameters from 42.0M to 14.4M.

title: Pattern avoidance classes of parking permutations with fixed lucky sets
abstract: For a parking function, the resulting sequence after all cars have parked is called the associated parking permutation. For each parking function, cars that park in their preferred spot are called lucky cars. In this paper, we enumerate parking permutations that avoid a specified set of permutation patterns in $\mathfrak{S}_3$ and whose lucky cars are the first $k$ cars. Often, the enumeration simplifies to a product of a fraction with a binomial coefficient, recovering existing sequences in the OEIS. For two of the classes, the enumerations are new sequences.

title: On Packed Passenger Permutations
abstract: An occupied seat in a binary row is called packed if both of its immediate neighbors are occupied. We give a self-contained combinatorial account of this statistic, equivalently the number of overlapping occurrences of 111. An occupied-block decomposition yields a coefficient formula at fixed occupancy and a direct proof of the sharp minimum max{0,3m-2n-2} for m passengers in n seats, including arrangements attaining the bound. The same decomposition gives a rational generating function, recurrences, expectations, and avoidance asymptotics. Full rows, in which every empty seat would become packed upon being filled, are related to independent sets of a path. A neighborhood-union expansion also gives exact counts on rectangular grids. The emphasis is a unified elementary presentation and explicit extremal constructions, rather than a new general enumeration method.

title: Multiplayer Stopping Games with a Conditionally Atomless Filtration
abstract:
Stopping games are the multiplayer generalization of optimal stopping problems, in which each player independently chooses when to stop, and the payoff depends on who stops first and when. While the existence of $\varepsilon$-equilibria in two-player stopping games with integrable payoffs is known, the multiplayer case has remained open.
  We prove that every multiplayer stopping game in discrete time with integrable payoff process admits an $\varepsilon$-equilibrium for every $\varepsilon > 0$, provided the filtration is conditionally atomless. This condition is satisfied, in particular, when the underlying probability space is $\{0,1\}^{\dN}$ endowed with the uniform measure and its natural filtration.
  Our method also shows that every three-player stopping game, without the restriction to conditionally atomless filtration, admits an $\varepsilon$-equilibrium, for every $\varepsilon > 0$.
  The proof combines techniques developed for two-player stopping games and for multiplayer quitting games, with a key new insight: the richness encoded in a conditionally atomless filtration can substitute for an external public randomization device, allowing players to coordinate without an explicit coordination signal.

title: Elapsed-Service-Time-Aware Preemption for Age of Information Minimization
abstract: We study the age of information and peak age of information in status update systems with an arbitrary number of independent sources sharing a single server with generally distributed service times. We consider a general age-dependent self-preemptive policy in which an in-service update from source $c$ is preempted by a new same-source arrival with a probability $p_c(x)$ that depends on the elapsed service time $x$. This formulation subsumes the non-preemptive, fully self-preemptive, and probabilistically preemptive policies as special cases, and also accommodates threshold-based preemption. We develop a unified analytical framework based on non-homogeneous absorbing continuous-time Markov chains and semi-Markov chains to derive explicit expressions for the average age of information and peak age of information of each source under general per-source service-time distributions and age-dependent preemption rules. The framework applies to both single-source and multi-source systems and enables joint tuning of per-source preemption parameters. Numerical results for fifteen service-time distributions in the single-source setting reveal that the benefits of preemption depend strongly on the service-time hazard-rate structure, with threshold-based preemption providing its most notable additional gains over age-independent policies for distributions with unimodal hazard rates. For a dual-source system with lognormal service times, jointly tuned threshold-based preemption achieves lower sum average age of information and peak age of information than the considered age-independent policies, highlighting the importance of cross-source interactions in preemption decisions.

title: Isospectral Deformations of Diagonal Matrices by Symmetric Matrices in Dimension Four
abstract: For a diagonal matrix $D$ with distinct diagonal entries in an algebraically closed field $K$ we study the symmetric matrices $Q$ with entries in $K$ such that the affine line $D+tQ$ has the same eigenvalues in $K$ as $D$. We study the equality of characteristic polynomials, $χ_{D+tQ}(x)=χ_D(x) \text{ for all }\: t\in K$ and examine the resulting system of equations. For generic diagonal matrices of size at most $4$ we show that only the trivial symmetric matrix $Q=0$ satisfies this isospectral condition. We use this result to compute the degree of a field extension that appears in the invariant theory of quadratic forms under congruence action.

title: Perfect Partitions of Regular Bipartite Graphs
abstract: Let $I_{n,n}$ be a fixed perfect matching of the complete bipartite graph $K_{n,n}$, and let $L_{n,1}=K_{n,n}-I_{n,n}$. A perfect set of $L_{n,1}$ is a $1$-factorization of $L_{n,1}$, that is, a set of $n-1$ pairwise edge-disjoint perfect matchings whose union is $E(L_{n,1})$; a perfect partition of $L_{n,1}$ is a partition of the set of all perfect matchings of $L_{n,1}$ into perfect sets. Brualdi, Chiang, and Li (2005) asked whether $L_{n,1}$ admits a perfect partition. Identifying both sides of the bipartition with $[n]=\{1,2,\ldots ,n\}$, the perfect matchings of $L_{n,1}$ are exactly the derangements of $[n]$, the perfect sets correspond bijectively to the reduced Latin squares of order $n$, and the perfect partitions are exactly the perfect matchings of the $(n-1)$-uniform hypergraph whose vertices are the derangements of $[n]$ and whose edges are the perfect sets. We first give, for every $n$, a constructive lower bound on the maximum number of pairwise disjoint perfect sets of $L_{n,1}$. We then show that $L_{5,1}$ has exactly $42$ distinct perfect partitions and that $L_{6,1}$ has at least $82$ distinct perfect partitions; these are the first examples demonstrating that perfect partitions need not be unique. Finally, we exhibit two distinct perfect partitions of $L_{7,1}$, resolving the $n=7$ open problem raised by Brualdi et al.

title: An improved lower bound for maximal partial Room squares
abstract: We establish a new asymptotic lower bound for the volume of a maximal partial Room square of even order $n$. We prove that its volume is at least $\frac{2\sqrt{66}-6}{57}n^2-O(n)$, improving the leading coefficient $1/8$ in the lower bound obtained by Meszka and Rosa. The proof combines two counting arguments, one based on a transversal of empty cells and the other on the graph of occurring symbol pairs.

title: Non-Kähler Hyperbolicity: Surfaces and Codimension One
abstract: We study hyperbolicity notions for compact complex manifolds defined by special Hermitian metrics and by holomorphic maps from $\mathbb C^{n-1}$ (divisorial hyperbolicity). For surfaces we show that divisorial and Brody hyperbolicity coincide and that Hermitian-symplectic and Kähler hyperbolicity coincide when $h^{2,0}=0$. In any dimension we prove obstructions to Gauduchon hyperbolicity, show that projective spaces are not divisorially hyperbolic, and give divisorially hyperbolic manifolds that are not balanced hyperbolic.

title: Higher theta lifts via BGG resolutions
abstract: We compute higher theta lifts of ladder representations of general linear groups over division algebras over non-archimedean local fields. We achieve this by constructing BGG-type coresolutions and proving that their terms are acyclic for the covariant theta functor. We then compute the resulting complex explicitly, determining the higher theta lifts and the degrees in which they are nonzero.

title: Seeking the dense half in $K_4$-free graphs
