title: Information-Spectrum General Formulas for the Capacity Region of Classical-Quantum Multiple Access Channels
abstract: For classical-quantum multiple access channels (cq-MACs) with two senders, we give several general expressions for the capacity region, valid for arbitrary sequences of channels. In the case of asymptotically vanishing error ($\varepsilon=0$), the capacity region is expressed in terms of spectral inf-mutual information rates. For every $0\le\varepsilon<1$, the $\varepsilon$-capacity region is expressed in terms of a quantity defined through a linear combination of three alternative hypotheses. In particular, the outer bound of Kubo and Nagaoka (2015) is tight. Our results include the quantum counterpart of the general formula of Han (1998) for the classical MAC. The most important ingredient is the one-shot inner bound of Sen (2021), which we apply to each member of an arbitrary channel sequence.

title: Randomized and Oracle-Based Feasible Directions Methods for Nonsmooth Nonconvex Constrained Optimization
abstract: Minimizing nonsmooth nonconvex objectives over general convex sets using no derivatives of the objective, together with structural access to the constraint set, poses a fundamental geometric difficulty: at boundary points, the feasible direction cone may fail to be closed, preventing the construction of finite sets of search directions that capture all feasible descent directions. We develop a feasible-directions framework for problems structured as the difference between a continuously differentiable function and a convex function over a closed convex set, and access the objective without knowledge of its decomposition, through exact line searches along feasible segments. To address the geometric obstruction, we introduce $η$-feasible directions, which remain uniformly separated from the boundary of the feasible direction cone, enabling finite-direction search even in the presence of nonlinear constraints. We present two algorithmic realizations of this framework. The first assumes access to an $η$-direction oracle and extends feasible-directions methods from linear to general convex constraints. The second replaces the oracle by a noise-augmented randomization scheme that constructs spanning directions from the affine-hull inner normal and almost surely avoids nonsmooth boundary points when initialized outside that set. Under curvature bounds and Lipschitz continuity of the smooth component's gradient, we jointly control the spanning coefficients and feasible step lengths of the oracle construction. This yields finite-time approximate $d$-stationarity along every unit feasible direction admitting a prescribed positive step length. For both methods, we also establish a rate in the proximal directional minimization (PDM) measure, assuming uniformly bounded direction-set sizes. Randomized exploration ensures that, almost surely, every accumulation point is $d$-stationary.

title: A Universal Threshold Theory for Local Properties of Random Linear Codes
abstract:
Thresholds for local properties tell us which guarantees to expect from random linear codes (RLCs) and help us carry those guarantees over to structured codes. A monotone property is $b$-local if a collection of at most $b$ codewords can witness its satisfaction or failure, as in list decoding and list recovery. The threshold of $\mathcal P$ is the code dimension at which the probability that an RLC in $\mathbb{F}_q^n$ satisfies $\mathcal P$ crosses $1/2$ in a sharp transition. We show that the threshold of a $b$-local property $\mathcal P$ is within $O(b)$ dimensions of the expectation threshold. This is the dimension predicted by the best union bound over covers of $\mathcal P$: families of subspaces such that the span of every witness contains at least one member.
  This gives a general derandomization statement: Any decreasing local property satisfied by RLCs at a given rate holds at a similar rate for pseudorandom ensembles that fool the cover union bound. In addition to previously studied ensembles, these include codes whose parity-check matrix is sampled from a small-bias distribution. Because our threshold characterization applies to all local properties, this derandomization also reaches properties beyond the scope of earlier reductions, including maximum loads in linear hashing for arbitrary input sets, rank-metric list decoding, and list decoding from insertion-deletion errors and burst errors.
  Our theorem unifies and strengthens prior works on row-symmetric and coordinate-wise linear characterizations, which located the threshold to within $O(q^{2b}\log_q n)$ and $O(b^2+nb/\log_2 q)$ dimensions, respectively. We obtain $O(b)$ error for every $b$-local property, independently of alphabet size. Under suitable pseudorandomness bounds, the rate loss vanishes for every $b=o(n)$, compared to $b=O(\log n)$ for earlier frameworks.

title: Holomorphic calculus on $L^p(\ell^q)$ I: optimal angles
abstract: Let $L$ generate a symmetric contraction semigroup. We prove a holomorphic Hörmander calculus on $L^p(X;\ell^q)$ at the optimal angle $\max\{\arcsin|1-2/p|,\arcsin|1-2/q|\}$, with boundary Sobolev order $s>3$.

title: Randomly shifted lattice rules for SDEs with constant diffusion: error bounds uniform in time discretization and dimension
abstract: We study randomly shifted rank-1 lattice rules for computing $\mathbb{E}[g(\mathbf{X}_T)]$, where $\mathbf{X}_T$ is the terminal state of a stochastic differential equation (SDE) with constant diffusion matrix. Discretizing the SDE by the Euler--Maruyama scheme with $m$ uniform time steps turns the expectation into an integral whose dimension grows with $m$ and whose integrand has a nested composition structure; both complicate the lattice rule error analysis. We generate the Brownian path by the Brownian bridge construction and handle the nested structure using the multivariate Faà di Bruno formula and a rooted-tree expansion. Under suitable regularity and growth conditions, we prove that an $N$-point randomly shifted lattice rule with a uniformly random generating vector achieves a mean absolute sampling error of $O(N^{-1+\varepsilon})$ for every $\varepsilon\in(0,1/2)$ and every prime $N$, with the implied constant independent of $m$. To improve stability and control higher error moments, the median lattice estimator is used. The estimator takes the median of $R=2k-1$ independent lattice estimates and achieves an $L^q$ error of $O(N^{-1+\varepsilon})$ for every $1\le q<k/(1-\varepsilon)$. We further establish error bounds independent of both the state dimension and the Brownian path dimension under an additional summability condition on the columns of the diffusion matrix. Numerical experiments show that median lattice estimators converge faster than Monte Carlo estimators and remain stable as the number of time steps $m$ grows. For models satisfying the additional summability condition, stability is also observed as the state and Brownian path dimensions increase.

title: Finiteness of singularities for higher-weight axially symmetric minimizers of the relaxed Dirichlet energy
abstract: Let $k\ge2$ be an integer. We prove that every minimizer of the Bethuel--Brezis--Coron relaxed Dirichlet energy in the signed meridional $k$-axial class, with continuous $H^1$ degree-zero data on the boundary of a ball, is smooth outside a finite subset of the symmetry axis. This extends the weight-one finiteness theorem of Hardt--Lin--Poon and resolves the finite-singularity question posed by Martinazzi--Rivière as Open Problem~A, in the fixed-boundary Bethuel--Brezis--Coron setting with continuous degree-zero data. The interior argument uses a distributional graph-boundary identity, height-preserving half-turn replacements, and exact square completions retaining the current cost. Cap-valued crosscuts and a finite incidence count exclude singular accumulation at the boundary poles.

title: Using Transformers to Generate 3-Manifold Triangulations
abstract: Using dehydration signatures as an encoding, we train GPT-2-style transformers to generate triangulations of 3-dimensional manifolds. Our main runs each use approximately 3 exaFLOPs, spanning a 200 million parameter model trained on 60 million sphere triangulations to an 11 million parameter model trained on 1.1 billion sphere triangulations. The optimal model has 10 blocks, width 640 and generates dehydration signatures of closed manifolds of various topological types at a rate of 6.9%, 82% of which are spheres. To investigate how our method scales, we use the technique of IsoFLOP curves on 15-tetrahedron triangulations of the 3-sphere, over a compute range of 6 to 3000 petaFLOPs, and observe neural scaling behaviour. We extract a parameter scaling exponent of $α= 0.49$ ($[0.48, 0.50]$ stat, $\pm 0.02$ syst), and an optimal ratio of 234 tokens per parameter for training. In addition, we present a number of smaller experiments, including evidence that transformers are able to learn to count degree-one edges near-perfectly, but get progressively worse when counting edges with higher degrees.

title: Branched Covers and Fiberwise Degeneration along Weak Kähler Geodesics
abstract: On the projective line, we construct a pair of smooth Kähler potentials whose weak geodesic has isolated quadratic zeros of the fiber form at two fixed points throughout an interior time interval. The geodesic is smooth near these zeros, and its space-time form has constant rank one there. For the same fixed endpoints, the minimum fiber eigenvalue of the nondegenerate Monge-Ampère approximations tends to zero, answering AIMPL Problem 2.5 in the negative. The construction works on every compact connected Riemann surface with a prescribed Kähler form and realizes any positive even order of vanishing. Taking products yields higher-dimensional examples in which the fiber rank drops by one along a smooth hypersurface while the space-time form retains maximal rank nearby. The proof starts from a semipositive model built from a branched cover. We make its endpoints strictly positive by local corrections and use comparison along holomorphic curves to prove that the weak geodesic still agrees with the model on an explicit interior region. There a ramification point of local degree $m$ gives a fiber zero of order exactly $2m-2$.

title: Group-free radial Kunze-Stein phenomenon on affine buildings
abstract: We give a geometric proof of the radial Kunze--Stein phenomenon on the good vertices of a thick, locally finite, regular affine building of irreducible type. The proof uses a positive spherical function, its joint eigenvalues for sphere averages, and the growth of vector-distance spheres. Conjugation by this function and complex interpolation yield a weighted $\ell^2$ estimate and the boundedness of radial operators with $\ell^p$ kernels for $1\leq p<2$. We also present proofs by the averaging operators norms, by the Schur test and by Helgason transform. A further interpolation gives weighted mixed-exponent estimates. No transitivity assumption on the automorphism group is required; in particular the argument applies to buildings of type $\widetilde A_2$ without a Bruhat--Tits realization.

title: Topology-Inspired Interfaces in Non-Local Mass-Spring Lattices
abstract: Non-local couplings offer a means of engineering the dynamics and topology of discrete lattices beyond the constraints of nearest-neighbour (NN) interactions. Here, we extend the mass-spring Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) model to incorporate beyond-nearest-neighbour (BNN) connections that preserve the chiral symmetry of the diatomic unit cell, investigating how their range and strength shape the bulk response. We show that the accessible winding numbers are bounded by the lattice connectivity, while the spring stiffnesses select the specific topological phase. We further investigate the challenges posed by non-local interfaces, where the extended connectivity inherently introduces local boundary perturbations. The dynamic freedom afforded by BNN couplings is exploited by examining interfaces between dynamically and topologically dissimilar bulk media, revealing a band-gap-induced asymmetry in the localisation of interface states. We show that the interfacial configuration provides a means of controlling the existence and character of localised interface modes, with changes to the interface enabling the tuning of mode frequencies, localisation and hybridisation with the bulk bands.

title: The minimal excludant and the least $r$-gaps of $\ell$-regular partitions
abstract: The minimal excludant (mex) of an integer partition $λ$ is the smallest positive integer that is not a part of $λ$. In this paper we study an analogue of this statistic for $\ell$-regular partitions with $\ell\geq2$, that is, partitions in which no part is divisible by $\ell$. Recently, Meher \cite{Meher} defined the minimal excludant for $\ell$-regular partitions. Motivated by Meher \cite{Meher}, for an $\ell$-regular partition we define its least $r$-gap as the smallest positive integer not divisible by $\ell$ that appears fewer than $r$ times as a part, and we obtain the two-variable generating function for the number of $\ell$-regular partitions of $n$ with a given least $r$-gap. Let $σ^{\mex}_{\ell}(n)$, and $σ^{\mex}_{\ell,r}(n)$ be the sum of the of the mex values over all $\ell$-regular partitions of $n$ and least $r$-gaps over all $\ell$-regular partitions of $n$ respectively. Using Jacobi's triple product identity, we derive explicit expressions for the generating function of $σ^{\mex}_{\ell}(n)$, and $σ^{\mex}_{\ell,r}(n)$, with separate formulas for even and odd $\ell$. We also show that the sequence $\{σ^{\mex}_{\ell,r}(n)\}_{n\ge0}$ is weakly increasing for every $\ell\ge2$ and $r\ge1$. Also, using Ingham's Tauberian theorem, we establish Hardy--Ramanujan type asymptotic formulas for $σ^{\mex}_{\ell,r}(n)$ when $\ell=4,5,7$ and $r\ge1$ is arbitrary. Lastly, we prove $σ^{\mex}_{\ell,r}$ is odd infinitely often, and we establish a quantitative lower bound, showing that the number of such n up to X grows at least like log log X.

title: Newton Steps are Faster for Linear Complementarity Problems
abstract:
Linear Complementarity Problems (LCPs) with sufficient matrices form a well-studied class of problems, dating back from the foundational works of Cottle and Dantzig (1968). LCPs capture convex quadratic programs, and admit reductions from problems such as discounted stochastic games or mean-payoff games. While the original approach for solving these problems was based on pivoting methods, in their 1991 book, Kojima, Megiddo, Noma, and Yoshise introduced an interior point method (IPM) with running time that is polynomial in the input size, but which depends linearly on a certain parameter called the handicap number of the matrix. Despite the ensuing rich literature on sufficient LCP IPMs, the linear dependence on the handicap number has not been improved since then.
  We present an IPM whose running time depends on the square root of the handicap number. The algorithm can decrease the duality gap by a constant factor in $O\left(\min\left\{\sqrt{n} (1+κ),n^{9/8}\sqrt{1+κ}\right\}\right)$ iterations. Curiously, this can already be achieved using standard Newton updates. We analyze the IPM in a norm defined by a local weighting, where centralizing Newton steps quadratically converge to the central path, without any dependence on the handicap number. The weights arise from a characterization by Rump (Linear Algebra and Its Applications, 1997, 1998, 2003) of the sign-real spectral radius and its relation to sufficiency; another ingredient of our proof is a new operator norm characterization of the handicap number.
  Moreover, the connection to Rump's work also enables us to show coNP-completeness of testing sufficiency, and approximation hardness of the handicap number.

title: Interlacing of the Volume and Half-Volume Spectra
abstract: We give a direct proof of the weak interlacing inequalities \[ω_p\leq\widetildeω_p\leqω_{p+1}\] between the volume and half-volume spectra of a closed connected Riemannian manifold $M^{n+1}$, $n+1\geq3$. We also prove that, for a residual set of smooth metrics, the area of every smooth embedded half-volume CMC boundary lies outside the rational span of the areas of smooth closed embedded minimal hypersurfaces. For dimensions $3\le n+1\le 5$, these results yield strict interlacing for generic metrics and a lower bound of order $A^{n+1}$ for the number of distinct half-volume CMC boundaries with area at most $A$.

title: On the anisotropic mean curvature flow in the Gaussian space
abstract: In this paper, we study the anisotropic mean curvature flow in the Gaussian space endowed with a Finsler metric obtained from a Minkowski metric by a conformal deformation. We first derive the conformal transformation formulas for the fundamental tensor, the Cartan tensor, and the Chern connection of the conformally related Finsler metrics. Based on these formulas, we express the anisotropic mean curvature in the Gaussian space in terms of the corresponding anisotropic mean curvature with respect to the original Minkowski metric, and derive the associated evolution equation. Finally, we establish the short-time existence and uniqueness of smooth solutions by reformulating the geometric evolution equation as a strictly parabolic quasilinear partial differential equation.

title: Geometric Functional Inequalities for Markov Processes: An Invitation via the Langevin Diffusion
abstract: Functional inequalities provide a language for reasoning about the long-time properties of ergodic Markov processes in terms of their macroscopic geometry. This article offers an informal introduction to functional inequalities for readers who are more familiar with probabilistic tools based around couplings, Lyapunov techniques, and similar. The main ideas are developed through the overdamped Langevin diffusion, where various functionals related to this convergence admit particularly transparent expressions, and for which the key associated inequalities -- namely, the Poincaré and logarithmic Sobolev inequalities -- are especially well-studied. We explain the qualitative content of these inequalities, what they imply about convergence to equilibrium, how they transform and compose under natural operations, and how they interface with classical probabilistic approaches. Related inequalities are discussed more briefly, and an annotated guide is provided for readers wishing to enter the wider literature.

title: Instability of Self-Similar Implosions for the Compressible Euler Equations
abstract: We prove that all known regular self-similar implosion solutions of the isentropic compressible Euler equations are unstable to shock formation. The perturbations can be chosen to be small in a class determined by the regularity threshold of the background. The proof relies on an amplification mechanism which occurs along the surface of the backward sonic cone from the implosion point. Motivated by our main results, we formulate an implosion censorship conjecture for the compressible Euler equations, stating that classical implosions are unstable to shock formation.

title: The Chow ring of a wonderful compactification
abstract: The theory of wonderful compactifications provides a common framework encompassing the constructions of important varieties such as the Fulton-MacPherson configuration spaces, the moduli space of $n$-pointed stable rational curves, and the De Concini-Procesi models of subspace arrangements, and, more generally, of smooth compactifications in which the subvarieties in a building set are replaced by a simple normal crossings boundary divisor. We give a presentation of the Chow ring of a wonderful compactification, assuming only that the Chow ring of the ambient variety surjects onto that of each subvariety in the induced arrangement. Our results recover and extend many previously known presentations and apply to a broad range of new examples.

title: Distinguishing invariants of Cayley Graphs, Hamming graphs, and wreath product actions
abstract: Let $Γ$ be a nontrivial group that acts on a graph $G=(V,E)$. The total distinguishing number $D''_Γ(V\cup E)$ (distinguishing index $D'_Γ(E)$) of the action is the least number of labels required for a total labeling (edge labeling) of $G$ so that the only elements of $Γ$ that preserve the labeling belong to the pointwise stabilizer of $V\cup E$ (pointwise stabilizer of $E$). We obtain upper bounds of these invariants for Cayley graphs and under various group actions, including free actions, wreath product actions, and coordinatewise actions on Cartesian powers of graphs. Our first main result shows that, if $Γ$ acts faithfully on $G$, with $|V|\geq 2, |E|\geq 1$ and the natural action of the wreath product $W=Γ\wr S_k$ on $V^k$ induces an action of $W$ on the Cartesian power $G^{k}=(V^{k},E_k)$, then $ D''_{W}(V^k\cup E_k)\le D''_Γ(V\cup E)+k-1 $ for any $k\geq 2$. We also establish the sharpness of several of our bounds through examples involving cyclic, symmetric, and alternating groups. Moreover, we determine these distinguishing invariants for the symmetric group action on Hamming graphs.

title: Hybrid Newton-BFGS high-index saddle dynamics for accelerating saddle-point searches
abstract: We propose a hybrid Newton-BFGS high-index saddle dynamics (HiSD) method for accelerating saddle-point searches. The method constructs a Newton correction on the unstable subspace from the available negative eigenpairs, while BFGS updates based on projected secant information approximate the inverse Hessian on the stable subspace. By combining Newton and quasi-Newton corrections, the method incorporates curvature information in both subspaces while preserving the ascent-descent structure of HiSD. Accounting for the evolving stable subspaces, we establish local $Q$-superlinear convergence of the full-memory version near nondegenerate saddle points under suitable assumptions. We further develop a limited-memory version for large-scale problems and provide fixed-step and line search strategies. Numerical experiments show local convergence behavior consistent with the theory and demonstrate acceleration on ill-conditioned problems and degenerate saddle manifolds in neural-network loss landscapes. The method also supports efficient upward and downward saddle searches for a liquid crystal model, further illustrating its broad applicability to saddle-point computation.

title: Nonlinear optimal stopping and domineering claims
abstract: We study nonlinear optimal stopping and domineering claims in a Brownian--Poisson filtration, under a nonlinear evaluation induced by a Lipschitz BSDE driver satisfying a comparison condition. A nonlinear domineering claim is a strong $\mathcal{E}^f$-martingale dominating the reward process at every stopping time. We first establish the existence of such claims for every optional reward in $\mathcal{S}^2$. For left-limited, right-upper semicontinuous rewards, we prove a local dual representation at every stopping time: the nonlinear optimal stopping value equals the essential infimum of the values of all domineering claims defined on the remaining stochastic interval. This infimum is attained by a claim constructed from the associated reflected BSDE. We further show that a global domineering claim attains the value at a prescribed stopping time if and only if the reflection processes have accumulated no increase up to that time, with the appropriate endpoint convention. When the reward is right-upper semicontinuous in $\mathcal{E}^f$-expectation and the family of contact times is nonempty, its essential infimum is optimal. Under strict comparison, we also establish a necessary contact condition for optimality. No convexity assumption on the driver is required.

title: Bernstein-Sato polynomials of generic Pfaffian ideals
abstract:
We determine all roots and their multiplicities in the Bernstein--Sato polynomial of every generic Pfaffian ideal. In the nonmaximal case, the roots lie in explicit rational windows indexed by the rank strata. Integral roots retain their label multiplicities, whereas every nonintegral root is simple, including values with several labels. The proof combines graph-module relations, skew Capelli operators, central characters, and a weighted Mellin integral. We deduce the strong motivic monodromy conjecture for Pfaffian ideals, with pole orders bounded by Bernstein--Sato root multiplicities. For Pfaffians of size $2r$, the largest possible root multiplicity as the matrix size varies is $\lfloor(\sqrt{8r+1}-1)/2\rfloor$. In the nonmaximal case we also prove that the nonunipotent part of the Verdier specialization has zero nilpotent monodromy.
  Keywords. Bernstein-Sato polynomial, Pfaffian ideal, root multiplicities, strong monodromy conjecture.

title: Extending graph metrics to hyperspaces of vertex sets: optimization and reinforcement learning applications
abstract: An undirected connected graph can be interpreted as a metric space by considering the path distance between its vertices. Extending this perspective, we explore how walks in the graph, viewed as sequences of subsets of vertices $V$, fit into a more general framework where the path distance emerges as a special case of broader metrics that define hypertopologies on the space of subsets of $V$. In this paper, we propose a general framework to address this issue, motivated by the extension of recent reinforcement learning algorithms on graphs through Lipschitz function extensions. Our approach demonstrates how models for dynamical systems and related machine learning techniques can be adapted to (quasi-pseudo-metric) hyperspaces, offering a novel perspective for the analysis and modeling of dynamical systems. Finally, we illustrate the practical relevance of our theoretical contributions through a concrete graph optimization example, highlighting the utility and effectiveness of our proposed approach.

title: Object ideals and idempotent completeness
abstract: We construct an idempotent complete Frobenius exact category with an idempotent complete stable category in which a complete ideal cotorsion pair of object ideals induces a cotorsion pair of objects that fails to be complete. This gives a negative answer to the question of Fu, Guil Asensio, Herzog and Torrecillas under idempotent completeness. The construction uses a lemma on dense triangulated subcategories and an example of Bondarko and Sosnilo in which a weight structure fails to extend to the idempotent completion. The induced cotorsion pair is hereditary, and every object admits an ordinary precover from its left class and an ordinary preenvelope into its right class. We characterize which objects admit special precovers and which admit special preenvelopes.

title: Bergman Kernel Zeros on Rational Hartogs Triangles
abstract: We prove the Edholm--Mathew nonvanishing conjecture for the palindromic polynomials associated with rational Hartogs triangles. For relatively prime positive integers $m>n$, we show that $e^{-i(m-n)θ}Q_{m,n}(e^{iθ})$ is strictly positive for every real $θ$ and derive an explicit lower bound. The proof expresses this trigonometric polynomial as a finite average of products of unnormalized Fejér kernels. It follows that $Q_{m,n}$ has exactly $m-n$ zeros in the punctured unit disc, counted with multiplicity. As a consequence, a rational Hartogs triangle has a zero-free Bergman kernel if and only if its exponent is the reciprocal of a positive integer.

title: Decomposable polytopes with few vertices
abstract: A polytope $P$ is decomposable if it can be written as the Minkowski sum of two polytopes that are not homothetic to it. It is well known that decomposable $d$-dimensional polytopes with $2d$ or fewer vertices are the simplicial prisms. More recent work shows that, with two exceptions in low dimensions, decomposable $d$-dimensional polytopes with exactly $2d+1$ vertices are either pentasms or capped prisms. All these examples have a line segment for a summand. In this paper, we extend this conclusion to decomposable $d$-polytopes with exactly $2d+2$ or $2d+3$ vertices. In both cases, all such polytopes, with three exceptions, have a line segment for a summand. The exceptional cases are specified in detail.

title: Riemannian hypermaps to complex space forms
abstract: In this paper, we propose the notion of a \textit{hypermap}, defined as a Riemannian map whose range distribution is tangent to a real hypersurface of a complex space form. This construction leads to a new direction in Riemannian map theory. We establish the fundamental Gauss and Codazzi equations for a hypermap and use them to investigate the extrinsic geometry of its range leaves. In particular, when the ambient complex space form is non-Euclidean, we prove that these leaves cannot be totally umbilical and that their shape operator fails to be parallel. We further incorporate the Hopf condition and define \textit{Hopf hypermap}, thereby obtaining the analog of Hopf hypersurfaces. We also examine the umbilical case and show that an umbilical hypermap cannot exist to a non-Euclidean complex space form. This motivates introducing the \textit{$η$-umbilical hypermap}, which broadens the class of examples for studying the interaction between the range geometry and the ambient complex structure. Finally, we analyze the principal curvatures associated with these hypermaps, including results on their multiplicities and constancy.

title: Brauer groups of generalised Markoff surfaces
abstract: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic zero with $a,b,c\in k^\times$ and let $m\in k\setminus\{0,4abc\}$. We compute the Brauer group of the generalised Markoff surface $ax^2+by^2+cz^2-xyz=m$. We also construct several counterexamples to the integral Hasse principle, which are explained by the Brauer--Manin obstruction.

title: The parity of the number of missing integers in partitions
abstract: Missing integers in partitions have been studied by many authors. A missing integer of a partition is a positive integer smaller than its largest part that does not occur as a part. We investigate parity biases for the number of missing integers in partitions and overpartitions. For every integer $c\ge2$, we prove that the coefficients $a_c(n)$ of $(-cq;q)_\infty/(-q;q)_\infty$ are eventually strictly positive and provide an effectively computable threshold. The proof uses the circle method, combining a saddle-point analysis on the major arc with explicit uniform estimates on the minor arcs. Specializing to $c=2$ and $c=3$, and verifying the remaining finite cases, we show that partitions and overpartitions of $n$ with an even number of missing integers outnumber those with an odd number for $n>34$ and $n>27$, respectively. We further prove that, for $n>10$, the difference between the numbers of ordinary partitions with an even and an odd number of missing integers is smaller than the number of partitions of $n$ into distinct parts. These results confirm three conjectures of Bhoria, Eyyunni and Santra. We also give a combinatorial interpretation of $a_c(n)$ for every integer $c\ge4$ in terms of colored partitions, generalizing the partition and overpartition interpretations of Bhoria, Eyyunni and Santra for $c=2$ and $c=3$, respectively.

title: Global Solvability in Critical Sobolev Spaces for divergence-type equations associated with elliptic systems of vector fields
abstract: In this work, we present global solvability results, in critical Sobolev spaces, for divergence-type equations associated with elliptic systems of vector fields.

title: Construction of Transverse Metrics from Transversely Elliptic Operators on Foliated Manifolds
abstract: The existence of a transverse metric on a foliated manifold is typically used as a framework for studying transversely elliptic basic differential operators. This article details a method for constructing such a transverse metric directly from the principal symbol of the operator. Consequently, rather than treating the transverse metric as a mere working assumption, we demonstrate that its existence is a necessary condition for the very presence of a transversely elliptic operator.

title: A Hypergeometric RM Surface: Integral Monodromy and Level-11 Covers
abstract: We study a genus-two hypergeometric family whose Jacobians have real multiplication by $\Q(\sqrt5)$. We identify the relevant primitive factor and integral rank-two monodromy; at one real embedding the projective image is $Δ(2,5,\infty)$, while the conjugate image is nondiscrete. At the primes above $11$, the degree-$12$ Borel covers are quadratic pullbacks of genus-one triangular modular curves. The same rank-two systems have finite-field hypergeometric Frobenius traces, yielding the local Euler factors and a quadratic transformation twisted by the character of $2$.

title: Recurrence and Uniqueness Criteria for Markov Processes from Moments of Integral-Type Functionals
abstract: We investigate recurrence and uniqueness of continuous-time Markov chains using moments of integral-type functionals. Unlike the classical criteria from Chen (2004) and the Feller-Reuter criterion, we develop general unified conditions for recurrence and uniqueness of Markov processes based on moments of integral-type functionals. The associated criteria follow directly from these conditions whenever the mean functionals can be expressed explicitly. As applications, explicit recurrence and uniqueness criteria are derived for single-birth, single-death, and birth-death processes on trees.

title: Thurston algorithm for real entire maps: existence and uniqueness
abstract:
This paper deals with the real Thurston pullback algorithm for entire maps with finitely many finite singular values, all real. Given a finite forward-invariant marking containing the singular values and satisfying an interval no-Levy-cycle condition, the pullback is shown to have a unique fixed point and it is shown that every orbit converges to it. The resulting entire map uniquely realises the marked dynamics up to positive affine conjugacy. Thus this paper established Thurston realisation and uniqueness in the setting of real entire maps with a finite postsingular set.
  As usual, the realisation problem reduces to the existence of a fixed point of the Thurston map $T$ which in the real setting acts on a simplex $W$ of dimension $s-2$ if the required postsingular set consists of $s$ points. The key estimate concerns a finite real preimage interval: when its critical multiplicity is bounded and its endpoint values stay separated from the singular values unless they equal to one, its hyperbolic diameter grows at most double-logarithmically as the separation tends to zero.
  An expansive marking (absence of Levy cycles) then rules out configurations near the boundary of the simplex whose displacement under the Thurston map is at most a fixed multiple of their distance to the boundary. Using a version of the Brouwer fixed point theorem, this immediately implies that the Thurston map $T$ has a fixed point. The argument permits infinitely many real and non-real critical points and different behaviours as the real variable tends to $+\infty$ and $-\infty$.
  Additional estimates for fixed labelled inverse branches, which are not strictly necessary for the proof of the Main Theorem, are given in the appendices.

title: The Zhukovskiy-Volterra gyroscope: geometry and reduction
abstract: We describe a symplectic reduction of the Zhukovskiy integrable case of motion of a rigid body about a fixed point with a gyroscope in $\mathbb R^n$ to an integrable magnetic flow on a sphere $S^{n-1}$. We also present Zhukovskiy's geometric interpretation of motion of the Euler top with a gyroscope, aka the Zhukovskiy--Volterra gyroscope, and perform a symplectic reduction of this system to an integrable magnetic flow on a $2$-dimensional sphere.

title: Online Optimization for Controlling HVAC Systems
abstract: Heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning (HVAC) systems account for a significant portion of buildings' energy consumption, motivating the design of energy- and cost-efficient control strategies. However, conventional strategies employ simple, reactive control, without incorporating a model. Therefore, in this paper we adopt an economic model predictive control framework and focus on designing online algorithms to solve the control input design problems with a limited computational budget. In particular, we propose two tailored online algorithms based on projected gradient descent, with a custom projection routine, and the projected primal-dual method. We discuss the pros and cons of both algorithm designs, focusing in particular on computational efficiency. We further compare them through numerical experiments simulating the control of an HVAC system over the course of a day. The results show that computationally efficient online solvers for HVAC systems control are indeed possible. Moreover, the performance closely matches that of a baseline algorithm with unlimited computational budget, in terms of reference temperature tracking and comfort temperature range enforcement.

title: Prescribed Color Patterns in Tight Hamilton Cycles and Spanning Trees
abstract: We compare transversal and pattern thresholds for two spanning structures. For every fixed $k\ge 3$ and $α>0$, we prove that every sufficiently large $n$-vertex $k$-graph collection with minimum codegree at least $(1/2+α)n$ contains a tight Hamilton cycle with any prescribed color pattern. Hence the transversal and pattern thresholds for tight Hamilton cycles coincide asymptotically. For spanning trees, we show that for every $α>0$ there exists $c=c(α)>0$ such that every $n$-vertex graph collection with minimum degree at least $(1/2+α)n$ contains every $n$-vertex tree with maximum degree at most $n^c$ and any prescribed color pattern. On the other hand, we construct spanning trees of maximum degree $\sqrt n+1$ whose pattern threshold exceeds their transversal threshold by a positive linear term.

title: Over-the-Scene Computation: Illumination-Programmed Functional Sensing of Unresolvable Populations
abstract: Decisions about dense populations depend on how much will cross a boundary by a deadline and when the first member arrives. Conventional radar forms a range-Doppler map, whose cells add noise and whose detections merge unresolved members. We introduce over-the-scene computation, where illumination makes the scene compute such functionals without resolving members. With random echo phases, a correlator's mean output energy sums member reflectivities weighted by a kernel set by the waveform and template. The waveform's ambiguity function is this computation's transfer function, determining computable functionals and their noise cost. One readout aggregates members over a small delay-Doppler area but along a line segment growing with duration, longest for the chirp of matching slope among constant-envelope waveforms. Members predicted to share a range lie on such a line, so a chirp's mean beat spectrum is the predicted range profile at a look-ahead horizon set by its rate. For unbiased estimation, a Cramer-Rao bound over all equal-energy waveforms favors resolving members above unit signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and grouping weaker ones into unit-SNR sets. At 0.65 members per cell, -10 dB member SNR, and one sweep, the chirp's bin sum inside the boundary comes within 16% of this bound in root-mean-square error and, with 77 times fewer samples per horizon, outperforms every unbiased estimator from a coherent processing interval of equal dwell, bandwidth, and energy. No finite set of waveform-template probes determines an unconstrained Rayleigh-fluctuating population's first arrival, but bisection localizes it if first arrivals outweigh later arrivals' sidelobes.

title: Richardson dispersion and anomalous dissipation for the random velocity model with controlled sweeping
abstract: The present paper establishes the Richardson dispersion law, predicting the particle separation with time according to $\E R_t^2 \sim t^3$, as well as anomalous dissipation for the associated tracer, for a random Hölder continuous velocity vectorfield with controlled sweeping.

title: Random complex cross ratios
abstract: We study the cross ratio of four independent points chosen uniformly on the Riemann sphere. A positive integral over a two-dimensional simplex gives its normalized planar density. We then evaluate this integral in terms of the Bloch--Wigner dilogarithm, providing a closed formula. We describe its symmetries, real-axis values, moment bounds and geometric interpretations. We use these to evaluate the mean ideal-tetrahedron volume directly from the density, recovering $π/6$, a recent theorem of Kabluchko and Schange. We then prove that the expected distance between two independently sampled hyperbolic geodesics in $\mathbb{H}^3$ is $4/3$, by evaluating the logarithmic potential of the cross-ratio distribution on the negative real axis. Further applications give the joint dihedral-angle density and an exact acute-tetrahedron probability, and a branched-cover probability law on the modular surface with exponentially small cusp tails.

title: Determination of the Lamé parameters and density at a fixed frequency
abstract: We establish global uniqueness for the inverse boundary value problem of three-dimensional time-harmonic isotropic elasticity with smooth real Lamé parameters satisfying strong convexity and a smooth positive mass density. At a fixed known nonzero frequency for which the corresponding Dirichlet problems are uniquely solvable, the full displacement-to-traction map uniquely determines all three coefficients. The proof first recovers the full boundary Taylor expansions of $λ$, $μ$, and $ρ$, and derives an exact Green--Betti identity for a four-component reduction, with the terms involving $W=ω^2ρ$ and $\nabla W$ retained. Three independent physical polarizations of the rank-three characteristic quotient yield a complete $3\times3$ matrix of polynomial moment identities. A Cauchy transform construction produces an exact relative transport matrix $H$, normalized to $I_3$ in a common exterior region. Its invertibility follows from the determinant identity $\det H=\sqrt{μ_2/μ_1}>0$. Holomorphic dependence on the projective null direction, established by differentiating the transport equation at a fixed physical point, leads to a finite-type rigidity system that determines the Lamé parameters. Finally, products of physical elastic solutions and Fourier uniqueness recover the mass density.

title: H^{s,p} estimates for weak solutions of fractional nonlocal equations in divergence form
abstract: This paper establishes interior $H^{s,p}$ regularity for weak solutions to fractional nonlocal equations in divergence form with general kernels. Under the $(δ, R)$-vanishing condition on the coefficients, we prove that for $p>2$, if the source term $f\in L^p_{loc}$, then the solution $u\in H^{s,p}_{loc}$. In contrast to Byun and Kim \cite{BK2025}, our result holds in the borderline case for $f$ without requiring differentiability assumptions. Our approach simplifies previous methods by using the stability properties of the fractional gradient to derive the good-inequality directly, thereby avoiding reliance on maximal functions. The proof integrates Vitali's covering lemma, Hardy-Littlewood maximal theory, self-improving estimates, and compactness arguments. This work extends classical $W^{1,p}$ regularity to fractional nonlocal settings under minimal kernel assumptions.

title: Generalized Chromatic Polynomials of Cycles and uni-cyclic Graphs
abstract: In \cite{R81}, Read obtained an explicit formula for the generalized chromatic polynomials of cycle graphs using the classical deletion-contraction principle. In this paper, we take a linear-algebraic approach and present a new proof of Read's formula by realizing the generalized chromatic polynomials of cycle graphs as traces of certain linear operators. As an application of this approach, we also derive explicit formulas for the generalized chromatic polynomials of uni-cyclic graphs.

title: Sequential Certification of Partially Identified Product Targets: Information Limits and Adaptive Sampling
abstract: We study the cost of certifying a scalar target driven by a product of centered Bernoulli means when an unobserved terminal gate leaves irreducible uncertainty. Each factor can be queried independently at a price. We derive the exact identified interval and determine when a requested accuracy is feasible. At every fixed strictly feasible interior instance, the optimal high-confidence expected cost is $(1+o(1))\log(1/δ)/D^*$, where $D^*$ is an answer-and-allocation information game; a globally honest procedure attains this benchmark. At product cancellation, we solve the game through a one-dimensional inverse-KL equation and explicit cost weights. For two tickets, quartic projections and rational bounds give checkable global optimality gaps. Joint confidence--precision limits expose a failure of the analyzed fixed pilot: it can cost asymptotically at least twice the optimum. A charged, precision-aware pilot with checkpoint certification restores optimal expected cost in exact arithmetic when $\log\{e+\log(1/g)\}=o(\log(1/δ))$ for effective precision $g$, including exponential and certain double-exponential precision scales. Pooled rescue preserves validity and cannot increase observation cost on coupled paths. Implemented auditors verify returns by rational inequalities; reproducible experiments show both savings and finite-confidence overhead. These guarantees concern the specified independent-reference model and its scalar target.

title: Arithmetic Kac Theory for Ramified Species
abstract:
Let $K=k((t))$, where $k$ is algebraically closed of characteristic zero, and let $Λ$ be an acyclic ramified species over $K$. An indecomposable $Λ$-module can split after extending $K$. The number of its distinct geometric indecomposable summands is the degree of its residue endomorphism field $\operatorname{End}_Λ(M)/\operatorname{rad}\operatorname{End}_Λ(M)$. We use the positive roots and cyclic automorphism of the unfolded quiver to determine the number of isomorphism classes at every nonzero rank and residue degree $e\ge1$: it is zero, an explicitly computable finite number, or $|K|$. For every invariant imaginary root of the unfolding, including at nonprimitive ranks, we construct a smooth invariant family of absolutely indecomposable representations whose rational quotient by the change-of-bases group has dimension $1-q_d(β)$. We characterize ranks admitting absolutely Schur representations by the Schur roots of the unfolded quiver.
  For the associated species over finite fields, we realize the polynomials counting absolutely indecomposable representations as graded traces of the unfolding automorphism on preprojective BPS cohomology. Galois-orbit formulas and Möbius inversion then recover the counts at each residue degree. Finally, we prove an all-rank symmetrizable analogue of Kac's constant-term conjecture: the constant term of the polynomial counting all indecomposables, rather than only absolutely indecomposable ones, equals the corresponding Kac--Moody root multiplicity. This constant is independent of the symmetrizer and modulation.

title: On the Connected Components of Structure Graphs of Associative Rings
abstract: The article studies the notion of the structure graph of an associative ring with unity. It is known that the structural graph of a ring with $n$ elements has at least $n$ connected components. The article investigates when this lower bound is attained. A hypothesis is stated that the only rings of order $n$ having exactly $n$ connected components are the rings $\mathbb{Z}_2$, $\mathbb{Z}_3$, $\mathbb{Z}_7$, $GF(4)$, and their direct sums. The hypothesis is proved for all rings except residue rings modulo a prime of the form $7+12k$, $k\geq181$, and Galois fields of characteristic~2 with extension degree $\geq17$.

title: Multivariable Congruence Jumping: Periodic States, Integral Realizations, and Descent
abstract: Congruence jumping replaces coordinates by integer quotients and updates polynomial divisibility relations. We extend this procedure to several variables and retain integer coefficients by recording their common factor separately. For three-variable systems of divisibilities with signed binomial numerators, we classify all positive integer exponent tuples of period at most two under three successive coordinate jumps: seven fixed tuples and twenty-two cycles of exact period two. No odd period greater than one occurs. At the chosen representatives of the twenty-two exponent two-cycles, there are eighty-four returning sign assignments. All have realizations with nonzero pairwise-coprime integer coordinates, and exactly seventy-four have such realizations with every coordinate positive throughout the six jumps. Explicit constructions and congruence arguments establish this classification. We also study jumps that decrease a specified height, distinguishing points that admit no immediate decrease from minima of entire connected components of the jump graph. For the four-variable family $Q_λ(x,y,z,w)=kxyzw$, where $Q_λ$ is the sum of the four squares plus $λ$ times the six pairwise products, finite bounds give complete classifications for $λ=1,2,3$. For $λ=1$, positive integer solutions exist exactly for $k=2,8,10$. These results distinguish returns of the polynomial data from integrality and positivity of the coordinate sequences.

title: A characterization of purely atomic von Neumann algebras
abstract: Let $M$ be a semifinite von Neumann algebra with a faithful normal semifinite trace $τ$, and let $Φ$ be an Orlicz function. We prove that the noncommutative Orlicz space $L^Φ(M,τ)$ is contained in $M$ if and only if $M$ is purely atomic and there is $δ>0$ such that $τ(e)\geqδ$ for every nonzero projection $e\in M$. We also prove that every left $M$-module map on $L^Φ(M,τ)$ is bounded. As a consequence, a left ideal of $M$ contained in $L^Φ(M,τ)$ and dense in it admits an $M$-invariant algebraic complement if and only if it is equal to $L^Φ(M,τ)$. These results extend a theorem of Fidaleo and Zsidó from $L^2$ to all noncommutative Orlicz spaces.

title: Multiplicity via symmetry for the Minkowski mean curvature equation: Dirichlet and Neumann problems
abstract: We consider the Minkowski mean curvature equation $$ -\operatorname{div}\left(\frac{\nabla u}{\sqrt{1-|\nabla u|^2}}\right) =λu+μh(x,u) \quad \text{in } Ω, \quad \mathcal B u = 0 \quad \text{on } \partial Ω, $$ where $\mathcal B \in \{ \mathcal D, \mathcal N \}$ is a Dirichlet or Neumann boundary condition and $Ω$ is a smooth bounded domain, required to be convex in the Neumann case. Moreover, $λ, μ\geq0$ are parameters, and $h(x,u)$ is odd with respect to $u$ and positive for $u > 0$. Using minmax methods in nonsmooth critical point theory, we prove that $λ>λ^\mathcal B_k$ yields at least $k$ pairs of nontrivial solutions with negative energy for every $μ\geq0$, where $λ_k^\mathcal B$ are the corresponding Laplacian eigenvalues, indexed by $λ^\mathcal B_0=0$. Moreover, if $H(x,u):=\int_0^u h(x,t)\,dt=o(u^2)$ as $u\to0$, we prove that for $λ\in[λ^\mathcal B_k,λ^\mathcal B_{k+1})$ and every $j\geq\max\{1,k\}$, sufficiently large $μ$ yields at least $2j-k$ distinct pairs of solutions: $j$ with negative energy and $j-k$ with positive energy.

title: Clique partitions and distinct color sets in list colorings
Uniqueness of Extremizers and Convergence of the Euler-Lagrange Iteration for the Critical Hardy-Littlewood-Sobolev Inequality
abstract: Let $n \ge 3$, $2 \le α< n$, and $1 < p,r < \infty$ satisfy $p^{-1}+r^{-1}=1+α/n$. We prove uniqueness, up to common translations and dilations, of the normalized nonnegative extremizing pairs for the corresponding Hardy-Littlewood-Sobolev inequality. More generally, all positive finite-energy solutions of the Euler-Lagrange system belong to a single symmetry orbit. The proof compares two solutions at different relative scales. Total positivity of order two identifies the second eigenspace of an associated compact self-adjoint operator and forces each nonzero difference to change sign exactly once. The opposite orientations obtained at the two ends of the scale parameter then yield uniqueness. The same method proves radial nondegeneracy modulo dilation. We also establish strong convergence of the normalized alternating Euler-Lagrange iteration from every nonnegative, radially nonincreasing initial datum to a fixed extremizing pair, without rescaling the iterates. Square-root mass variables reduce the exclusion of several concentration profiles to a static spectral estimate and an energy-increment argument. The analysis includes sublinear exponents and the logarithmic borderline decay regimes.

title: Minimal surfaces with density two at infinity
abstract: We prove that a connected, properly embedded minimal surface without boundary in $\mathbb{R}^3$ and with density two at infinity is a catenoid or a singly periodic Scherk surface.

title: NOMA Assisted Coordinated Beam Hopping for VLEO Satellite Communication Systems
abstract: This paper investigates a non-orthogonal multiple access assisted coordinated beam hopping (NOMA-CBH) scheme in multidimensional very low Earth orbit (VLEO) satellite communication systems, where multiple satellites employ CBH and coordinated beams jointly serve ground users and a dedicated ground station (GS). To characterize the VLEO-specific propagation environment, we develop a channel model that incorporates atmospheric attenuation, Doppler effects, and pointing perturbations. Building upon this architecture and channel model, a low-complexity decoupled (LCD) algorithm is designed to optimize beam scheduling and power allocation. We further derive closed-form outage probability expressions for the ground users and the GS, perform asymptotic analysis to characterize their diversity orders, and evaluate the delay-limited throughput. Simulation results demonstrate that: i) The NOMA-CBH with LCD algorithm achieves an enhanced system sum rate relative to orthogonal multiple access with coordinated beam hopping (OMA-CBH); ii) Across the considered heterogeneous traffic-demand operating points, the NOMA-CBH scheme achieves higher aggregate delivered traffic than the benchmark schemes; and iii) The outage performance of NOMA-CBH is better than that of OMA-CBH.

title: Non-Isothermal Plane Couette Flow for the Boltzmann Equation in Three Dimensions
abstract: We study the Boltzmann equation for a non-isothermal plane Couette flow in the three-dimensional channel $\mathbb T_x\times(-1,1)_y\times\mathbb T_z$ for Maxwell molecules. For sufficiently small shear rate and wall temperature perturbations, we construct a unique steady solution near the global Maxwellian. For the corresponding unsteady boundary value problem, we establish the global existence and uniqueness of solutions arising from small perturbations of the steady state, together with their exponential convergence to the steady state as $t\to\infty$. A major difficulty in both the steady and unsteady problems is to close the outgoing mass fluxes generated by diffuse reflection. To overcome this difficulty, we develop a new boundary flux transmission framework which, in the slab geometry, yields steady and time-dependent wall flux estimates through the boundary-to-boundary transmission between the two walls. We further extend this framework to damped transport equations with diffuse reflection in general bounded $C^1$ domains, even when the damping coefficient degenerates at large velocities.

title: Between Hi-Fi and MMI: the overlap of redundancy and synergy in partial information decomposition
abstract: Partial information decomposition (PID) splits the information that two sources carry about a target into redundant, unique and synergistic parts, with nonnegative decompositions lying on a segment where redundancy measures are bounded by the positive part of the co-information and the smaller source-target information. We parameterize this segment by the overlap, the common excess of redundancy and synergy over their net balance, and show that for many of the named PID measures, their redundancy can be written as the largest positive part of the co-information over a set of reference distributions. This common form induces an ordering of those PIDs on the segment. With the smallest redundancy and synergy and the largest unique atoms of any nonnegative PID, the information-theoretic version of Hi-Fi, a feature-importance method, is the zero-overlap end of the segment for two sources, with the maximum overlap bound given by the minimum mutual information (MMI) PID. We introduce, by splitting the co-information into a pairwise maximum- entropy part and the third-order connected information, a PID that sits at zero overlap except when pairwise redundancy and triadic synergy coexist. For three or more sources the bivariate results hold on every pair of merged source groups, and among all nonnegative solutions of the lattice equations MMI and Hi-Fi still give the smallest and largest unique atoms but zero overlap on all pairs at once is often unattainable. Two inequalities across pairs are necessary in general and sufficient for three sources. For identity targets zero overlap is possible exactly when the sources' information diagram is nonnegative. In random three- and four-source distributions zero overlap on all pairs fails in 21-100% of the cases.

title: Adaptive pairwise preference elicitation for decision support: identifying the best alternative with fewer judgments
abstract: Interactive decision support systems often require repeated preference judgments, although identifying the best alternative may not justify eliciting all \(n(n-1)/2\) pairwise comparisons. We propose ALEC (Adaptive Lexicographic Elicitation of Comparisons), which re-ranks the alternatives after each judgment and asks the first unobserved pair in the lexicographic order of the current ranking, using the Analytic Hierarchy Process as the concrete setting. Under a log-normal error model, directly comparing a contrast maximises the one-step reduction in its effective resistance. Posterior bounds on the probability of a wrong choice or of exceeding a relative-loss tolerance provide stopping rules valid under adaptive questioning, while a consistency-and-margin condition gives a deterministic certificate of agreement with the full-matrix winner. Simulations show that re-ranking is most useful in larger problems with limited budgets; ALEC outperforms Harker's original rule in most scenarios with \(n\ge11\), while under a common stopping rule it achieves higher hit-rate point estimates than the stronger Harker-log variant at a modest additional questioning cost. With a 5\% loss tolerance and a cap of \(2n\) additional comparisons, the stopping rule saves \res{prot-s06-saveadd-min}--\res{prot-s06-saveadd-max}\% of them, while among runs stopped by the bound the observed rate of losses above tolerance remains at most \res{s06-errearly-max}\%, against a nominal 10\%. ALEC therefore provides an adaptive elicitation module for decision support systems that balances decision precision against user effort.

title: The Short Pulse equation on the half lines: a Riemann--Hilbert approach
abstract: In this work, we analyze the initial boundary value (IBV) problems for the Short Pulse (SP) equation $u_{xt}=u+\frac{1}{6}(u^3)_{xx}$ (classical solutions) on the half-lines $x\ge 0$ and $x\le 0$ under the condition of sufficient decay as $x\to +\infty$ or as $x\to -\infty$. Using the Riemann--Hilbert (RH) problem approach, we show that these two IBV problems differ substantially regarding the boundary values required for problems to be well-posed. Namely, the solution of the ``right problem'' ($x\ge 0$) is uniquely determined by the initial data $u(x,0)$, $x\ge 0$ alone, whereas for the ``left problem'' ($x\le 0$), two boundary functions $u(0,t)$ and $u_x(0,t)$ have to be prescribed, together with the initial data, for a well-posed problem.

title: Idiosynchromatic Poetry
abstract: We prove equivalences of asymmetric partition relations involving natural numbers and products of weakly compact cardinals $κ$, infinite cardinals $λ<κ$ and natural numbers to certain classes of finitary problems in the theory of edge-coloured digraphs. We are able to determine three classes of Ramsey numbers exactly, typical examples in these classes are $r(ω^2 2, 3)$, $r(κλ2, 3)$ and $r(κλ3, 3)$. We moreover provide general upper bounds for $r(ω^2 m, 3)$ and $r(κλm, n)$.

title: Sharp moderate deviations and uniform Berry--Esseen bounds for Hotelling's $T^2$-statistic via Stein's method
abstract:
Let $\mathbf X_1,\ldots,\mathbf X_n$ be independent random vectors in $\mathbb R^d$ with common mean $\boldsymbolμ_n$, where $d\ge2$ is a fixed integer. Let $\bar{\mathbf X}_n=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf X_i$ denote the sample mean and let \[ \widehatΣ_n=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n (\mathbf X_i-\bar{\mathbf X}_n) (\mathbf X_i-\bar{\mathbf X}_n)^\top \] denote the sample covariance matrix. Assume that the average covariance matrix is positive definite and that $\widehatΣ_n$ is nonsingular almost surely. For testing $H_0:\boldsymbolμ_n=\boldsymbolμ_0$, the Hotelling statistic is \[ T^2_{H,n} =n(\bar{\mathbf X}_n-\boldsymbolμ_0)^\top \widehatΣ_n^{-1} (\bar{\mathbf X}_n-\boldsymbolμ_0). \] Under $H_0$, we establish finite-sample Cramér-type moderate deviation results and uniform Berry--Esseen bounds under finite $p$th moments for $2<p\le3$. The moderate deviation error order is optimal over independent triangular arrays, as shown by explicit constructions. For identically distributed observations with a fixed distribution, we obtain \[ \sup_{0\le x\le b_n} \left| \frac{\mathbb P(T^2_{H,n}\ge x^2)} {\mathbb P(χ_d^2\ge x^2)}-1 \right| =
O\!\left((1+b_n)^p n^{-(p-2)/2}\right) \] for every nonnegative sequence $b_n=o(n^{(p-2)/(2p)})$. The uniform Berry--Esseen bound is $O(n^{-(p-2)/2})$. The proof uses a radial Stein identity and a recursive error estimate. We apply the results to chi-squared calibration in simultaneous testing.

title: The universal property of the decomposition space of quasisymmetric functions
abstract: Aguiar, Bergeron, and Sottile showed that the coalgebra of quasisymmetric functions is terminal among connected graded coalgebras with a zeta function. After developing the notions of gradings and zeta functions for decomposition spaces, we establish an objective homotopic version of this result. Namely, the decomposition space $Q$ of quasisymmetric functions is terminal: for any conservatively graded decomposition space $X$ with zeta function $F$, there is a unique graded ikeo-culf span $X \leftarrow W \rightarrow Q$ inducing $F$ from the special zeta function on $Q$. More generally, for gradings in any complete decomposition space $M$ with indecomposable identities, the terminal object is $J(M)$, the free decomposition space on the nondegenerate simplices of $M$; the quasisymmetric case is $Q=J(B\mathbb{N})$.

title: Few-Weight Linear Sets and Divisibility of Rank-Metric Codes
abstract:
We study $\mathbb F_q$-linear sets whose positive point weights belong to a prescribed finite set $A$. The integer $e=\gcd(A)$ always divides the rank of the defining subspace, but the divisibility does not by itself imply linearity over $\mathbb F_{q^e}$. We show that it does in a broad parameter range. Let $L_U$ be an $\mathbb F_q$-linear set of rank $N$ spanning $PG(h-1,q^m)$, $h\ge2$, without being equal to it, and assume that $q\ge m$ and that the minimum weight of its points is $a\ge2$. Combining the theorem of Csajbók, Marino and Pepe on the maximum field of linearity with the lower bound of Adriaensen and Santonastaso for the size of a linear set containing a point of weight one, we prove that $L_U$ is also defined by an $\mathbb F_{q^t}$-subspace, for some divisor $t$ of $m$, whose $\mathbb F_q$-dimension is exactly $N+t-a$. Under a natural gap condition excluding divisors of $m$ in the interval $(e,N-e]$, this forces $a=e$ and the defining subspace to be $\mathbb F_{q^e}$-linear.
  Through geometric duality, the point weights of the dual of a system are the deficiencies $m-w$ of the rank weights $w$ of the associated code. For rank-metric codes in which the subcode generated by the codewords of nonmaximum rank contains codewords of maximum rank, we show that deleting suitable coordinates yields the $\mathbb F_q$-expansion of a code over $\mathbb F_{q^t}$. We show that the codes in which the codewords of nonmaximum rank generate a subcode without codewords of maximum rank are exactly the direct sums of a simplex code and a code of length smaller than $m$. We derive field-reduction results for two-weight and three-weight rank-metric codes, and show that no gap condition is needed when $m$ divides the length or when the code has only two nonzero weights. Finally, we study two-dimensional codes of length at most $m$ and provide families of three-weight examples.

title: Recovering the Length of a Path from its Signature
abstract: We prove the length conjecture of J. Chang, T. Lyons and H. Ni for paths of bounded variation for arbitrary real Banach spaces and any reasonable tensor (algebra) norms. More precisely, we establish the missing lower bound and in this way show that the length of a tree-reduced path is recovered from the asymptotic behaviour of its normalised signature. The main technical argument uses the norm duality and shuffle algebra to express natural powers of polygonal length approximations as combinations of linear functionals acting on restricted signatures, which are then glued by suitable integrations into a linear functional of controlled growth acting on the full signature. In particular, the full proof combines tools of classical analysis and functional analysis, such as localisation by continuous cutoff functions, Stone-Weierstrass approximation of continuous functions by signature polynomials, the Hahn-Banach theorem and a support detection lemma for compactly supported real signed Borel measures.

title: $p$-parity conjecture for Panchishkin Galois representations
abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime, and let $V_1$ and $V_2$ be symplectic self-dual $p$-adic de Rham representations of $G_{\mathbb{Q}}$ that are pure (of weight $-1$) and satisfy the Panchishkin condition at $p$. Suppose that $V_1$ and $V_2$ are residually isomorphic, compatibly with their Panchishkin filtrations. We prove the relative $p$-parity conjecture relating the ratio of the global root numbers of $V_1$ and $V_2$ to the difference of their Bloch-Kato Selmer dimensions. We have no restriction on the dimension of the Galois representation, the Hodge-Tate weights or the monodromy operator at $p$, and the residual isomorphism need not be symplectic. The proof expresses ratios of local root numbers in terms of local invariants over the cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extension: a new invariant introduced at $p$, and local Iwasawa $λ$-invariants at $\ell\neq p$. Both are compatible with the arithmetic local constants of Mazur-Rubin and Nekovář. A key input, proved using Sen theory, is that the Bloch-Kato and strict local conditions at $p$ coincide over the cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extension, generalising results of Coates-Greenberg and Nekovář. As applications, we obtain new cases of the $p$-parity conjecture, including cases of rank greater than two: Artin twists of CM Hida families, orthogonal Artin twists of ordinary modular forms, symmetric cubes along Hida families, and families of abelian surfaces, together with unconditional numerical examples.

title: Hardness of integer linear feasibility with cyclic support
abstract: We prove that integer linear feasibility is strongly $NP$-complete even when the constraint matrix has exactly two nonzero entries in every row and column, with its support forming a single cycle. This holds already for monotone systems (one positive and one negative coefficient in each inequality) with nonzero coefficients of absolute value $2$ or $3$ and right-hand sides in $\{-1,0,1,2\}$. No variable bounds are supplied separately from the system. For systems in which each inequality involves at most two variables, this strengthens known hardness results by restricting all numerical data to fixed finite sets. For systems in which each variable occurs in at most two inequalities, this establishes, to the best of our knowledge, the first $NP$-hardness result for feasibility. We also give negative answers, unless $P=NP$, to questions on polynomial-time solvability of integer programs with bounded coefficients and bounded totally $Δ$-modular treewidth, and on fixed-parameter tractability of integer bound propagation with respect to coefficient and right-hand-side magnitudes.

title: A Proximal Newton Framework with Local Superlinear Convergence for Simple Bilevel Optimization
abstract: In this paper, we study a penalty method for simple bilevel optimization in which the lower-level objective has a convex composite structure. Our approach is based on a vanishing-penalty reformulation, which gives rise to a sequence of penalized problems as the penalty parameter decreases. A key difficulty is that metric subregularity of the lower-level optimality mapping does not, in general, yield a uniform error bound for the penalized problems as the penalty parameter vanishes, preventing a direct application of standard proximal Newton theory. To address this difficulty, we first analyze a regularized proximal Newton step by exploiting the specific structure of simple bilevel problems, and establish the local estimates that underpin superlinear convergence. Building on this local analysis, we propose SiB-Newton, which incorporates the proximal Newton step into a globalization strategy. We establish convergence guarantees for SiB-Newton and show that, under suitable local conditions, Newton steps are eventually accepted and the iterates converge at a superlinear rate. Numerical experiments on synthetic examples verify the predicted local superlinear convergence rate.

title: Some polynomial spaces are Euclidean balls
abstract: In this paper, we establish a matrix criterion for a space to be homeomorphic to a closed Euclidean ball. As applications, we prove that the normalized space of $K$-Lorentzian polynomials on an arbitrary open convex cone $K$ is homeomorphic to a closed Euclidean ball, giving an affirmative answer to Brändén and Leake's question, and we also settle Brändén's conjecture that the normalized space of homogeneous multiaffine real stable polynomials is homeomorphic to a closed Euclidean ball. In addition, our results show that the normalized space of homogeneous $K$-stable polynomials of degree $d$ is homeomorphic to a closed Euclidean ball.

title: A characteristic mapping method for dissipative evolution equations
abstract: The Characteristic Mapping (CM) method is a transport scheme which discretizes the Lagrangian flow map as a composition of spatial interpolants. This adaptive approximation technique has demonstrated novel resolution properties and the ability to efficiently simulate the fine scales of inviscid turbulent flows. In this work, we construct an extension of this approach to the solution of dissipative problems, including the Navier-Stokes equations. The extension lifts a general scalar evolution equation to a path in a group of diffeomorphisms, where the semigroup approach of the CM method can be exploited. We give an interpretation of this lift through the geometric framework of optimal transport. We then introduce a semidirect product evolution technique to perform the time stepping of the map components. The map is evolved based on the semi-Lagrangian CM approach, and its log-Jacobian is evolved explicitly by an exponential integrator. The numerical scheme is demonstrated to be high-order accurate and is tested on a range of canonical nonlinear dissipative equations. By retaining the resolution properties of the CM method, the approach shows a promising ability to simulate turbulent fluid flows across all Reynolds numbers.

title: Shifted Lagrangian geometry of curves in Radko surfaces
abstract: We describe the shifted Lagrangian geometry of curves in Radko surfaces, through their global integrations and their homotopy Poisson algebras. We construct the adjoint symplectic groupoid of the surface explicitly, show that admissible curves integrate to embedded Lagrangian subgroupoids, which are 1-shifted Lagrangians, and characterize when their shifted intersections are clean. For a component of the degeneracy locus, a canonical Hamiltonian flow on its shifted self-intersection recovers the modular period. On the infinitesimal side, the homotopy Poisson algebra of a connected admissible curve not contained in the degeneracy locus is $L_\infty$-isomorphic to its underlying cochain complex, and its $L_\infty$-isomorphism class is determined by the total contact multiplicity. The brackets of arity at least two can be removed by a change of tubular neighbourhood exactly when all contacts are transverse. At tangential contacts, the binary bracket retains the modular vector field. We establish this distinction using a general characterization of the $L_\infty$-isomorphisms induced by changes of tubular neighbourhood, valid for arbitrary coisotropic submanifolds.

title: The isoperimetric problem in the Riemannian Heisenberg $3$-space
abstract: We prove that every closed weakly stable constant mean curvature surface immersed in the Riemannian Heisenberg space ${\rm Nil}_3$ is an embedded rotational sphere. As a consequence, we solve the isoperimetric problem in ${\rm Nil}_3$: the isoperimetric domains of ${\rm Nil}_3$ are exactly the regions enclosed by rotational constant mean curvature spheres, and for each prescribed volume there is a unique such domain, up to ambient isometry. For small volumes, the isoperimetric result was proved by Tomter in 1993.

title: Gradient higher integrability for a general class of degenerate parabolic double phase systems
abstract: We establish quantitative local higher integrability estimates for weak solutions of degenerate parabolic systems with generalized double phase growth, whose prototype is $$u_t-\operatorname{div}\left(\frac{G'(|Du|)}{|Du|}Du+a(x,t)\frac{H'(|Du|)}{|Du|}Du\right)=0\qquad\text{in }Ω_T.$$ Here $G$ and $H$ are Young functions satisfying suitable structural assumptions. The nonnegative coefficient $a$ is allowed to vanish and has a concave modulus of continuity $ω$ with respect to the parabolic distance. For $Ψ(z,\varkappa)=G(\varkappa)+a(z)H(\varkappa)$, we prove that solutions in $L^\infty(0,T;L^s(Ω,\mathbb{R}^N))$, $2\le s<\infty$, satisfy $Ψ(\cdot,|Du|)\in L^{1+\varepsilon}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ for some $\varepsilon>0$, provided $$\limsup_{ρ\to 0+}ω(ρ)\frac{H(ρ^{-\frac{n+s}{s}})}{G(ρ^{-\frac{n+s}{s}})}<\infty.$$ For bounded solutions, the corresponding condition involves $H(ρ^{-1})/G(ρ^{-1})$. These conditions extend the known interpolative gap bounds from power growth to general growth functions and continuity moduli. In particular, for $G(\varkappa)=\varkappa^p$, $H(\varkappa)=\varkappa^q$, and $ω(ρ)\simeqρ^α$, they recover $q\le p+sα/(n+s)$ and $q\le p+α$, respectively. The proof combines an intrinsic stopping-time argument with inverse-function estimates to derive Poincaré and reverse Hölder inequalities adapted to the general growth phases.

title: The probabilistic bound for perfect hashing is sharp only for binary alphabets
abstract: We investigate the optimal asymptotic rate $R_q$ of perfect $q$-hash codes, a fundamental extremal problem in combinatorics, information theory, and computer science. Let $B_q=-\log_2(1-q!/q^q)/(q-1)$ denote the classical probabilistic lower bound. We prove that $R_q=B_q$ if and only if $q=2$, establishing an explicit strict improvement for every $q\ge3$ and settling the first assertion of a conjecture of Xing and Yuan (Combinatorica 43 (2023), 347--366). More significantly, we show that, for every $η>0$, $R_q\ge B_q+\exp(-(2+η)q)$ for all sufficiently large integers $q$. This improves the previously known increments of scale $\exp(-3q+O(\ln q))$ by an exponential factor. We also establish a structural limitation of the concatenation method. For pairwise uniform inner codes of subexponential length, the resulting rate bound exceeds $B_q$ by at most $\exp(-3q+o(q))$. Thus, exponentially long inner codes are necessary to achieve the new improvement scale within this framework. Our proofs combine Fourier analysis, high-dimensional simplex codes, additive permutation counts, and entropy bounds for hypergraph matchings. We further strengthen lower bounds from short inner codes and improve several known numerical estimates.

title: Non-standard behaviour of semibounded forms and their representations
abstract: A number of results is presented concerning the extreme behaviour of products of linear operators or relations from one Hilbert space ${\mathfrak H}$ to another Hilbert space ${\mathfrak K}$. It is shown that there exists a relation $T$ from ${\mathfrak H}$ to ${\mathfrak K}$ such that the closure of the nonnegative relation $T^*T$ in ${\mathfrak H}$ is not equal to the nonnegative selfadjoint relation $T^*T^{**}$; moreover, this may happen for a singular but also for a regular (i.e., closable) relation $T$. In fact, as an extreme situation the paper contains a construction of a densely defined closable operator $T$, such that ${\rm dom\,}T^*T=\{0\}$, while $T^*T^{**}$ is a densely defined selfadjoint operator. Likewise it is shown that there exist a linear relation $T$ from ${\mathfrak H}$ to ${\mathfrak K}$ and a nonnegative everywhere defined contraction $R$ in ${\mathfrak K}$ for which the product $RT$ is singular and the product $R^{1/2} T$ is regular. Such results illustrate situations that can arise in the Lebesgue type decomposition of linear relations and the Lebesgue type decomposition of semibounded forms.

title: Classification of cohomogeneity one steady gradient Ricci solitons in dimension four and five
abstract: In this paper, we first prove Appleton's conjecuture on the uniqueness of noncollapsed steady solitons constructed in \cite{Appleton}. We also classify non-Ricci-flat $κ$-noncollapsed cohomogeneity one steady gradient Ricci solitons in dimension four and five. After passing to a finite cover, in dimension four, they must be the Bryant soliton or Appleton's noncollapsed 4d steady soliton; in dimension five, they must be the Bryant soliton or solitons constructed by Ivey--Dancer--Wang.

title: Common zeros of homogeneous polynomials and the weight hierarchy of projective Reed-Muller codes
abstract: We determine the maximum number of common zeros in projective space of any set of linearly independent homogeneous polynomials of the same degree, when the degree is smaller than the cardinality of the finite field. This proves the conjecture of Beelen, Datta and Ghorpade and determines the complete weight hierarchy of the corresponding projective Reed-Muller codes. The proof uses Green's hyperplane restriction bound, combined with a footprint argument that reduces the problem to the affine case solved by Heijnen and Pellikaan. Wei duality then determines the hierarchy in sufficiently large degrees, recovering the complete hierarchy in every degree for the projective plane.
