Finally, we prove an upper bound valid in every degree, and conjecture that it is always sharp.

title: A diameter-one set in $\mathbb{R}^5$ that cannot be covered by six diameter-one balls
abstract: We construct a compact set of diameter $1$ in $\mathbb{R}^5$ which cannot be covered by six Euclidean balls of diameter $1$. Its convex hull is a full-dimensional convex body satisfying the same property. Moreover, a finite subset of diameter $1$ cannot be covered by six closed balls even when their radius is increased to $0.50001$. The compact set is the quadratic image of the unit sphere in the space of symmetric $3\times3$ matrices of trace zero. A hypothetical cover leads to twelve spherical ellipses covering ${\mathbb S}^2$ and arranged in six antipodal pairs. Using Euler's formula, we replace them by twelve pentagonal regions contained in the ellipses. An area estimate then gives a contradiction.

title: An interpretation of the BMO boundedness of Hörmander--Mikhlin multipliers
abstract: We prove a pointwise domination of Poisson variances for Hörmander--Mikhlin multipliers on the real line. The estimate holds in operator order for operator-valued functions and gives a direct Fourier-side proof of BMO boundedness. The same argument gives an algebraic proof of the one-dimensional Schur multiplier estimate of Conde-Alonso, González-Pérez, Parcet and Tablate ( Annals of Mathematics, 2023), formulated here using Poisson BMO. The endpoint estimates are proved for $L^2$ functions and Hilbert--Schmidt operators; interpolation gives the corresponding $L^p$ and Schatten estimates.

title: Uniform Three-Fold Product Expansion of Algebraic-Geometry Codes over a Fixed Field
abstract:
A collection of classical codes $C_1,\dots,C_m$ has product expansion if every low-weight word in the sum of their extensions to the product space can be written as a sum of words supported on few lines, each line being a codeword of the corresponding $C_i$. For $m=2$ product expansion is equivalent to robust testability of the tensor code, while for $m\ge 3$ it is strictly stronger; it is the hypothesis on the local codes behind recent constructions of good quantum LDPC codes, good quantum locally testable codes, and quantum codes with transversal non-Clifford gates. No explicit family over a fixed field was previously known to achieve constant rate, linear distance for both the code and its dual, and 3-fold product expansion at growing length.
  We prove that for the one-point evaluation codes $C_i$ of length $N_i=728\cdot27^{\,i-1}$ and pole order $\lfloor N_i/5\rfloor$ on the Garcia--Stichtenoth tower over $\mathbb{F}_{729}$, the triple $(C_i,C_i,C_i)$ has product expansion with a constant independent of $i$. The dual codes $C_i^\perp$ then form an explicit fixed-field family of rate tending to $109/130$ and relative distance at least $8/65$. The proof is geometric: we view the words of the sum code as arrays on the product of three copies of the $i$-th curve of the tower, where the parity checks are sections of a line bundle. An exact generation theorem describes the sum-code words supported on the grid footprint of a suitable divisor. A support-localisation argument then shows that every low-weight array lies on such a divisor, after deleting a small number of coordinates. We also give a sufficient criterion for three-fold product expansion in terms of degree and genus ratios, yielding explicit families over every non-prime finite field of order at least $512$. The principal conclusions have been formally verified in Lean 4.

title: Dense Exact Factorizations of Countable Topological Groups
abstract: We prove that every countably infinite group endowed with a topology of countable weight in which every nonempty open set is infinite admits an exact factorization into two dense infinite subsets. More generally, every finite partial exact factorization with nonempty factors extends to an exact factorization of the whole group in which both factors meet every member of a prescribed at most countable family of infinite subsets in infinitely many points. This settles the countable case of a question of Protasov and Slobodianiuk. The proof uses the finite graph Ramsey theorem, invariant finitely additive probability measures on amenable groups, and a structural lemma on quadratic coverings based on Neumann's coset covering lemma.

title: A Second-Order Semi-Implicit Projection Time-Stepping Scheme for the Shallow-Water Equations on the Sphere Using Compatible Finite Elements
abstract: We propose a second-order, semi-implicit time-stepping scheme for the shallow-water equations on the sphere discretised with compatible finite elements. The scheme splits the advection operator from the wave operator, applying a DG-upwind SSPRK3 method to the advection part and an $H(\text{div})$-conforming implicit discretisation to the wave part, solved efficiently via hybridisation. The scheme follows a three-step symmetric splitting: an explicit half-step, a full advection step, and an implicit half-step that simultaneously projects the velocity back into the $H(\text{div})$ space. This symmetry guarantees global second-order accuracy and confines the stability restriction to the CFL condition of the advection step alone. The time-step can therefore be extended beyond this limit by subcycling the advection step without additional implicit solves. The method is implemented in Firedrake and validated against a standard suite of spherical shallow-water benchmarks, demonstrating stable results for Courant numbers up to 1 (with two advection subcycles) with second-order finite elements, second-order convergence, and good parallel scaling.

title: Counting multigeodesics and the Selberg-Delange method
abstract: We study the counting function $\mathcal{P}^m(X,x)$ for $m$-multigeodesics of length at most $x$ on a compact hyperbolic surface $X$ where $m$ is a positive integer. Building on the Selberg-Delange method, originally developed for counting integers with exactly $m$ prime factors in the interval $[1,x]$, we prove a large $x$ asymptotic for $\mathcal{P}^m(X,x)$. We show that for fixed $m$ as $x\to\infty$ the asymptotic is independent of the surface, whereas for $\frac{m}{\log x}$ bounded away from zero, the asymptotic depends on an infinite Euler product over the lengths of primitive closed geodesics. We also study the distribution of the function $ω_1$, defined on multigeodesics $Γ$ as $ω_1(Γ)=k-1$ for $Γ=(γ_1,...,γ_k)$ a $k$-multigeodesic. We show that as $x\to\infty$, the distribution of $ω_1$ in the set of multigeodesics of length $\leq x$ is close to that of a Poisson random variable with parameter $\log x$. Both of these theorems rely on studying the generating function of the random variable $ω_1$ which we relate to the Selberg zeta function.

title: AI-Native Task-Oriented Semantic Communications over a Relay: Benefits and Vulnerabilities
abstract: Semantic communication (SemCom) using a relay node is considered, where the relay assists in conveying task-relevant information from a source to a destination, with meaning defined by classification labels. A joint end-to-end design of the source encoder, relay transformation, and destination decoders is developed to optimize both semantic inference accuracy and perceptual reconstruction quality for image data. Relay-assisted schemes are shown to outperform direct transmission, with gains that become more pronounced in low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) regimes across different relaying strategies. Alongside these performance benefits, however, a key security vulnerability introduced by the relay is identified, and a Byzantine attack is formulated in which the relay injects structured, learned perturbations into its transmitted signal. The attack operates on intermediate communication representations subject to channel effects, with perturbations generated through a learned mapping applied at test time. It is shown to significantly degrade semantic inference accuracy at the destination. These results reveal a clear trade-off between SemCom gains and security risks in relay-assisted systems, motivating the need for secure relay designs that account for insider threats.

title: Multifractal scaling of quantum eigenfunctions in the thermodynamic limit
abstract: We prove multifractal scaling of measures related to the eigenfunctions of Schrödinger operators with point-like bump potentials, in the thermodynamic limit, in dimension $d\geq 5$. This is consistent with a longstanding expectation in the physics literature in these dimensions. The fractal exponents are computed explicitly as a function of the parameter defining the moments. Our result requires a weak disorder condition on the location of the scatterers and a strong coupling condition on the sequence of eigenvalues.

title: On some stochastic evolutions on Laguerre-Polya functions
abstract: We prove uniqueness in law for three stochastic evolutions on normalised Laguerre-Pólya functions arising as scaling limits of matrix characteristic polynomial dynamics. In particular, this implies that Ahn's universal Brownian Gibbs line ensemble arising from random matrix products has the law of the logarithms of the reciprocal zeros of the solution, unique in law, to a simple stochastic equation on entire functions started from $\mathrm{e}^{-z}$. The method of proof relies on some integrable structure of the problem in the special form of a new duality with finite-dimensional diffusions which is closely related to intertwinings.

title: Fitness advantages, prediction of resistances and protocol design: exploiting the synergy between mathematical modelling and statistics
abstract: Tumour evolution and treatment resistance are driven by the interplay between clonal heterogeneity, selective pressures, and therapeutic interventions. In this work, we propose an integrated mathematical and statistical framework to investigate clonal selection, predict radioresistance, and optimize radiotherapy protocols. We develop a multi-clonal dynamical model incorporating proliferation, resource competition, epigenetic instability, and clone-specific radiosensitivity. Through the statistical analysis of 255,150 in silico simulations, we identify key biological determinants of treatment response and characterize the effects of evolutionary competition and radiotherapy on clonal composition. Our results show that evolutionary dynamics favour highly proliferative clones, whereas radiotherapy selects radioresistant populations and reduces tumour heterogeneity. We further investigate how tumour characteristics influence resistance trajectories and identify trade-offs between tumour control, toxicity, and resistance selection across different treatment schedules. Optimal protocols are determined for distinct patient profiles, accounting for dose, fractionation, and timing. Finally, we demonstrate how treatment history affects the efficacy of second-line therapies. Overall, our findings highlight the potential of combining mechanistic modelling and statistical inference to understand cancer evolution and support personalized radiotherapy design.

title: On Sufficient Conditions for Rank Zero in Families of Elliptic Curves
abstract: In this article, we study the Mordell Weil ranks of elliptic curves in the family $E_D:y^2=x^3+Dx$, where $D\in\mathbb{Z}\setminus\{0\}$. Under suitable congruence conditions on $D$ and its prime divisors, we use $2$-descent via a rational $2$-isogeny to study the rank of $E_D$. Under our congruence hypotheses, the ranks of these matrices give sufficient conditions for $E_D$ to have rank zero. We give explicit sufficient conditions for the curves $E_D$ to have Mordell Weil rank zero over $\mathbb{Q}$ in the following cases: (i) $D$ is an odd negative integer, (ii) $D$ is an odd positive integer, and (iii) $D$ is a positive even integer. Also we give a quantitative result describing how many square free parameters satisfy the required matrix-rank condition. In particular, our results show that these rank zero criteria hold for a significant proportion of the admissible parameters.

title: LithoSAGE: Spatially Adaptive and Geometrically Equivariant Neural Operators for Computational Lithography
abstract: Operator learning offers an efficient surrogate for lithography simulation, replacing costly numerical solutions with direct model inference. However, existing learning architectures are not designed to simultaneously provide geometric equivariance and adaptability to layout windows with different physical extents, and thus their generalization capability is limited. To address this problem, we propose LithoSAGE, a spatially adaptive and geometrically equivariant neural operator method trained on lithography data. Within its basic Fourier neural operator architecture, spectral weights are expressed as continuous functions of normalized radial frequency through a learnable sum of Gaussians. This representation preserves the geometric properties of the lithography system and incorporates rotation and translation equivariance, spatial interaction decay, and direct evaluation on different layout windows. Experiments predict aerial images from mask layouts and resist images from aerial images, demonstrating the geometric equivariance and spatial adaptivity of LithoSAGE. Comparisons with other architectures also assess prediction errors and parameter efficiency.

title: Hypocoercivity for a thermostatted Boltzmann equation
abstract: We study the Boltzmann equation for a gas on the three-dimensional torus. Its particles collide with one another and with a thermal reservoir whose temperature varies in space. The reservoir heats the gas in some regions and cools it in others, driving a nonequilibrium energy current. For the isotropic cutoff kernel, with Maxwell molecules or hard potentials, we prove global well-posedness and exponential convergence to the same stationary state for initial data with a common Gaussian upper bound and Gaussian moment bound. These bounds determine how weak self collisions must be relative to bath collisions. The estimates are uniform over bath profiles between fixed positive temperature bounds. For any nonconstant reservoir profile on the three-dimensional torus, this stationary state cannot be a local Maxwellian. When particles collide only with the bath, relative entropy to the stationary state cannot increase. Once self collisions are added, arbitrarily small perturbations can initially increase it, even though they later return exponentially.

title: Boundary-preserving randomized neural network methods for Poisson equations on general two- and three-dimensional domains
abstract: In this paper, we propose a boundary-preserving randomized neural network method for Poisson equations with Dirichlet boundary conditions in two and three dimensions. A linear lifting imposes the boundary conditions exactly, without balancing penalty weights between interior and boundary residuals. We construct the liftings by generalized barycentric coordinates and transfinite interpolation on convex and nonconvex polygons and polyhedra, and by radial parameterization on star-shaped curved domains. Numerical experiments on different domains show that the proposed method substantially reduces errors compared with the standard randomized neural network method.

title: Towards a twistless converse theorem
abstract: We prove a finiteness theorem for Dirichlet series satisfying the Euler product, analytic continuation, and functional equation expected of a holomorphic newform. For any fixed level $N$, even weight $k$, and exponent $σ$, only finitely many such series have Dirichlet coefficients $\ll n^σ$. No hypotheses on twists by Dirichlet characters are assumed. The proof combines a combinatorial spanning theorem for Ramanujan sums with an operator-theoretic argument that uses two distinct primes to establish discreteness of the possible Hecke eigenvalues.

title: Domination and maximal intersecting families in comaximal graphs of commutative rings
abstract: The comaximal graph $\mathcal{G}(R)$ of a commutative ring $R$ has as vertices the nonunits outside the Jacobson radical, two being adjacent if they generate $R$ as an ideal. For rings with $k\ge 4$ maximal ideals, only the bounds $2\leγ(\mathcal{G}(R))\le k$ were known, to our knowledge. We prove $γ=γ_t=γ_c=k$ whenever $3\le k<\infty$, without finiteness or Artinian hypotheses, classify the minimum dominating sets, and determine the domatic number. Independent dominating sets correspond to maximal intersecting families of subsets of $\{1,\dots,k\}$; we obtain a closed formula for the independent domination number of every finite non-local ring, which can be exponentially larger than the domination number. The proofs rest on the class sizes of the blow-up description of $\mathcal{G}(R)$ due to Moconja and Petrović, which we determine for every ring with finitely many maximal ideals, finite or infinite; with them, domination problems on $\mathcal{G}(R)$ become weighted extremal problems on subsets of $\{1,\dots,k\}$, and the formula for the independent domination number follows from the multiplicative form of these sizes. We also treat rings with infinitely many maximal ideals, graph polynomials, and lattices whose maximal ideals are prime.

title: Sigmoid Tensor Decomposition for Compact Representations of Binary Data
abstract: Nonlinear low-rank decompositions are receiving growing attention as a way to represent structured data with fewer parameters than conventional linear methods. Existing nonlinear approaches have focused mainly on matrices, which limits their ability to capture multidimensional structure. We propose a nonlinear tensor decomposition based on sigmoid nonlinearization in the Tucker and tensor-train formats. A binary tensor is represented by a low-rank real-valued score tensor, whose parameters are estimated by minimizing the binary cross-entropy loss. The resulting optimization problem is jointly nonconvex, but becomes convex with respect to one factor or score block when the remaining factors are fixed, as in the corresponding matrix case. We evaluate the method on several structured binary tensors and compare it with conventional Tucker and tensor-train decompositions across a range of common ranks. These results indicate that sigmoid nonlinearization is particularly effective in the low-rank regime, where it can provide more accurate binary reconstructions than conventional linear tensor decompositions at comparable model sizes.

title: Fourier inequalities and sign uncertainty II
abstract: Building on our earlier work, we present an $L^2$-$L^1$ inequality for radial Fourier eigenfunctions, relating this to the sign uncertainty principle of Bourgain, Clozel and Kahane. We also propose a generalisation of the aforementioned uncertainty principle.

title: Solving polynomials in large pseudo-finite sets
abstract: Using techniques from model theory, we prove analogues of Rado's and Sárközy's theorems on solutions to polynomial equations in dense sets of definable groups and fields equipped with well-behaved measures. As a special case, we adapt our results to pseudofinite structures, to deduce non-qualitative asymptotic results.

title: Ignoring Blow-Ups for Approximations
abstract: It is well known that for SDEs with non-Lipschitz coefficients, the Euler scheme can fail to converge in an Lp sense. It is also widely observed that convergence fails only due to rare explosive trajectories, that distort the expectation. In this work we demonstrate that almost any method of removing these rare explosive trajectories leads to convergence in a suitable strong and weak sense. We apply this framework to coefficients that grow faster than linearly at infinity and Lennard-Jones type coefficients that explode like a reciprocal power on a compact set.

title: Viscosity-variational inequality solutions of fully nonlinear second-order stationary mean field games with nonseparable and nondifferentiable Hamiltonians
abstract: We analyse stationary fully nonlinear uniformly elliptic second-order mean field games with nonseparable and nondifferentiable Hamiltonians by introducing the notion of viscosity-variational inequality solution. In this formulation of the problem, the value function is the viscosity solution of the Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman (HJB) equation, and the Kolmogorov--Fokker--Planck (KFP) equation for the player density is understood as a nonstandard variational inequality that no longer involves partial derivatives of the value function. The advantages of this formulation are found in its stability and continuity properties for handling weak convergence arguments, which we use to prove the existence of solutions of the problem. Furthermore, we prove the equivalence of the notion of viscosity-variational inequality solution with the notion of a partial differential inclusion solution, where the value function is a strong solution of the HJB equation and the player density is a very weak solution of the KFP equation with coefficients belonging to subdifferential sets of the Hamiltonian. Finally, we prove the uniqueness of solutions in the case of separable Hamiltonians with strictly monotone couplings.

title: Overholonomicity of Overconvergent $F$-isocrystals over Laurent Series Fields
abstract: We prove that $K$-valued overconvergent $F$-isocrystals over smooth $k((t))$-varieties are overholonomic and construct the triangulated category of overholonomic complexes of Frobenius type which is stable under six operations and contains overconvergent $F$-isocrsytals.

title: Torsion points in families of elliptic curves
abstract: We study the specialization of torsion points in one-parameter degenerations of elliptic curves with singular fibers of Kodaira type. We describe the resulting torsion curves, their ramifications, intersection multiplicities, and irreducible and connected components.

title: On generalized token graphs with tokens of different colors
abstract: We generalize the concept of token graphs, and we call them supertoken graphs. In this work, we consider the variant in which tokens are distinguishable (for instance, by color) and at most one token is allowed on each vertex. We formally define this kind of supertoken graphs and present their basic properties. We study their diameter, in which cases they are Cayley graphs, and their spectra. Moreover, we provide bounds or exact values for the independence, the vertex cover, the clique, and the chromatic numbers of these graphs. Finally, we characterize the cases in which the supertoken graphs of complete graphs are planar.

title: Gradient potential estimates for k-Hessian equations
abstract: For $2\le k<n$, we prove pointwise gradient bounds for proper weak $k$-convex functions in terms of a local average and a Wolff potential of the full Hessian measure $F_k[u]$. The estimate yields local Lipschitz regularity for $F_k[u]=f$ with $f\in L^{n/k,1/k}_{\mathrm{loc}}$, and for $F_k[u]=|Du|^p$ when $0<p<nk/(n-k)$. Both the Lorentz index $1/k$ and the upper bound on $p$ are sharp.

title: Drift-Resilient Predictive Interference Management: Online Adaptation of an Extreme-Value Predictor
abstract: Predictive interference management supports ultra-reliable low-latency communication (URLLC) by allocating finite-blocklength resources against a high conditional quantile of next-slot interference. Building on an extreme-value-theory/kernel-density-estimation (EVT/KDE) predictor with quantile-defined interference states, this paper makes the predictor resilient to unannounced shifts in the interference distribution. Its cumulative refitting on all past observations does not specify how the state partition and retained samples should evolve after a regime change. We show that drift first makes the quantile partition inefficient: cumulative refitting preserves tail support and coverage but cannot recover conditional resolution, and pays for it in channel use, whereas discarding history starves the tail estimator. We therefore propose event-triggered quantile-space adaptation. A nonparametric cumulative sum (CUSUM) on the predictor's level stream detects change. At each confirmed event, the quantile partition is re-derived from post-change observations, retained history is re-binned under it, and each state is refit from a bounded per-state memory, capped to balance stale-regime bias against tail-estimation variance, with a closed-form L-moment tail estimator. At a nominal coverage target $η\!=\!0.99$, relative to matched cumulative refitting with fixed states, the proposed method reduces channel use by $5.7$--$13.2\%$ and quantile pinball loss by $25$--$50\%$ across abrupt, incremental, compound, downward, and reversal drift, with coverage changing by $-0.5$ to $+1.0$ percentage points. At matched achieved coverage, it saves $4$--$18\%$ of channel uses, while resource use in load-only and stationary cases changes by less than $0.5\%$. With $K$ samples per state and $L$ states, predictor memory is bounded at $O(KL)$ rather than growing as $O(t)$.

title: The first gap for minimal submanifolds in spheres
abstract: Let $f:M^n\to\Sn^{n+q}(1)$ be a minimal immersion of a closed connected manifold with $n\ge3$ and $q\ge2$, and let $S$ be the squared length of its second fundamental form. We prove an integral inequality that gives $\max_M S\ge n$ if the immersion is not totally geodesic. If $n\ne4$ or $q=2$, equality $\max_M S=n$ holds if and only if the immersion is a Clifford minimal hypersurface; if $n=4$ and $q\ge3$, equality holds if and only if the immersion is a Clifford minimal hypersurface or the standard minimal embedding of $\mathbb{CP}^2$ in $\Sn^7(1)$. Both classifications are understood up to an ambient isometry, a totally geodesic inclusion, and a finite covering. We construct the integral inequalities using polynomial weights and divergence identities. The required algebraic estimates are proved by sums of squared tensor norms.

title: Variably saturated flow on polygonal and cut meshes using a mass-conservative hybrid virtual element
abstract: A hybrid virtual element formulation (HVEM) is presented for transient flow in variably saturated soils governed by Richards' equation. The nodal heads are the only global degrees of freedom, and a Darcy flux is assumed in each polygonal element and condensed. The flux combines a divergence-free part with a particular field of linear divergence that absorbs storage and sources, so that the water balance of every element holds identically, at every iterate and for any time step, and that of the whole domain at convergence. To guarantee rank-sufficiency with no stabilisation parameter, the divergence-free fields are harmonic polynomials ordered by their behaviour under rotation, giving a closed-form rule for the number of flux parameters, derived on regular polygons and verified numerically on distorted ones and on elements with hanging nodes. Darcy's law is written in each element for the Kirchhoff potential, which removes the conductivity from the diffusion while the head stays continuous across material interfaces. A Kirchhoff mean of the conductivity makes hydrostatic equilibrium and gravity drainage exact on any mesh. The storage is lumped on the nodes with weights supplied by the assumed flux. All the element operators reduce to boundary integrals, so that the nonlinear iterations need only nodal values. The formulation is assessed on solutions in closed form, on published benchmarks and on rainfall over homogeneous and layered slopes, where independent solutions provide a further check. It converges at second order in the head on polygonal and locally refined meshes, also where gravity dominates, and closes the water budget in every test. On a layered slope, cut grids refined in a band along the surface reach the accuracy of a uniform grid twice as fine with about 40% of the nodes. Its structure, shared with the HVEM for elastoplasticity, suits coupled analyses of slopes.

title: Density and holes of the visible points in certain cut-and-project sets
abstract: We study the set of visible points from the origin in certain cut-and-project sets, specifically the density of the set. We generalize to all real quadratic number fields the formulas for the density found by G. Hammarhjelm, and the corresponding error bounds proved by I. Gringlaz, R. Kumar, B. Weiss. We also find the possible densities of the set of visible points in the cut-and-project set, with a constant generic lattice, and a changing window with constant volume. We also study bounds for the distance of large holes in the set of visible points of certain cut-and-project sets, generalizing theorems originally proved by P. Erdős for $\mathbb{Z}^2$.

title: Open Problems on the Null Space and Image Space of the Adjacency Matrix
abstract: Akbari, Cameron, and Khosrovshahi proposed two questions concerning the null space and the image space of graphs. Although these problems have been studied in several cases, they have not yet been fully resolved. In this work, we present constructions of graphs that satisfy both the problems.

title: Darboux transformations of linear birth-death processes
abstract: In a previous paper we characterized the lower-upper (LU) and upper-lower (UL) factorizations of the infinitesimal generator of a possibly nonconservative birth-death process whose Darboux transformations are again generators of birth-death processes. Here we apply these results to several classical models with linear rates and explicitly known spectral measures: the $M/M/\infty$ queue (Charlier polynomials), the linear birth-death processes (Meixner and Laguerre polynomials), and the linear models of Ismail, Letessier and Valent (associated Laguerre polynomials). For each of them we compute the factors in closed form, determine the admissible ranges of the parameters, and describe the rates, spectral measures and orthogonal polynomials of the Darboux-transformed processes.

title: A Note on the Cut-Locus-Corrected Fréchet Mean Central Limit Theorem
abstract: We record two observations concerning \cite{HLW24}. First, the proof of its Theorem~1 yields the population linearization (13)--(14) at \textit{any critical point} of the Fréchet function $F_μ$, under its remaining geometric and measure-theoretic assumptions; neither isolation nor a nonsingular Hessian of $F_μ$ is needed. Second, its Theorem~2 is given a shorter proof by applying the M-estimator theorem \cite[Theorem~5.23, pp.~53--54]{vdV98} to negative squared distance in normal coordinates, as opposed to the Donsker argument used there. We verify the pointwise differentiability, local square-integrable Lipschitz bound, second order expansion of population loss, consistency, and empirical maximization hypotheses. The resulting covariance retains the cut-locus correction. The same argument applies to suitably selected local sample Fréchet minima when the population Hessian is positive definite.

title: Biharmonic surfaces with flat normal bundle in the four-dimensional sphere
abstract: We prove that a proper biharmonic surface with flat normal bundle in the four-dimensional unit sphere $\mathbb S^4$ lies minimally in a small hypersphere of radius $1/\sqrt{2}$. Since the surfaces with constant mean curvature and those with parallel normalized mean curvature vector field are already understood, the core of the paper is the non-existence of biharmonic surfaces with flat normal bundle in $\mathbb S^4$ whose mean curvature is not constant and whose normalized mean curvature vector field is not parallel. We first show, adapting an argument of Fu, Hong and Yang, that the gradient of the mean curvature is a principal direction. Then the problem reduces to a first order system of ordinary differential equations with a constraint, and we show that this system has no admissible solutions by an elimination argument.

title: Universal $x$-$y$ duality in equivariant topological recursion and quartic Kontsevich model
abstract:
Topological recursion is a universal procedure that generates an infinite family of multi-differentials with different interpretations in various areas of mathematics. Recently, a new understanding of topological recursion has emerged from $x$-$y$ duality, which relates two such families through explicit formulae. We study $x$-$y$ duality, its parametrised version, and symplectic duality in the setting of equivariant topological recursion. We explicitly analyse the pole structure of the resulting dual families and provide recursive formulae for the different types of polar parts. In contrast to classical topological recursion, the dual family has additional poles at fixed points of the group action, and at anti-diagonals determined by the group action.
  We show that the partition function $Z_P(E)=\int_{H_N} e^{-N\,\mathrm{Tr}(EΦ^2+P(Φ))}dΦ$ of the Kontsevich matrix model with arbitrary potential $P$, where $dΦ$ is the Lebesgue measure on Hermitian $N\times N$ matrices and $E$ a positive matrix, admits a Fock space realisation related to the character expansion of the IZHC integral. The Fock space framework provides two mutually $X$-$Y$ dual families of multi-differentials relative to an implicitly defined spectral curve $(X,Y)$. The solution $Y(X)$ succeeds for the quartic Kontsevich model with potential $P(Φ)=\fracλ{4}Φ^4$. We identify a network of duality transformations and symplectic shifts which relate the quartic Kontsevich model with the $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-equivariant spectral curve. The proposed construction yields a conjectural all-genus solution to the quartic Kontsevich model, which reproduces recursive structures previously established for genus $g\leq 1$.

title: A globally convergent stochastic semismooth Newton method for strongly convex problems in Hilbert spaces
abstract: We propose and analyze a globalized stochastic semismooth Newton method for stochastic optimization problems in Hilbert spaces where the objective is strongly convex with Lipschitz continuous, Newton differentiable gradient. Gradient and generalized Hessian information are only available through mini-batching. In each iteration, a full semismooth Newton trial step is accepted or rejected based on a stochastic residual test and rejected steps are replaced by damped steps in the same Newton direction. Throughout, we admit gradient estimators with affinely growing variance, as arises in optimization problems with random partial differential equations as constraints. We prove non-asymptotic global R-linear convergence in expectation as well as almost sure convergence. For sufficiently fast-growing batch sizes, the method transitions almost surely into a regime of pure Newton steps and converges R-superlinearly almost surely. The method is applied to the optimal control of a random elliptic equation featuring a Huber tracking term as well as a random parabolic equation with a Moreau--Yosida penalization of an almost sure state constraint.

title: Parameter-dependent inhomogeneous boundary-value problems in spaces of continuously differentiable functions
abstract: We investigate a broad class of linear inhomogeneous boundary-value problems of order $r$ for systems of ordinary differential equations depending on a parameter $μ$ belonging to an abstract metric space $\mathcal M$. The solutions belong to the spaces of continuously differentiable vector-valued functions $(C^{(n+r)})^m$, $n\in\mathbb{N}\cup\{0\}$, $m, r \in \mathbb{N}$. The boundary conditions have the most general form $By=c$, where $B$ is an arbitrary continuous linear operator from $(C^{(n+r)})^m$ to $\mathbb{C}^{rm}$. Thus, they may contain derivatives of the unknown vector-valued function of integer and/or fractional orders up to $n+r$ inclusive. We establish necessary and sufficient conditions for the continuous dependence of solutions on the parameter $μ$. Furthermore, we prove that the solutions of the original problems can be approximated in the space $(C^{(n+r)})^m$ by solutions of systems of ordinary differential equations with polynomial coefficients, polynomial right-hand sides, and multipoint boundary conditions, where the approximating problems are constructed independently of the right-hand sides of the original problem.

title: Tilting bundles and modifying modules in relative dimension one
abstract:
For projective morphisms $π:Y\to X=\operatorname{Spec}R$ over noetherian complete local rings, with fibres of dimension at most one and $\mathbf{R}π_*\mathcal{O}_Y\cong\mathcal{O}_X$, we construct a tilting fan from cones of pretilting bundles. Maximal cones parametrize tilting bundles, and facet adjacency encodes irreducible mutation. Completeness in positive rank is equivalent to finiteness of tilting bundles modulo line-bundle twists. For closed fibres that are split ADE highest-root cycles or their Stein contractions, we identify tilting bundles with chambers of restricted affine Tits cones and determine the fan.
  Over normal Gorenstein complete local domains, reflexive pushforward takes pretilting bundles on normal projective birational models with fibres of dimension at most one and $π^!\mathcal{O}_X\cong\mathcal{O}_Y$ to modifying modules. Pushforwards of canonical tilting bundles recover models as module blowups and detect contractions by additive containment, yielding an Auslander--McKay embedding.
  The hypersurfaces $R=S[[u,v]]/(uv-f)$, with $S$ a regular complete local ring and $f\in S$ a nonzero nonunit, generalize type $A$ Du Val surfaces and $cA_n$ threefolds to arbitrary dimension. We classify modifying modules by divisor flags and rank-one reflexive twists; flag blowups turn the embedding into an equivalence. If $f$ has $r\ge2$ prime factors counted with multiplicity, reflexive pushforward on any maximal-flag model gives a mutation-preserving surjection from tilting bundles, parametrized by chambers of affine type $\widetilde{A}_{r-1}$, to maximal modifying modules. Its fibres are affine Weyl group orbits determined by repeated factors. All maximal-flag models and maximal modification algebras are derived equivalent. These algebras are noncommutative crepant resolutions exactly when $S/(p)$ is regular for every prime factor $p$ of $f$.

title: On the Spectral Dependence of Decentralized Stochastic Gradient Tracking
abstract: We study how the spectral geometry of the mixing matrix enters the convergence of decentralized stochastic gradient tracking (GT) for smooth strongly convex problems. General bounds contain the factor $Δ_λ^{-3}$ in the higher-order stochastic term, where $Δ_λ$ is the absolute spectral gap. We show that, even for two agents with identical quadratic objectives, the exact steady-state mean-square disagreement scales as $α^2σ^2Δ_λ^{-3}$ as the nontrivial eigenvalue approaches $-1$, provided the stepsize $α$ is sufficiently small relative to the gap. Here $σ^2$ is the gradient-noise variance. By unrolling the disagreement recursion, we establish a stochastic bound that averages all nontrivial eigenvalue contributions for diagonalizable mixing matrices, up to an eigenvector conditioning factor. As a real or complex eigenvalue approaches the unit circle away from $1$, its contribution grows as the inverse cube of its distance to the circle; growth can be slower near $1$. For symmetric mixing with gaps $p$ at $1$ and $ν$ at $-1$, the weighted sum $θ_1/p+θ_2/ν^3$ replaces the prior factor $(Δ_λν^2)^{-1}$. For $N$ agents, $Nθ_1$ and $Nθ_2$ count the nonnegative and negative nontrivial eigenvalues, respectively. On a symmetric family, a finite-horizon lower bound for the average iterate matches the worst-case factor $p^{-1}+ν^{-3}$ up to universal constants. Numerical experiments confirm the predicted scaling.

title: Operational Indirect Rate-Distortion Functions for Classification Tasks
abstract: In goal-oriented communications, indirect source coding involves two sources: a semantic source $X$ and an observation $Z$, which is the only source available at the encoder. In this paper, we consider this framework for classification, where the decoder only needs to reconstruct $X$. We argue that the gap between the indirect rate-distortion function and the performance of practical learned coding schemes, such as variational information bottleneck (VIB) and variational autoencoder (VAE) architectures, comes from three effects: the latent representation, the choice of the deep neural network (DNN) architecture and training loss, and whether the encoder is aware of the task. To quantify these effects, we introduce four operational rate-distortion functions that account for the DNN architecture and the training loss, and we establish a hierarchy among them. We then derive these functions for a Gaussian mixture source, where $X$ is the mixture state. Numerical results, both for the Gaussian mixture and for practical coding schemes on the CIFAR-100 dataset, quantify the rate loss incurred by each effect.

title: P-curvature from a TQFT viewpoint
abstract: This paper is motivated by the recent discovery, in symplectic topology, of a relation (partly proved, partly conjectural) between quantum connection and quantum Steenrod operations. We introduce an abstract TQFT framework, based on certain features of the definition of deformed symplectic cohomology, in which such a relation holds generally.

title: A Story of Algebra and Categories I: Algebraic Theories
abstract: This is the first part of a series of expository notes on homotopical and categorical algebra. It charts a course from ordinary algebraic structures such as monoids, groups, and rings to their various homotopy-coherent generalizations and equivariant versions. The emphasis is on the ideas that lead to and connect the constructions, as well as where and how they appear in nature.

title: On minimal singular vectors of $V^κ(\mathfrak{g})$ for types $B$ and $C$
abstract: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a finite-dimensional simple Lie algebra of type $B$ or $C$ over ${\mathbb C}$. Given $κ\in{\mathbb C}$, let $V^κ(\mathfrak{g})$ be the universal affine vertex algebra associated with $\mathfrak{g}$ at level $κ$. We characterize the weights of minimal singular vectors of $V^κ(\mathfrak{g})$ with respect to the generalized Cartan matrix, when $V^κ(\mathfrak{g})$ is not simple and $κ$ is not critical. Furthermore, we determine the corresponding longest Weyl elements in the Kashiwara-Tanisaki character theorem of the singular vectors.

title: Failure of Pólya-Szegő inequality for weighted nonlocal seminorm and on nonlocal C-K-N inequality
abstract:
We create counterexamples to show that Pólya-Szegő type of inequality fails for the weighted nonlocal seminorm \begin{equation*}
  [u]_{W^{s,p, α}(\mathbb{R}^d)} := \left( \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \frac{|x|^{α_{1} p} |y|^{α_{2} p} |u(x)-u(y)|^{p}}{|x-y|^{d+sp}} \, dx \, dy \right)^{\frac{1}{p}} \ , \end{equation*} in all three regimes $α_1 +α_2 < 0, \, α_1 +α_2 = 0$, and $α_1 +α_2 >0$. These counterexamples are such that it completely settles the first two cases for all parameters. We also provide necessary and sufficient conditions on the parameters for $ [u]_{W^{s,p, α}(\mathbb{R}^d)} < \infty$, thus extending an earlier known result of [Serena Dipierro and Enrico Valdinoci, A density property for fractional weighted Sobolev spaces]. We also provide another proof of the fractional C-K-N type inequality, for most of the parameters (Hardy and Sobolev are included), using a familiar technique which is involved in the proof of fractional Sobolev inequality of [Eleonora Di Nezza, Giampiero Palatucci, and Enrico Valdinoci, Hitchhiker's guide to the fractional Sobolev spaces, Bulletin des sciences mathematiques] together with a symmetrization technique.

title: Fermat quotients with CM Jacobians and trivial automorphism group
abstract:
Let $F_n$ be the Fermat curve of degree $n$ over $\mathbb Q$, and let $D_n=F_n/S_3$ be its quotient by coordinate permutations. We prove that $D_n$ has trivial geometric automorphism group for every $n\ge 11$ with $\gcd(n,6)=1$. Its Jacobian has complex multiplication. For $n=11$, this Jacobian is absolutely simple of dimension five. We construct an isogeny over $\mathbb Q$ of degree $11^5$ from $\operatorname{Jac}(D_{11})$ to the Jacobian of $y^{11}=x(1-x)^2$.
  For primes $p\equiv 1\pmod 3$, we also consider the metacyclic quotients $C_p$ of $F_p$ over $\mathbb Q$. By a theorem of Carocca, Lange and Rodríguez, their Jacobians are absolutely simple and have complex multiplication. We prove that $C_p$ has trivial geometric automorphism group if and only if $p\ge 19$. Write $p=r^2+rs+s^2$ with $r,s$ positive integers. The natural degree-three cover $Y_p\to C_p$ satisfies $\operatorname{gon}(Y_p)=r+s$, so $\operatorname{gon}(C_p)\ge \lceil(r+s)/3\rceil$. Since $g(C_p)=(p-1)/6$, both the genus and the gonality of $C_p$ tend to infinity with $p$.

title: Classification of analytic $\text{SO}^o(p,q)$-actions on closed $(p+q-1)$-dimensional manifolds II : $p \geq 3$, $q=1,2$
abstract: This paper provides a classification of analytic actions of the semi-orthogonal groups $\text{SO}^\circ(p,1)$ and $\text{SO}^\circ(p,2)$, for $p \geq 3$, on closed, connected manifolds of dimension $p$ and $p+1$ respectively. It is a sequel to a previous paper, which treats the case $p,q \geq 3$. Adapting Uchida's methods, we explicitly construct analytic actions of $\text{SO}^\circ(p,1)$ on $\text{S}^{p}$ and $\text{S}^{p-1} \times \text{S}^{1}$, and analytic actions of $\text{SO}^\circ(p,2)$ on $\text{S}^{p+1}$, $\text{S}^{p} \times \text{S}^{1}$ and $\text{S}^{p-1} \times \text{S}^{2}$, and we classify them up to analytic isomorphism, using a result of Hitchin and Schneider's classification of analytic $\text{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ actions on surfaces. The main result demonstrates that any analytic $\text{SO}^\circ(p,q)$ action, $q=1,2$, on a closed, connected $(p+q-1)$-dimensional manifold is covered by one of the constructed actions or by an action on $\text{SO}^\circ(p,q) \times_P \text{S}^1$, where $P$ is a maximal parabolic subgroup of $\text{SO}^\circ(p,q)$.

title: Necessary and sufficient conditions for the self-normalized central limit theorem for independent triangular arrays
abstract: For a rowwise independent triangular array $\{X_{n,i}:1\le i\le n\}$, put $S_n=\sum_{i=1}^nX_{n,i}$ and $V_n^2=\sum_{i=1}^nX_{n,i}^2$. We prove that $S_n/V_n\xrightarrow{\mathrm d}{\mathrm N}(0,1)$ implies $\max_{i\le n}|X_{n,i}|/V_n\xrightarrow{\mathbb P}0$. The same assumption gives $V_n^2/b_n^2\xrightarrow{\mathbb P}1$ for any choice of medians $b_n^2$ of $V_n^2$. Combined with the results of Shao (2018), this yields necessary and sufficient conditions for the self-normalized central limit theorem and resolves his conjecture for independent sequences. The proof identifies the joint limits of the sum and its sum of squares, then uses the standard normal ratio to remove every non-Gaussian component.

title: Linear bounds and sharp exponential growth for commuting matrix algebra
abstract: For any $m$ pairwise commuting matrices $\{A_i\}_{i=1}^{m}\subset \M_n(\F)$, we prove $\dim_\F \F[A_1,\cdots, A_m]\leq (2^m-1)(n-1)+1$, answering Bergman's question on the existence of a linear bound for a fixed number $m$.

title: Categorified convergence: dropping the 'ultra' from 'virtual ultracategories'
abstract: Virtual ultracategories are a recent categorification of topological spaces seen as sets of points together with a convergence relation between points and ultrafilters. However, a topology can also be described in terms of convergence of filters: in this paper, we thus introduce an analogue of virtual ultracategories based on filters rather than ultrafilters. At the topological level, convergence of filters is completely determined by its restriction to ultrafilters. Our main result shows that, under the assumption of tautness, the same phenomenon holds at the categorified level, thereby offering a non-ultra-biased perspective on virtual ultracategories.

title: The stochastic Ginzburg-Landau equation with harmonic potential in the full subcritical regime
abstract: In this paper, we construct the complex Ginzburg-Landau dynamic associated with the harmonic oscillator, with a random force which is white in time and covers the full subcritical range in space. We are able to renormalise the non-linearity using the same constant as the one used to renormalise the problem associated to the Laplacian. By an extension of the problem to complex times, we are able to prove that the solution of the complex Ginzburg-Landau is equal in law to the solution of the purely dissipative case, i.e. the associated complex $Φ^4$ model, but along a complex axis of time.

title: Exact regions for the symmetrized Blest coefficient
abstract: Spearman's rho treats all ranks alike, yet in many comparisons of two rankings an agreement at the top matters more than one at the bottom. Blest's rank correlation builds this preference into Spearman's rho, and its symmetrized version $η$, introduced by Genest and Plante, does so without favoring either of the two rankings. How far can such a top-weighted coefficient stray from other rank correlations? We answer this question for Spearman's rho, Blomqvist's beta and Chatterjee's rank correlation $ξ$ by determining the exact set of values that $η$ and each of these coefficients can attain jointly. Given Spearman's rho, $η$ can differ from it by at most $27/128$, and the extreme values of $η$ are attained only when the two rankings agree perfectly on the top ranks and are completely reversed on the bottom ranks, or vice versa. Given Blomqvist's beta, $η$ obeys exactly the same sharp bounds as Spearman's rho. For Chatterjee's rank correlation, both boundary curves are explicit and are attained by copulas with densities. Here symmetrization has a surprising effect. Compared with Blest's original coefficient, $η$ has a narrower range at fixed Spearman's rho, but near independence a wider range at fixed Chatterjee's rank correlation, where $|η|$ can come close to $\sqrt{11ξ/5}$ while Blest's coefficient stays below $\sqrt{32ξ/15}$. The proofs combine explicit Kantorovich potentials from optimal transport with a convex relaxation that turns out to be exact.

title: Overcompressive shocks in a $2\times2$ hyperbolic system of conservation laws
abstract: Overcompressive shocks in a $2\times2$ hyperbolic system of conservation laws describing small-amplitude longitudinal-torsional waves in an elastic rod are investigated. A viscous regularization method with an anisotropic dissipative matrix is applied to the system. A qualitative analysis of phase portraits has revealed that a two-parameter family of heteroclinic trajectories, representing the structure of an overcompressive shock, exists in one of six domains in the parameter plane. It is established that the model admits overcompressive shocks, which belong to the first type according to the classification of Liu.

title: The index of mesoscopic Wilson--Dirac operators: I
abstract: This is the first of a series of papers which will be devoted to a study of the index of mesoscopic Wilson--Dirac operators on closed Riemannian manifolds. The aim of the series is to discretise the index of the Dirac operator. On flat tori, this is achieved by the Wilson--Dirac operator of lattice gauge theory on a regular lattice. On a general closed Riemannian manifold, however, no regular lattice is available. As an intermediate step between the continuum Dirac operator and its discretisations, we introduce mesoscopic Wilson--Dirac operators on any closed Riemannian manifold, defined by integrating covariant differences over distances comparable to a fixed length scale. In this paper, we define the index of the mesoscopic Wilson--Dirac operators via spectral flow and prove that it agrees with that of the continuum Dirac operator at all sufficiently small scales. The proof rests on an elliptic estimate uniform in the scale and a Rellich-type compactness theorem. In the second paper, we shall pass from mesoscopic operators to discrete Wilson--Dirac operators.

title: Shock solutions of a 3D spherical piston problem for the compressible Euler equations
abstract: This paper establishes the global well-posedness of shock solutions for a 3D spherical piston problem to the compressible Euler equations. The main mathematical challenges are the nonlinear coupling between the free shock boundary and the moving piston, alongside potential gradient catastrophes induced by spherical geometric source terms. To overcome these difficulties, we reformulate the problem using Riemann invariants and introduce a tailored directional derivative along the unperturbed piston trajectory. Then we can extend the local solution to construct a global piecewise smooth solution including a single shock under some moderate assumptions.

title: Arithmetic theta products and doubling at arbitrary level
abstract:
We prove an arithmetic doubling identity for the standard arithmetic theta series on $X_0(N)$ at arbitrary positive level, with constant $ψ(N)/24$ for the fixed genus-two Eisenstein series. The product comparison covers all pairs of integral indices. At rank zero, an explicit Epstein zeta correction agrees with the middle Bruhat orbit of the Eisenstein derivative.
  The common-component calculation combines integral CM adjunction, the cyclic difference divisor, and compact Green-current identities. It retains the different, conductor, internal contacts, and proportionality contacts at every prime, including dyadic and supersingular places. Finite intersections, curvature, and discriminant heights identify the nonpositive coefficients with an explicit modular completion. Uniform estimates for parameter derivatives give strong Fourier convergence. Green-energy estimates justify the double Petersson pairing. The full cusp lift exists as a Bochner integral and equals its Mordell--Weil projection.
  For $\mathbb Z/(2N)\mathbb Z$, explicit prime-power recursions determine the complete zero-component trace spectrum, including the dyadic factor. They give the scalar-to-vector Petersson norm correction and an isometric normalization on the active subspace. The Bruinier--Yang theorem then yields the scalar height formula on the specified Jacobi newform line. We also prove a double Rankin--Selberg criterion based on positive diagonal coefficients and record the paired analytic factorization with its ramified local integrals retained explicitly.

title: Diameter bounds for complexes that are close to flag or close to normal
abstract: The Hirsch problem asks how large the diameter of the dual graph of a simplicial complex can be, in terms of its number of vertices. For normal complexes, the classical bounds are the Larman-Barnette bound, which is linear for fixed dimension, the Kalai-Kleitman bound, which is quasi-polynomial, and the Adiprasito-Benedetti bound n-d, which however holds only for flag complexes. After sharpening the Larman-Barnette and the Kalai-Kleitman bounds, we study how the three bounds deteriorate when flagness or normality is weakened. We give three ways to quantify the distance from flagness, and in each case we bound the diameter in a way that interpolates between the Adiprasito-Benedetti and the Larman-Barnette bounds. We also quantify the distance from normality by a parameter q, and obtain a bound that is a polynomial of degree q in n. Finally, we conjecture a statement on flag layered families that would imply an interpolation between the Adiprasito-Benedetti and the Kalai-Kleitman bounds.

title: Funnel MPC for port-Hamiltonian systems
abstract: Port-Hamiltonian systems are an energy-based modelling formalism, that has strong ties to the physical models and allows interconnection of systems. Funnel MPC, a Model Predictive Control (MPC) scheme, allows for output tracking with prescribed error bounds. Earlier works focused on systems with stable internal dynamics, which typically excludes port-Hamiltonian systems. We introduce a modified stage cost design that takes into account the port-Hamiltonian structure of the system and allows deactivation of the funnel cost. We show initial and recursive feasibility for a class of port-Hamiltonian systems with relative degree one including unstable internal dynamics.

title: Fourier level inequalities on the discrete cube via complex hypercontractivity and Riesz transforms
abstract:
Eldan's level-$1{:}3$ inequality is a central tool in his second-order correlation inequalities for increasing Boolean functions. His proof is going to Gaussian space and uses an entropy estimate for second Hermite tensors. We give a direct proof on the discrete hypercube. For increasing real-valued functions $f,g:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, we prove $$ W_3[f,g]\ge -2W_1[f,g]\log\!\left(\frac{\sqrt{\mathrm{Var}(f)\mathrm{Var}(g)}}{W_1[f,g]}\right). $$ The proof combines complex hypercontractivity with the discrete Riesz transforms. We also give a short proof of a level-$1:d$ inequality obtained by Keller and Kindler.
  As an application, we recover Eldan's correlation inequality with a slight improvement. If $f,g:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ are increasing and $g$ is antipodal, then $$ \mathrm{Cov}(f,g)\ge \frac1{24}\,\frac{\sum_i\mathrm{Inf}_i[f]\mathrm{Inf}_i[g]}{\sqrt{\log\!\left(4e\sqrt{\mathrm{Var}(f)\mathrm{Var}(g)}/(\sum_i\mathrm{Inf}_i[f]\mathrm{Inf}_i[g])\right)}}, $$ where the square-root logarithm cannot be improved as shown in the OR--majority example.

title: A Note on the OpenAI Construction of Counterexamples to the Kaplansky Direct-Finiteness Conjecture
abstract: We give a human-readable exposition of OpenAI's construction of a group algebra in characteristic two that is not directly finite. We then adapt the argument to show that, for every prime $p$, there exists a hyperbolic group $G_p$ such that $\mathbb{F}_p[G_p]$ is not directly finite.

title: Generalized Hopf bifurcations: a homological analysis and obstructions to their existence
abstract: A generalized Hopf bifurcation takes place when varying a parameter of a (semi)dynamical system causes an attractor $K$ to become a repeller. In doing so, it expels a (parameter-dependent) family of attractors. In this paper we concentrate on two questions: (1) what do the expelled attractors look like?, and (2) can any attractor $K$ undergo a generalized Hopf bifurcation? Regarding (1), we compute the cohomology of the expelled attractors in terms of the cohomology of $K$; in the case of continuous-time dynamics this can be improved to a computation of their Borsuk shape. As for (2), we show that certain compacta cannot undergo generalized Hopf bifurcations and, when the ambient space has dimension $ \leq 3$, give a complete topological characterization of which can.

title: Isomorphisms and automorphisms of minimal comaximal hypergraphs of commutative rings
abstract: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with exactly $n\ge 2$ maximal ideals and let $k\ge 2$. We study the minimal $k$-uniform comaximal hypergraph $\mathcal{H}_k(R)$, whose vertices are the nonunits outside the Jacobson radical and whose edges are the irredundant $k$-element comaximal families. For $2\le k\le n$ we show that $\mathcal{H}_k(R)$ is a blow-up of the hypergraph of irredundant $k$-coverings of $\{1,\dots,n\}$, and that its reduced form reconstructs the maximal ideals up to permutation; for $k>n$ there are no edges. We obtain a general description of $\mathrm{Aut}(\mathcal{H}_k(R))$ and characterize isomorphisms of such hypergraphs. For $3\le k\le n$ its automorphism group properly contains that of the comaximal graph, and for finite rings with $n\ge 3$ and every $2\le k\le n$, $\mathcal{H}_k(R)$ has the same isomorphism invariants as the comaximal graph, namely $|J(R)|$ and $R/J(R)$. The case $k=2$ recovers and extends the automorphism results for comaximal graphs obtained previously. We also compare the minimal and non-minimal comaximal hypergraphs and identify a condition under which the latter has the same automorphism group and isomorphism invariants as the comaximal graph. The same method determines the vertex set and the automorphism group of the $k$-zero-divisor hypergraph of a product of integral domains, and shows that for finite products of finite fields this hypergraph determines the ring.

title: A stability order barrier and SSP bound for Runge--Kutta methods with non-negative coefficients: AI-assisted proofs
abstract: We prove three results about Runge--Kutta methods with non-negative coefficients. First, every $s$-stage implicit Runge--Kutta method of order at least two has SSP coefficient at most $2s$; the bound is sharp and is attained by a known diagonally implicit method, so full implicitness gives no advantage over DIRK at second order. This extends the second-order DIRK result of Kocsis \& Németh to full coefficient matrices and settles a conjecture of Ketcheson, Macdonald & Gottlieb. These proofs were found with the assistance of AI tools, which uncovered an interesting relationship between the Butcher matrices for SSP methods and phase-type distributions, and led to the proof of the second result: a bound on the SSP coefficient of $s$-stage implicit Runge--Kutta method of order at least three. The third result in this work is a proof that a third-order Runge--Kutta method with entrywise non-negative $A$ and $b$ cannot be algebraically stable. This algebraically intensive proof was also AI-assisted. This paper describes the iterative process of AI-assisted results, and presents an approach that centers human understanding and creativity in the AI-assisted mathematical endeavor.

title: A positive answer to Barsotti and Carman's question on unit groups of Burnside rings of fusion systems
Quantifying the remaining search space in analogue optimisation
abstract: Benchmarking analogue optimisers requires certifying not only how close a returned energy is to the optimum, but also how many better configurations may remain. Semidefinite relaxations provide rigorous bounds on the ground-state energy and selected observables, yet reveal little about the size of this residual search space. We introduce a deterministic, instance-specific upper bound on the number of binary configurations whose energies improve upon a returned state by a prescribed margin. Combined with a semidefinite energy interval, this yields a complementary certificate of both the magnitude and multiplicity of any possible improvement. To judge an analogue optimiser's native performance, we provide a generalisation of the framework to obtain bounds on the Haar volume of the remaining continuous phase-space. To further characterise the remaining search space, we extend our bounds to resolve regions in configuration space in both the binary and continuous setting. Our approach couples a variational-Chernoff reduction with an elimination bound of the resulting partition function. Comparisons with exact enumeration and independent Haar sampling are consistent with the bounds on small instances. In numerical experiments at $N=1000$, even the largest family-median bound restricts the potentially improving binary configurations to less than $10^{-144}$ of the full configuration space, while the largest upper bound on the corresponding Haar volume is of order $10^{-499}$.

title: Constructive Probability, Foundations and Numerical Analysis for mathematical finance and machine learning
abstract: This monograph sets out a constructive theory of stochastic processes in the continuum, in the sense of constructive field theory: the continuum is not postulated but reached as the limit of a sequence of lattice approximations, with the renormalisation the limit requires exhibited rather than assumed, and the limit controlled by estimates that can be checked. The primitive object is not a sigma-algebra but de Finetti's prevision, the price of finitely many gambles at a fixed resolution, which coherence turns into a conditional expectation. The theorem at the centre of the book, called plainly the fundamental theorem, is at once de Finetti's fundamental theorem of probability, the fundamental theorem of Bayesian statistics, and the one-period fundamental theorem of asset pricing; the financial vocabulary is a convenience only. The applications are two, mathematical finance and machine learning, and they are one mathematics read in opposite directions: an assessment is a price in the one and a prediction in the other, and both are computed by one adjoint recursion, the adjoint of a propagation in the first case and backpropagation in the second. Carried through, the two directions give sharp rates of convergence rather than asymptotic orders: for the moments of Ito diffusions, for the value function of Feynman-Kac semigroups, and for the measure changes of the fundamental theorem, the last as a limit theorem for reweighted generators, under a condition keeping the reweighting well behaved. A measure change is thus calculated, not postulated: a lattice approximation with Farkas' lemma computes it, completeness makes it unique, and the passage to the continuum is earned by the regularity of what is computed. Sixty-seven Python scripts regenerate every numerical table, and much of the finite-dimensional core of the argument has been verified in Lean 4.

title: The Approximation Property without the Bounded Approximation Property in a Separable Banach Space and Its Dual
abstract:
We investigate whether a dual Banach space with the approximation property (AP) must necessarily have the bounded approximation property (BAP). Using a quantitative renorming theorem for the space of absolutely summable sequences, we establish a direct-sum construction yielding a negative answer.
  More precisely, we construct a separable Banach space (X) such that both (X) and its dual (X^*) have the approximation property, while neither space has the bounded approximation property. The construction uses a sequence of equivalent renormings of (\ell_1) with increasingly restrictive finite-dimensional approximation bounds. By assembling these spaces through a (c_0)-direct sum, we obtain a dual space whose approximation property is preserved, but whose approximation constants cannot be uniformly bounded.
  We establish the required transfer principles, including the preservation of approximation bounds under complemented coordinate projections and the descent of the bounded approximation property from a dual space to its predual. We also provide an explicit complex-scalar version of the construction.
  The argument separates the external quantitative renorming input from the direct-sum construction and its functional-analytic consequences. In particular, the resulting example demonstrates that the approximation property of a dual space does not imply its bounded approximation property, even when the predual is separable and both spaces possess the approximation property.

title: Pappus's hexagon theorem for geodesic curves in $\SLR$ geometry
abstract: In this paper, we continue our investigation of the structure of Thurston geometries with non-constant curvature. We generalize the notion of cylinders, prove that they contain the types of geodesic curves. Moreover, we formulate and prove a statement analogous to Pappus's hexagon theorem for $\SLR$ geometry.

title: Existence, Uniqueness, Feller Property and Diricihlet form of the Keller-Segel particle system up to blow up
abstract: The Keller-Segel particle system as defined in \cite{ft} through the Dirichlet form theory (see \cite{f}) consists of $N$ planar Brownian motions interacting through the kernel $x\in \rr^2 \mapsto θK(x) = -θx/\|x\|^2$, where $θ>0$. One particularity of this model is that collisions (i.e. overlapping of particles) occur depending on the value of $θ$, making the well-posedness of the particle system delicate. In this work, we propose a new notion of solution of this SDE without relying on the Dirichlet form theory and prove uniqueness in law of such solutions. The proof relies on an excursion decomposition of the particle system based on the "barycenter-radius-angle" decomposition in \cite{ft}. As additional results, we prove that the solution is strong Markov, has the Feller property and fits in the definition of solutions in the Dirichlet form sense. Finally we prove that the law of the particle system starting from a configuration where all the particles overlap is explicit.

title: Universal Dimension Formula for Planar $C^r$ Splines at Degree $3r+1$
abstract: We prove that Schumaker's lower bound gives the dimension of $S_{3r+1}^r(Δ)$ for every nondegenerate triangulation $Δ$ of a polygonal disk in $\mathbb{R}^2$ and every integer $r\ge3$. After accounting for the local vertex contributions, we reduce the remaining dimension defect to compatible vertex functionals. Apolarity associates a unique polynomial with each face, and compatibility forces differences of adjacent face polynomials to contain powers of both endpoint forms. We eliminate the leading residual coefficient using Hermite relations when $r$ is odd and an additional coefficient comparison when $r$ is even. A uniform induction then raises the endpoint powers until all face differences vanish; the zero boundary face potentials imply that every vertex functional vanishes and the global defect is zero. Together with the known cases $r=1,2$ and Hong's higher-degree theorem, this yields the dimension formula for all $r\ge1$ and $d\ge3r+1$.

title: Uniqueness and nondegeneracy for a critical Choquard equation with Hardy potential
abstract: We study the critical Choquard equation \[ -Δu-μ|x|^{-2}u =\bigl(|\cdot|^{2-N}*|u|^p\bigr)|u|^{p-2}u \qquad\text{in }\mathbb R^N, \] where $|\cdot|^{2-N}$ is the Newton kernel, $p=\frac{N+2}{N-2}$, and $0<μ<\frac{(N-2)^2}{4}$. For every $N\ge3$, we prove that positive solutions in $D^{1,2}(\mathbb R^N)$ are radially symmetric about the origin, unique up to dilation, and nondegenerate. Our proof uses normalized logarithmic derivatives to obtain a cooperative system. The resulting monotonicity principle underlies both the uniqueness and nondegeneracy arguments, and remains effective in the subquadratic range $1<p<2$, corresponding to $N\ge7$. Consequently, the linearized quadratic form has Morse index one and the sharp inequality admits a global quadratic remainder estimate. The best constant is strictly concave in the Hardy parameter on $\bigl[0,\frac{(N-2)^2}{4}\bigr)$, is of class $C^2$ with strictly negative second derivative in the interior, and satisfies two-sided bounds that agree to first order at $μ=0$.

title: The Calkin--Wilf problems on $\ell$-ary partition functions
abstract: In their 1998 precursor to their celebrated paper ``Recounting the rationals,'' Calkin and Wilf listed nine open problems related to the function $b_{k,\ell}(n)$, the number of partitions of $n$ into powers of $\ell$ with each part appearing at most $k$ times. In this short paper, we answer five of their eight remaining open problems. As a consequence of our results, we extend and generalise results of both Carlitz and Reznick, and answer an open question of Reznick.

title: A Solution Method for Single-Source Capacitated Facility Location Problems Under Decision-Dependent Demand Uncertainty
abstract: We present a model and an exact solution method for single-source capacitated facility location problems with decision-dependent demand uncertainty. The model allows the joint probability distribution of customer demands to depend on the facility to which demand points are allocated. The number of possible decision-dependent distributions is therefore equal to the number of feasible allocations of demand points to (groups of) facilities. To address the exponential size of the model, we apply and extend a recent version of the L-Shaped method for stochastic programs with decision-dependent uncertainty. In particular,we compare the original optimality cut with a new optimality cut based on a bilinear reformulation. We prove that, separated together with the original one, the new cut yields a tighter restriction, at the expense of introducing bilinear terms. In addition, we prove an effective decision-independent valid inequality that significantly improves convergence. Extensive numerical tests on 180 instances demonstrate that the method, supported by the valid inequality, can find optimal or near-optimal solutions to problem instances with up to 620 potential probability distributions. The tests also show that, while the new cut closes slightly more instances, the original cut remains preferable in terms of solution time and optimality gap.

title: On Grassmann $4$-designs
abstract: We prove that there is a unique tight $4$-design in the real Grassmannian $G_{2,4}$, up to the action of $O(4)$. Using symmetric association schemes, we also construct an $N$-point $4$-design in $G_{2,4}$ for every even integer $N\geq10$. For symmetric association schemes of order less than $21$, we classify the pairs of rank-three primitive idempotents defining injective maps into $G_{2,4}$; their images are Grassmannian $4$-designs precisely for four schemes of order $16$.

title: A centroaffine perspective on improved Brascamp--Lieb and dimensional Brunn--Minkowski inequalities
abstract: We study dimensional concavity properties of even log-concave measures within the framework of weighted centroaffine differential geometry. We express the relevant local concavity inequalities in terms of a weighted Hilbert--Brunn--Minkowski operator and establish an anisotropic Poincaré inequality for odd functions and a strengthened Brascamp--Lieb inequality for even functions. As applications, we obtain quantitative dimensional concavity estimates for a class of geometric measures and measures with pinched Hessian, extending results of Cordero-Erausquin and Rotem for rotationally invariant measures and Eskenazis and Moschidis for the Gaussian measure.

title: Preconditioning for the time-dependent Stokes equations: stage-weighted Radau IIA and weighted discontinuous Galerkin time-stepping
abstract: We determine field-of-values equivalent preconditioners for the time-dependent Stokes equations discretized in time by stage-weighted Radau IIA Runge--Kutta time-stepping and discontinuous Galerkin time-stepping methods. By weighing each stage of the Radau IIA Runge--Kutta method differently we obtain preconditioners that are field-of-values equivalent, with constants independent of viscosity, timestep, and mesh size, to the system matrix. Similarly, by using weighted inner products in time to define the discontinuous Galerkin time-stepping method, we again obtain field-of-values equivalent preconditioners for the resulting system matrix. Numerical experiments are performed in two and three-dimensions which demonstrate robustness of the proposed preconditioners.

title: Shades and Convexity of Hypersurfaces
abstract: Let $f\colon M^n\to\mathbf{R}^{n+1}$, $n\geq2$, be a smooth immersion of a closed oriented manifold, with Gauss map $ν\colon M\to\mathbf{S}^n$. For each unit vector $u$, the shade $S_u\subset M$ is the set of points where $ν$ makes an acute angle with $u$. We show that $f$ is a convex embedding if and only if every shade is contractible. More generally, if every shade is $k$-connected, then $f$ is a convex embedding provided that $n\leq 2k+1$, or $n=2k+2$ and $H_{k+1}(M;\mathbf{Z})=0$. On the other hand, for every $n\geq 2k+3$ there is a nonconvex embedding $f\colon\mathbf{S}^n\to\mathbf{R}^{n+1}$ all of whose shades are $k$-connected. These results give sharp answers to a question of H. Wente in all dimensions.

title: Averages of sub-additive functions through non-Følner sequences
abstract:
We study the quantity $\sup_{φ\inΦ}\limsup_{n\to\infty}φ(F_n)/|F_n|$, where $\mathcal F= (F_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ is a sequence of finite subsets of a countable amenable group, and $Φ$ is a collection of subadditive functions. Under mild conditions on $Φ$ we prove that the aforementioned quantity equals the supremum over $φ\inΦ$ of the limit of $φ(F)/|F|$ as $F$ becomes more and more invariant, multiplied by a ``Følnerness'' constant $C(\mathcal F)\in[1,\infty]$. We have $C(\mathcal F)=1$ if and only if $\mathcal F$ is Følner. A corollary of this result is that every choice of a non-Følner sequence overestimates topological and measure-theoretic entropy by the multiplicative factor $C(\mathcal F)$ (in the positive entropy case).
  We obtain a generalization of classical results of Goodman, Krug, and Newton, on the so-called proportionality principle for sequence entropy, and their extension by Gao, Huang, and Zhu to countable amenable groups.

title: A Simple Approach to the Complexity of Mean Field Ising Spin Glasses
abstract: The geometry of spherical spin glasses is relatively well understood, thanks in large part to the Kac-Rice formula. However, this formula does not directly apply to discrete spin systems, and much less is known mathematically about the geometry of Ising spin glasses. In this paper, we present a simple method for counting local optima and gapped states in a broad class of discrete spin glasses. To illustrate its scope, we compute the annealed complexities ("configurational entropies," in the physics language) of mixed Ising spin glasses with potentials, such as external fields, and of the Ghatak-Sherrington model. These computations recover several existing results in the mathematics and physics literature as special cases. We can also compute energy-constrained complexity, finding a critical energy threshold analogous to the spherical case, but for gapped states of pure Ising spin glasses. Finally, we use our method to establish a form of disorder persistence for gapped states, identifying a transition between $3$-spin and $4$-spin glasses.

title: Almost S-GCD domains: localization, class groups, and extensions
abstract: Let $D$ be an integral domain and let $S\subseteq D\setminus\{0\}$ be multiplicative. We study the condition that, for each nonzero $a,b\in D$, some $(a^n,b^n)_v$ is $S$-principal. A power estimate extends this binary condition to arbitrary finite families and permits synchronization of exponents. We describe the obstruction to descent from the AGCD domain $D_S$ by bounded $S$-torsion and by a finiteness condition on intersections of principal ideals. For an almost Prüfer $v$-multiplication domain, the almost $S$-GCD property, the AGCD property of $D_S$, and torsion of the $S$-class group are equivalent. In Krull domains this gives a criterion in terms of the divisor classes of height-one primes meeting $S$, and finite rational class rank reduces the multiplicative set to one element. We prove conductor transfer without a principal-contraction hypothesis, polynomial transfer in several settings, a normalization homeomorphism away from $S$, and a finite-principal-cover criterion with a Picard-group obstruction. Explicit examples distinguish localization, bounded descent, and the global and sublocal conditions.

title: Fluctuations, Moderate and Large Deviations about Hydrodynamic Limits of Space-Time Hawkes Processes
abstract: We study Gaussian fluctuations, moderate and large deviations around the high-density hydrodynamic limit of critical and nearly critical space-time Hawkes processes initialized by a prescribed Poisson field of past events, with no subsequent immigration. Under a finite mean reproduction delay and centered displacements with finite spatial covariance, a positive cluster-transform estimate yields a distribution-valued central limit theorem (CLT) and a moderate deviation principle (MDP) throughout the moderate range.
