For finite nonzero mass of the initial profile, we obtain a full large deviation principle (LDP) for the space-time event measure in the vague topology; its good rate function is a quadratic branching-control energy with a prescribed initial trace and a finite-mass domain. The lower bound uses an explicit approximation by smooth reproduction controls, and the upper bound uses a microscopic exponential martingale and a global generator approximation. We distinguish exact-mean centering from PDE centering and compute deterministic bias corrections under second delay and fourth spatial moments. For a factorized heavy-tail power-law delay, we establish the CLT, MDP, and full measure-valued LDP for the space-time measure, with finite nonzero mass of the initial profile for the LDP. Its fractional control energy retains the source generated by the prescribed past. A source-preserving regularization proves approximation of every finite-action measure. Compact-kernel bounds for initial profiles of infinite mass and the degenerate case of a zero initial profile are stated separately.

title: Kappa Classes on the KSBA Space of Stable Toric Pairs
abstract: We study kappa classes on the normalization of the main component of the Kollár--Shepherd-Barron--Alexeev(KSBA) moduli space of stable toric pairs. Using a toric model obtained by a lattice modification, we compute all kappa classes on the moduli space by giving a combinatorial formula for their intersection numbers with all torus-invariant cycles. In particular, we identify the first normalized kappa class with the GKZ polarization of the toric variety corresponding to the secondary polytope. For interval configurations, we also obtain a closed formula for all top intersection products of normalized kappa classes.

title: Hypercyclic and topologically transitive semigroups of composition operators (revised and extended version)
abstract: Let $X$ be a separable locally compact metric space, let $E\neq\{0\}$ be a normed space, and let $G$ be a semigroup of continuous self-maps of $X$. Every $\varphi\in G$ induces the composition operator $C_\varphi f=f\circ\varphi$ on the space $C(X,E)$ of continuous functions endowed with the compact-open topology. We characterize the topological transitivity of the semigroup $\widehat{G}=\{C_\varphi:\varphi\in G\}$ by a condition that combines the run-away property of $G$ with an approximate form of injectivity, and we show that, when $E$ is separable, $\widehat{G}$ is topologically transitive if and only if it is hypercyclic. In particular, if every element of $G$ is one-to-one and $G$ is run-away, then $\widehat{G}$ is topologically transitive, and hypercyclic when $E$ is separable. For a single map $\varphi$ we obtain: $C_\varphi$ is hypercyclic $\iff$ $C_\varphi$ is topologically transitive $\iff$ $\varphi$ is one-to-one and run-away, and $C_\varphi$ is mixing $\iff$ $\varphi$ is one-to-one and strongly run-away. If, moreover, $\varphi$ is an open map (which is automatic on manifolds by invariance of domain), then $C_\varphi$ is Devaney chaotic. On an open interval all of these properties are equivalent to $\varphi$ being one-to-one without fixed points.

title: Random Fibonacci Tilings
abstract: The Fibonacci spiral is formed by a square-joining rule: begin with a unit square and attach squares whose side lengths follow the Fibonacci sequence; in the standard construction, choices of direction produce a spiral and a tiling of the plane. We study a randomization of this construction, in which the attachment axis alternates deterministically, while fair coin flips determine direction. For a lattice point we ask when the growing rectangle first covers that point and how the expected covering time depends on its location. Tracking the rectangle's boundary reduces this question to random subset sums of even- and odd-indexed Fibonacci numbers. We extend the construction to d dimensions, where coordinate subsequences are super-increasing, allowing us to derive exact covering probabilities and formulas for the expectation and variance. For $d\geq2$, the expected covering time grows logarithmically with distance from the initial block, while the variance remains uniformly bounded. We obtain exponential tail bounds for the delay beyond the earliest feasible covering stage. Finally, we extend the Fibonacci spiral to the randomized tiling through a square-by-square construction using circular arcs and quintic connectors. This construction uses one-step lookahead, admits a continuously differentiable parameterization, and recovers the Fibonacci spiral for the standard tiling.

title: Exotic smooth structures on complex projective spaces
abstract:
We study smooth structures on the topological manifold underlying complex projective space. We conjecture that every complex projective space $\mathbb{CP}^n$ with $n>3$ admits an exotic smooth structure.
  We prove two results providing strong evidence for this conjecture. First, the set of complex dimensions $n$ for which $\mathbb{CP}^n$ admits an exotic smooth structure has natural density one. Second, we explicitly identify $266$ congruence classes modulo $288$ such that $\mathbb{CP}^n$ admits an exotic smooth structure whenever $n>3$ lies in one of these classes. These classes cover more than $92\%$ of complex dimensions, improving the previously known lower bound of approximately $36\%$.
  We prove these results by first relating the concordance group of $\mathbb{CP}^n$ to suitable Atiyah--Hirzebruch filtration subgroups of its stable cohomotopy group, and then applying computations in chromatic homotopy theory at height $2$.

title: An Accelerated Proximal Gradient Method for Bures-Wasserstein Space
abstract: We study composite optimization over the Bures--Wasserstein (BW) space of Gaussian measures. Our main observation is that a useful class of BW problems can be lifted into the Euclidean space of affine transport maps, such that the lifted problems can be solved efficiently using accelerated proximal gradient methods. For objectives whose smooth and nonsmooth components admit convex smooth and convex proximable affine lifts, respectively, our algorithm BW-FISTA achieves minimax-optimal objective gap $O(k^{-2})$ after $k$ iterations. We verify these regularity conditions for potential and interaction energies together with common spectral regularizers, and we treat stochastic gradients under a suitable noise model. As a principal application, we consider Gaussian variational inference with a log-concave, log-smooth target. Here, the resulting entropy term is handled by an efficient, exact proximal step, and we improve the previous rate of $O(k^{-1})$ to $O(k^{-2})$. We numerically verify this predicted boost with synthetic experiments.

title: Symplectic singularities in Relative Langlands duality for products of general linear groups
abstract: It was shown by Braverman-Finkelberg-Nakajima that the regular perverse sheaf on the affine Grassmannian of type A is isomorphic to the ring object associated to a Gelfand-Tsetlin quiver. We use this result to identify, for any finite dimensional representation $\mathbf{N}$ of a product of general linear groups, the relative Langlands dual $(T^*\mathbf{N})^\vee$ of $T^*\mathbf{N}$ with the Coulomb branch of a suitable representation. By a result of Bellamy, this implies that $(T^*\mathbf{N})^\vee$ has symplectic singularities.

title: On do Carmo's Question: The Properly Embedded Case
abstract:
In this paper, we prove that every complete noncompact two-sided properly embedded constant mean curvature hypersurface of finite Morse index in Euclidean space is minimal. The result holds in every dimension. We assume no bounds on curvature or volume growth. This establishes the properly embedded case of the finite-index version of do Carmo's question.
  For nonzero mean curvature, we use the radii of inscribed balls to define a positive weight. This weight gives a polynomial bound on weighted volume, while its reciprocal satisfies a differential inequality involving the Jacobi operator. We combine these properties with stability outside a compact set to obtain finite total area. This leads to a contradiction.

title: h-dichotomies via noncritical uniformity and expansiveness for noninvertible evolution families
abstract: We establish characterizations of h-dichotomies for noninvertible evolution families acting on Banach spaces, in terms of appropriate notions of expansiveness and uniform noncriticality. Our results extend the corresponding characterizations previously obtained for invertible evolution families. To the best of our knowledge, no such characterizations have previously been established for general noninvertible evolution families. A key difference is that noninvertibility makes the structure of the stable spaces more delicate: in our positive-half-line result, finite codimension must be imposed at every time, rather than only at the initial time. We show by an example that the latter, weaker condition is insufficient. We also study evolution families on the negative half-line, using duality to obtain corresponding characterizations in terms of dual expansiveness and dual uniform noncriticality. General growth rates are treated by a time-rescaling argument.

title: A Central Limit Theorem For Random Variables Under A Constraint
abstract: We consider vectors chosen randomly from high-dimensional hypersurfaces of the form $\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n: \sum_{j=1}^n V_j(x_j)=an\}$. These in general asymmetric surfaces generalize classical spheres and include unbounded and disconnected surfaces. We show that under mild assumptions as $n\to\infty$, any weighted sum of the random coordinates is asymptotically Gaussian, provided that no weight dominates. An explicit reduction in the variance compared to the unconstrained case is observed. We also study a model with penalization of deviations from the constraint, interpolating between the unconstrained and the constrained case. Our approach involves an explicit representation of the characteristic function of the constrained random variables in terms of independent random variables.

title: An improved minimum degree threshold for fractional clique decompositions in partite graphs
abstract: We prove a Dirac-type condition for an $r$-partite graph to admit a fractional clique decomposition: every sufficiently large $r$-partite graph with $n$ vertices in each part and partite minimum degree at least $(1 - \frac{1}{30r^2}) n$ admits a fractional $K_r$-decomposition, subject to necessary divisibility conditions. This implies the same upper bound on the asymptotic minimum degree threshold for $r$-partite graphs to admit a $K_r$-decomposition, using a well-known reduction.

title: Spheres with transitive families of CMC hypersurfaces
abstract: The goal of this paper is to investigate the following question: what geometric restrictions does the existence of a transitive family of constant mean curvature hyperspheres impose on a Riemannian metric on $\mathbb S^n$? The notion of a transitive family can be made precise through the theory of Zoll families developed by Ambrozio, Marques, and Neves. Within this framework, we partially extend their local rigidity theorem for even conformal factors on $\mathbb S^3$ to every dimension $n\ge4$, assuming each hypersphere in the minimal Zoll family has the area of a round equator. Moreover, we give a partial answer to the following higher-dimensional version of a question posed by Robert Bryant: must a metric on $\mathbb S^n$, conformal to the round metric and admitting a Zoll family of hyperspheres with a common nonzero constant mean curvature, have constant sectional curvature? Finally, we also investigate inverse problems in the spirit of Hangan, asking which metrics make a fixed family of geodesic spheres have a common prescribed mean curvature.

title: Pointless K3 surfaces over finite fields
abstract: We prove that K3 surfaces with no rational points over the finite field with $q$ elements exist if and only if $q \leq 11$. Our approach applies linear programming techniques to improve on generic sphere packing bounds for the discriminants of even rootless definite lattices. These bounds are applied to constrain the possible zeta functions of K3 surfaces with no rational points via the Artin--Tate formula. The remaining cases are ruled out by direct analysis of primitive embeddings of particular lattices into Niemeier lattices.

title: Global solutions for continuous-time Burgers equations and infinite-volume polymer measures
abstract: We study the stochastic Burgers equation on the whole space, driven by space-homogeneous Gaussian noises that are white in time and colored in space, for both positive and zero viscosity. We show that in dimension one, for any fixed average velocity, there is a unique ergodic global solution to the Burgers equation for all nonnegative viscosities, and that the One Force---One Solution principle holds. We also describe the basin of attraction and show that these global solutions are one-point pullback attractors. Moreover, the viscous global solution converges to the inviscid global solution as the viscosity tends to zero. Our technique relies on the study of polymer measures; accordingly, we establish the existence and uniqueness of infinite-volume polymer measures in a given asymptotic direction, as well as their convergence to semi-infinite minimizers in the zero-temperature limit. We also establish the existence part of all these results in arbitrary dimension larger than one.

title: From elementary processes to chaos: a discrete-time two-stage contagion model and its continuous limit
abstract: Two-stage contagion, in which adoption requires two successive contacts with adopters, combined with population turnover produces bistability and relaxation oscillations in Katriel's differential-equation model, but no chaos. We derive from the elementary reactions of the process, without reference to the differential equations, a discrete-time model in which the population is updated in rounds of length $τ$, as in elections, meetings or turns of a game: each individual makes at most one transition per round, events compete as exponential risks, and adoptions take effect from the next round. The model is a Markov chain whose large-population limit is a map $F_τ$; Katriel's equations are recovered as $τ\to0$. Taking the probability $p$ of adoption after a single contact as bifurcation parameter, with rates and round length fixed, $F_τ$ goes from extinction through a window of chaos to a stable equilibrium; for $β/γ=46$, $μ/γ=0.002$, $γτ=5.5$ the window is $0.023\le p\le0.056$, bounded by the invasion threshold and by a boundary crisis beyond a subcritical Neimark--Sacker point. One-stage contagion ($p=1$), $p=0$ and permanent adoption showed no chaos. The chaotic attractor is essentially unique, with one positive Lyapunov exponent and an outbreak--recharge geometry. In the same window Katriel's equations have a periodic relaxation cycle with troughs of $10^{-44}$--$10^{-164}$: the round structure does not create the oscillation but turns it into chaos and shrinks the oscillatory range in $p$ from $(0.022,0.41)$ to $(0.022,0.056)$. The chaos is therefore not an artefact of discretising a stable state, but a property of two-stage contagion with synchronous updating.

title: Hyperpolarity of polar foliations of codimension two
abstract: We consider polar foliations of codimension two on compact simply connected irreducible symmetric spaces. In rank at least two, we prove that these foliations are hyperpolar, settling the remaining case of the hyperpolarity problem discussed by Lytchak. We show that, for irreducible spherical Coxeter quotients, the horizontal universal cover fails to be a spherical building precisely on the Cayley plane, where every such foliation is congruent to one of the two known homogeneous models.

title: Gelfand numbers of Schatten class embeddings in the quasi-Banach range
abstract: We prove Conjecture 1.4 of Prochno and Strzelecki [J. Approx. Theory 277 (2022), 105736] on Gelfand numbers of embeddings between finite-dimensional Schatten classes. For $0<p\le1$ and indices bounded away from the ambient dimension by a fixed proportion, we obtain the conjectured lower bound, uniformly in the target exponent $2\le q\le\infty$. Together with the known upper estimate obtained by Hinrichs, Prochno and Vybíral [Math. Ann., 380(3-4):1563-1593, 2021], this gives the exact asymptotic order in the previously unresolved range. As a consequence, we obtain a complete all-index description by combining our result with the estimates of Hinrichs, Prochno and Vybíral and of Prochno and Strzelecki. The proof is deterministic and is based on Hilbert--Schmidt projections on rectangular matrix spaces.

title: $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$- and $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$-invariant multidifferential operators
abstract: We determine the dimension of the space of $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$-invariant (n)-ary differential operators on weighted densities for arbitrary weights, including the singular cases in which the usual elimination procedure breaks down. The proof relies on the strong Lefschetz property established by Stanley \cite{s} and Watanabe \cite{w}. We also investigate the corresponding problem in the super case.

title: Space of Geometric Gibbs Measures: Uniqueness, Ergodicity, and Teichmüller Complex Manifold Structure
abstract: Building on our previous work, in which geometric Gibbs measures were introduced to complete the space of classical Gibbs measures under the Teichmüller metric, we establish the uniqueness of geometric Gibbs measures in this paper. This result completes the construction of a Teichmüller complex manifold structure on the space of all geometric Gibbs measures. Using the welding technique, we uncover a connection between geometric Gibbs measures and harmonic measures on dynamical quasicircles. This connection allows us to establish asymptotic conformal rigidity for these dynamical quasicircles. Finally, we establish a foundation for the systematic study of the ergodic properties of geometric Gibbs measures.

title: Modelling and analysis of a cocktail phage therapy with coinfection
abstract: We analyze a delay differential model for phage therapy in which a cocktail of $n$ different types of bacteriophages, each with its own latency period, is administered and coinfection is allowed. We prove the global existence, uniqueness and nonnegativity of solutions, and the existence of an invariant region, under suitable conditions, in which the bacteria are eradicated exponentially fast. We determine the stability of the bacteria-free equilibrium in terms of the administered doses and give sufficient conditions for the nonexistence of coexistence equilibria, showing that coinfection may allow bacteria and phages to coexist even when the doses are large. For a cocktail of two phage types with the same latency period, we obtain a complete description of the biologically feasible coexistence equilibria, which may be zero, one or two. Numerical simulations illustrate the theoretical results.

title: The singular Gaussian scaling limit for a tagged particle in the infinite-dimensional Dyson model at $β=2$
abstract: We prove a logarithmic central limit theorem for a tagged particle in infinite-dimensional Dyson Brownian motion at inverse temperature $β=2$, starting from the sine$_2$ point process. The fluctuation is of order $\sqrt{\log t}$, which is subdiffusive and substantially slower than the polynomial fluctuations of classical short-range interacting particle systems, reflecting the rigidity induced by long-range logarithmic repulsion. We further identify the scaling limit as the singular Gaussian field corresponding to the zero-Hurst parameter, which provides a realisation of the singular Gaussian field as a scaling limit of a tagged particle raised by Dürr, Goldstein and Lebowitz (Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 38 (1985)).

title: Twisted Yangians of quasi-split type DI and Drinfeld type current relations
abstract: We study the twisted Yangian associated with the quasi-split symmetric pair $(\mathfrak{o}_{2n}, \mathfrak{o}_{n-1}\oplus \mathfrak{o}_{n+1})$ of type DI. Working in the transposed $R$-matrix presentation of arXiv:2607.14692, we show that the generating matrix $S(u)$ admits no Gaussian decomposition. We decompose instead the matrix $\widehat{S}(u) = G\,S(u)$, where $G$ is the constant term of $S(u)$. A chain of quasi-determinantal embeddings lowers the rank within this family of pairs and ends at $(\mathfrak{o}_4,\mathfrak{o}_3)$. Together with a direct study of a degenerate block of type AI, this gives a presentation of the special twisted Yangian $SY^{\mathrm{tw}}(\mathfrak{o}_{2n},\mathfrak{o}_{n-1}\oplus \mathfrak{o}_{n+1})$ by Drinfeld type current relations. The two fork nodes of the Dynkin diagram carry Drinfeld's presentation of $Y(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$. All other relations are those of split type DI, except that the Serre relation with a doubled fork node has zero right hand side. For $n\ge3$ we obtain an explicit isomorphism between the $R$-matrix presentation of Guay and Regelskis and the Drinfeld presentation of Lu and Zhang. The Drinfeld generators are expressed through the Gaussian series of $\widehat{S}(u)$. With quasi-split type AIII (Lu and Zhang), this completes the explicit comparison for the classical quasi-split types with a nontrivial diagram involution.

title: GNS-like representations of a quasi *-algebra in Krein spaces
abstract: In this paper unbounded representations of quasi *-algebras on an indefinite inner product space are introduced and studied. After introducing the partial *-algebra of unbounded closable operators sharing a common dense domain in a Krein space, the appropriate notion of *-representation in this setting is developed, and a GNS-type construction for quasi *-algebras based on $α$-positive sesquilinear forms is established. Furthermore, the notion of abstract conditional expectation is generalized to quasi *-algebras and how \emph{admissible} abstract conditional expectations $P$ give rise to representable $P$-forms is shown. The relation between $α$-positive forms and $P$-forms is also clarified. Several examples are provided.

title: Oriented V-systems
abstract: We introduce the notion of an oriented $\vee$-system which gives a class of solutions of the oriented associativity equations generalising Veselov's $\vee$-system solutions of WDVV equations. An oriented $\vee$-system is a special configuration of pairs of a vector and a covector in a linear space. We show that the class of oriented $\vee$-systems is closed under taking subsystems and restrictions. We provide examples which include a multiparameter family related to imprimitive complex reflection groups.

title: An order-reversing embedding of Turing degrees into Arthur-Nimue-Merlin degrees (short version)
abstract:
The Arthur-Nimue-Merlin degrees are a generalization of the Turing degrees introduced by Kihara as a tangible description of the partially ordered set of Lawvere-Tierney topologies on the effective topos (equivalently, subtoposes of the effective topos). They are defined in terms of a three-player game that introduces both angelic and demonic non-determinism into oracle queries. We construct an order embedding of the Turing degrees with their order reversed into the Arthur-Nimue-Merlin degrees, whose image we call the "co-Turing degrees"; we then study the order relationship of these co-Turing degrees with the (naturally embedded) Turing degrees within the Arthur-Nimue-Merlin degrees.
  This is a short version of arXiv:2603.19946, focused on the main results.

title: New results on cyclic and ordered Ramsey numbers
abstract: Inspired by the work of Poljak, Bašić, Damnjanović, Stevanović, and Stošić used the Kissat SAT solver in a recent paper to systematically determine the small cyclic and ordered Ramsey numbers of several families of graphs. By studying the patterns in their data, Bašić et al. formulated 15 conjectures on cyclic and ordered Ramsey numbers. In this paper, we confirm 9 of their conjectures, trace confirmations of 2 more to existing literature, and, perhaps surprisingly, disprove another one.

title: Dynamics Aware Past-Future Information Bottleneck
abstract: The simplification of complex dynamical systems is essential for efficient estimation and control. A principled approach to this task is through the lens of information-theoretic compression. The Past-Future Information Bottleneck (PF-IB) provides a theoretical framework for compressing linear dynamical systems. However, the standard formulation often lacks structural consistency, yielding representations that are not realizable as dynamical systems. By constraining the objective to a specific manifold of block Hankel matrices, which we prove is a Lie group, we bridge the gap between PF-IB and realization theory. Our approach ensures that the resulting compressed dynamics are realizable, thereby enabling its direct application to estimation and control. We demonstrate our approach in numerical simulations.

title: A half-line of Schur idempotent norms
abstract: Using a family of bipartite graphs constructed by hanging identical rooted trees at every vertex of a highly symmetric graph, we show that every sufficiently large real number is the norm of an idempotent Schur multiplier on the bounded operators on $\ell^2$. This answers a question previously raised by the author.

title: Butler's conjecture for K3 curves
abstract:
Butler's conjectures predict that, on a general smooth curve $C$ of genus $g\ge3$, a general coherent system $[\mathcal{O}_C\otimes V\xrightarrow{\varphi}E]$ with semistable underlying bundle $E$ and $\dim V>\operatorname{rk}(E)$ has surjective evaluation map $\varphi$ and stable kernel.
  In this paper, we prove Butler's conjectures for $g\ge8$ in the two cases in which the Brill-Noether geometry of a general curve is known, namely rank one and the range $μ(E)>2g-2$. By deformation and openness, it suffices to establish the result on a single Brill-Noether-Petri general curve. We do so for curves on K3 surfaces of Picard rank one, using the wall-crossing theory of coherent systems developed by the first two authors.

title: Almost sure bounds and tail phases for critical non-Gaussian holomorphic chaos
abstract: Gu and Zhang asked for almost sure upper and lower bounds on the Taylor coefficients $a_n$ of $\exp(\sum_{k\ge1}X_kz^k/\sqrt{k})$ in the unit disc, and for the dependence of these bounds on the input tail. For independent, identically distributed, rotationally invariant complex inputs with $\mathbb E|X_1|^2=1$, we prove the universal almost sure bound $|a_n|=O((\log n)^{1/4})$. Almost surely, $\limsup_{n\to\infty}|a_n|/(\log n)^{1/4}$ is positive and finite exactly when $\mathbb E[|X_1|^2\log^+|X_1|^2]<\infty$, and is zero otherwise. For each input law, we define a deterministic scale such that, almost surely, the coefficients are bounded exactly when the scale is bounded, and tend to zero exactly when it vanishes. We also determine the almost sure logarithmic growth exponent as the maximum of contributions from collective fluctuations and individual large inputs. Explicit tails exhibit distinct thresholds for boundedness and for upper bounds at the scale in the phase criteria. Examples show that neither the leading tail nor the set of finite logarithmic moments determines the almost sure phase.

title: Tusnády's problem and online two-sample thinning
abstract:
We determine the sharp order of discrepancy in Tusnády's problem in every fixed dimension $d\ge 2$. The largest combinatorial discrepancy of $N$ points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with respect to axis-parallel boxes is $Θ_d((\log N)^{d-1/2})$, extending Wei's planar result and matching Nikolov's upper bound. More strongly, with high probability, this lower bound holds simultaneously for every subset obtained by deleting at most a sufficiently small fixed fraction of a uniform $N$-point sample.
  We apply this geometric estimate to online thinning of two independent samples of size $n$ from an unknown common distribution, where observations must be kept or discarded upon arrival. For every fixed dimension $k\ge 1$ and expected deletion budget $ρn$, with $0<ρ<2$, we prove that the minimax expected prefix discrepancy over lower orthants is $Θ_{k,ρ}((\log n)^{k+1/2})$. In dimension one, the optimal terminal discrepancy is instead $Θ_ρ((\log\log n)^{3/2})$, giving a sharp separation between the prefix and terminal objectives. For $k\ge 2$, we obtain terminal bounds differing by a factor of $\log n$.
  The lower bounds are based on Gaussian small-ball estimates for box-incidence matrices, while the upper bounds use stationary Metropolis thinning and, in one dimension, a terminal cancellation procedure.

title: Improved Index and Intersection bounds for Min-Max Geodesics
abstract: In this note, we show that the sum of the Morse index and number of intersections of min-max geodesics achieving the p-widths of a closed surface are bounded above by $p$, improving a result from our previous work. A key idea is that deformations coming from vertex desingularization and eigenfunctions of the Jacobi operator on geodesics are sufficiently independent.

title: Augmented Lagrangian methods with telescopic subproblems for MPCCs and cardinality constraints with general constraints: constraint-preserving swaps and B-stationarity
abstract: We consider optimization problems with general equality and inequality constraints and partitioned cardinality constraints, which include complementarity constraints. In the augmented Lagrangian method that we consider, the bounds and the cardinality constraints are kept in the subproblems, which are solved by the Telescopic Method. The limit points of this method are B-stationary, without constraint qualifications, if the penalty parameters remain bounded, but not in general. The reason is that the swaps of the Telescopic Method pass through points at which the constraints have different values, and the corresponding variation of the penalty term grows with the penalty parameter. With unbounded penalty parameters and a derivative test outside the current face, the feasible limit points at which a linear independence constraint qualification holds are M-stationary for MPCCs. We modify the swaps, by means of a scaled Newton restoration, so that they preserve the values of the constraints, and we prove that every feasible limit point at which this constraint qualification holds is then B-stationary (S-stationary for MPCCs), whatever the behavior of the penalty parameters. Counterexamples show that the modification is necessary, even with exact solutions of the subproblems, and that the constraint qualification cannot be weakened to one of Mangasarian-Fromovitz type. In the MacMPEC collection, the method found certified S- or B-stationary points in 185 of the 193 instances, more than Algencan and the regularization method of Scholtes. In experiments with cardinality-constrained portfolios and sparse principal component analysis, the constraint-preserving swaps improved the original swaps and the methods applied to complementarity reformulations.

title: On supersoluble like groups of automorphisms of compact Riemann surfaces
abstract: Let $G$ be a not necessary full automorphism group of a compact Riemann surface of genus $g$. We found sharp bounds for $|G|$ in the terms of $g$ when $G$ belongs to one of the following classes of finite groups sharing similar properties with supersoluble groups: 2-nilpotent, with the Sylow tower of supersoluble type, with $\mathbb{P}$-subnormal cyclic primary subgroups, widely supersoluble, with submodular Sylow subgroups, with submodular cyclic primary subgroups and strongly supersoluble.

title: Steinberg module and top-dimensional cohomology for arithmetic Chevalley groups
abstract: We prove that for a Chevalley--Demazure group scheme $\mathcal{G}$ of type $G_2$, $F_4$ or $E_8$ and a Euclidean ring $\mathcal{O}$ with field of fractions $K$, the Steinberg module of $\mathcal{G}(K)$ is generated by integral apartment classes. As a consequence, the top-dimensional rational cohomology of $\mathcal{G}(\mathcal{O})$ vanishes if $\mathcal{O}$ is a ring of integers, extending results of Tóth and of Brück--Santos Rego--Sroka.

title: A Theoretical Analysis of a Bilevel Optimization Formulation for Combined Local-Global Optical Flow Models
abstract: This paper analyzes a bilevel formulation for learning the regularization parameter of combined local-global (CLG) optical flow models. The lower-level problem computes the flow from a Lucas--Kanade data term and a quadratic or total variation (TV) regularizer, and the upper-level problem selects the parameter that minimizes the squared distance to a ground-truth flow. The setting is finite-dimensional, and a full-rank assumption makes the lower-level solution unique. For the quadratic model we derive sufficient conditions for the existence of an optimal parameter, for every optimal parameter to be positive, and for strict local optimality. For TV regularization an optimal parameter always exists, because the lower-level solution vanishes for large parameters, and we give a sufficient condition for positivity that accounts for the coupling of the two flow components through the local structure tensors. Synthetic examples illustrate the conditions, including cases in which they fail.

title: Simple Modules over Leavitt Path Algebras Generated by Indicator Functions on Paths
abstract: Let E be an arbitrary graph, K a field, and D the set of boundary paths of E consisting of both infinite paths and finite paths ending at singular vertices. The space KD of K-valued functions on D is a right module over the Leavitt path algebra LK(E). For a non- empty set S ? D that is strongly connected and closed under adding and deleting initial segments, we study the submodule N_S = 1_S.LK(E) generated by the indicator function of S. Let S_0 be the set of vertices lying on the paths in S. We show that N_S is simple if and only if S contains no breaking vertex of the hereditary saturated set H = E0 nS0. In particular, when S contains only infinite paths or when E is a row- finite graph, NS is a simple module. Up to isomorphism, the simple module NS depends only on S_0. When S is an infinite set of paths, the simple module NS is neither graded nor projective. The left module LK(E)1_S, obtained by twisting the action through the involution of LK(E), is simple exactly when NS is, and, when S is infinite, it is not isomorphic to any of the Chen simple modules. title: On the elliptic regularization of maximal slope curves
abstract: We consider the so-called Weighted Energy-Dissipation approximation of gradient flows in metric spaces. We prove the convergence of minimizers to maximal slope curves under assumptions that are close to those of the original existence theory for metric gradient flows. The proof relies on an energy-dissipation identity for the approximating curves and on an adaptation of a general stability result for maximal slope curves.
